Not affiliated with Cloudflare. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); the model list and details are built in, so nothing is fetched to show them; chat requests go to the URL in CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_BASE_URL through Hermes' own client with CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN, both read by Hermes per profile; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

plugins.name: coder
plugins.description: Run Hermes terminal commands in an existing remote Coder workspace. Disclosure — runs terminal commands inside your Coder workspace at CODER_URL using CODER_API_KEY; starts a stopped workspace automatically; forwards only the env vars you list in TERMINAL_CODER_FORWARD_ENV.

plugins.name: codex-account-switch
plugins.description: Windows desktop plugin that switches which Codex login and which Claude subscription account every local Hermes profile uses, with one idle-only, verified restart of the gateway (and, on Hermes before 0.22, of Hermes Desktop). Refuses while any profile is busy, restores the previous selection if a step fails, and writes a receipt that says whether the switch took effect. Disclosure — Windows only. A switch rewrites, through Hermes's own commands, the Codex credential order in every profile's auth.json and the CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR line in every profile's .env, so every profile that has the plugin enabled spends the same selected Codex login and the same Claude login (one Hermes-owned claude-auth folder; no token is copied between profiles). It reads Codex tokens from each profile's auth.json. On Hermes 0.22 and later it stops and restarts the gateway once Hermes's own idle proof and the gateway's drain report idle, and Hermes Desktop stays open and reconnects; on earlier Hermes it also reads the Desktop backends' dashboard session token from their process environment and closes and reopens Hermes Desktop (work started in the seconds after the idle check is cut off). It sends the target Codex token to OpenAI's usage endpoint and Claude login tokens to Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint (also when the setup screen opens); if the target Claude login has expired it first runs the claude CLI once so the CLI renews its own token, which rotates that login's refresh token. No telemetry and no automatic account rotation.

plugins.name: codex-chat-look
plugins.description: Independent Catppuccin Latte/Mocha desktop theme with peach accents, SDK-native gateway/profile switching and host-owned session density. Legacy plugin identity: codex-chat-look. No self-updater or native layout overrides. Disclosure — Desktop theme derived from FPSUnleashed's MIT-licensed desktop skin; switches gateway/profile via host.ensureAgent only on user selection and a palette command rewrites the native sessionListDensity setting; no network calls of its own.

plugins.name: codex-truly
plugins.description: Gives ChatGPT/Codex-subscription models the context window the backend actually accepts instead of the one its catalog advertises. Measured live on 2026-10-14: gpt-6.1-sol advertises 500K, caps at 872K and accepts 919,956 input tokens, while the -900k opt-in variant had silently stopped working because Hermes only raises a legacy 272K advertisement. The plugin reads the live catalog, writes one scoped model_overrides.<provider>.<model_id>.context_window entry per model (a documented step of context resolution, so no core patch), and ships a probe that bisects the API for the true ceiling because the refusal is a late SSE event, not an HTTP error. It also selects core's Codex-backed image provider so image_generate runs on the subscription with no OPENAI_API_KEY. Disclosure - uses the profile's Codex sign-in through Hermes's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: [openai-codex]); the plugin never reads auth.json and never holds a token, and network calls go only to chatgpt.com. Its only writes are scoped model_overrides entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset), through Hermes's atomic config writers; revert removes exactly what it wrote. No telemetry, no background processes, no shell commands, no self-updater. probe spends subscription quota (refused requests are free, accepted ones bill) and is never run automatically. Disclosure — uses the profile's Codex sign-in only through Hermes's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: openai-codex) and calls chatgpt.com only; its CLI and the model-callable codex_truly tool write scoped model_overrides context_window entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset) to config.yaml with no approval prompt, and `probe` sends large padding requests that spend subscription quota.

plugins.name: cognee
plugins.description: Knowledge-graph memory for Hermes — recall, remember, forget, and code search, backed by a local cognee server or Cognee Cloud. Disclosure — default local mode starts a detached cognee server (uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8011) plus a session-close watcher per session; turns, memory writes and indexed source go to that server and on to your configured LLM provider (OpenAI by default) or to Cognee Cloud / COGNEE_BASE_URL in remote mode; the store lives in ~/.cognee (outside HERMES_HOME, shared across profiles); cognee sends anonymous usage telemetry unless TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1.

plugins.name: cognition
plugins.description: Cognition session-end memory — facts regex-extracted from your messages at session end, stored in a local SQLite queue and JSON log under one repo label, with fetch-first merge, per-entry provenance, and budgeted prefetch (tools: cognition_search, cognition_status, read-only cognition_dream). Disclosure — saves verbatim excerpts (up to 400 chars) of your own messages that match preference/decision phrases in plain local files under HERMES_HOME/cognition/ (SQLite queue, JSON commit log) and re-injects them into later prompts sent to your model provider; the author name is read from ~/.gitconfig; the plugin makes no network calls of its own.

plugins.name: colorado-traffic
plugins.description: Live Colorado highway events from CDOT COtrip. No API key. Default corridor is I-70 Golden to east Denver. Separates incidents happening now from scheduled work and unverified Waze reports.

plugins.name: command-ledger
plugins.description: Local ledger of the slash commands you run in Hermes (built-in commands in the CLI, built-in and plugin commands on messaging platforms): /command-log shows how often each command was used, its share, in how many sessions and when last, per command, platform, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /command-log recent lists the newest commands (ten, or up to 100 with /command-log recent 50) with the alias typed. Disclosure — writes command metadata (command name, alias typed, surface, platform, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no arguments, session key or user id) to plugin-data/command-ledger/commands.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot block or change a command; no network

plugins.name: command-tray
plugins.description: Session command tray — shell commands the Hermes agent ran via the terminal tool (success and failure). Desktop pane and /commands. No API keys. Disclosure — records terminal commands with exit code, workdir and a 160-char redacted output preview to $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/command-tray/state.json; the Desktop pane inserts text through Hermes Desktop's internal hermes:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API) with clipboard fallback; no network.

plugins.name: commandcode-oauth
plugins.description: Command Code CLI-key model provider with a live OAuth catalog property bridge, plan limits and failover classification. Disclosure — uses the CLI-internal api.commandcode.ai/alpha/generate endpoint and CLI client headers, sends the full conversation, tool schemas, cwd path and OS/Python version, and imports a static key from the read-only CLI credential file or a browser hand-off; no OAuth exchange takes place. Hermes also bundles commandcode for the documented Provider API.

plugins.name: comment-scraper
plugins.description: Ask about the Reddit and Hacker News threads you exported with the Comment Scraper browser extension: list, read, search and quote them by comment number. Disclosure — starts a local stdio MCP server with npx -y comment-scraper-mcp@0.1.0, which npx downloads from npm on first run; the server only reads JSON exports in ~/Downloads and the folders directly inside it, never writes files, makes no network requests, stores no credentials and sends no telemetry.

plugins.name: compartment
plugins.description: Encrypted, fully offline memory provider. AEAD-encrypted local vault (vectors included), bundled embedding model, exact hybrid search, no API key and no network at runtime. One vault shared with Claude, Cursor and any other MCP client on the machine. Disclosure — installs the full compartment engine (about 27 Python packages including onnxruntime, tokenizers, mcp and system-tray dependencies) into the Hermes venv; the provider's system prompt instructs the model to store passwords and API keys in the encrypted vault.

plugins.name: completion-sound
plugins.description: Pick the sound Hermes Desktop plays when a turn finishes: one of the 14 built-in presets or your own audio file (mp3, wav, ogg), with an optional different sound during night hours. Files stay in the plugin's local storage. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

plugins.name: composer-modes
plugins.description: Cursor-style composer modes (ask / agent / plan / debug) for the Hermes desktop — the mode's operating note reaches the model inside the turn's model-facing bytes, never the bubble, transcript or session titles, and ask mode is enforced read-only on the tool side.

plugins.name: context-audit
plugins.description: Context-window forensics: per-turn input/output token estimates, the single largest tool output of each turn, oversized tool calls (args over 50 KB), and compaction events, recorded as metadata only (tool name, byte length, ids, timestamps — never args or results) in a local SQLite DB under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/context-audit/. Adds a /context-audit slash command that prints the top 5 context eaters over a window with one mitigation per entry.

plugins.name: corpus
plugins.description: Hosted Corpus MCP (Streamable HTTP at corpuslaw.us/api/mcp) plus two bundled skills: US law search/get_node/list_coverage over 571k+ provisions, and LLC/nonprofit formation intake (requirements, compare, NAICS lookup, handoff, USDC checkout, payment_status), with account.status for quota. Filing always stays human-gated and USDC pay is email-confirmed. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); no API key needed for anonymous research. The formation skill requires fixed vendor-authored marketing copy in the first reply and before payment, and sends founder PII (name, email, phone, address) to Corpus through links and MCP tools. Intake instructions are vendored; checkout requires exact-amount confirmation from the user in the current turn.

plugins.name: cortexlayer
plugins.description: CortexLayer memory provider — page-linked long-term memory with link-expansion retrieval, wired into Hermes' automatic per-turn recall (prefetch) and persistence (sync_turn), plus a pre-compress checkpoint so evidence Hermes' own context compaction would otherwise drop is saved first. Platform mode only: each turn's query and conversational content is sent to the hosted api.cortexlayer.net (HTTPS, API-key authenticated) for storage/retrieval — no local/offline mode. Requires a free CortexLayer account and API key.

plugins.name: covision
plugins.description: Read-only Covision meeting, assigned-task, and published-knowledge tools through the Covision Streamable HTTP MCP service, plus a workflow skill. Requires a Covision account, organization connector enablement, and browser OAuth consent; no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin.

plugins.name: crawl4ai
plugins.description: Crawl4ai self-hosted web content extraction. Requires CRAWL4AI_URL and CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN pointing at your instance.

plugins.name: crew
plugins.description: One /crew message becomes verified work on the kanban board. A coordinator owns every card until its proof command exits 0 - one writer per card, an independent verifier, a hard token budget per card, and a live local dashboard of every card, run and tool call. Disclosure — install.py creates four crew-* profiles cloned from your chat profile (including its .env provider keys and memories), deletes non-crew skills in them, updates crew in other profiles and on Linux starts a loopback dashboard service (127.0.0.1:8799, transcript excerpts; --publish serves it to one tailnet login), restarting it when an upgrade changes the plugin code; on native Windows the service and the optional nightly cron are skipped and the dashboard is started by hand, and proofs run in Git for Windows's bash; a Crew tab in the Hermes dashboard and a Crew page in Hermes Desktop build that board inside the Hermes backend, including its transcript excerpts, each live card's step count and last tool name, and its acknowledge action, under /api/plugins/crew/ to anyone with dashboard access; a detached coordinator makes read-only model decisions and runs card proof commands unattended with a scrubbed env, flagged or changed proofs only after the owner answers /crew-proof; card reports and questions are sent to the originating chat via hermes send; agent-written per-role lessons are injected into later crew turns.

plugins.name: cron-bulletin
plugins.description: Central Hermes Desktop inbox for reports produced by local cron runs.

plugins.name: crypto-prices
plugins.description: Live crypto price ticker for the desktop status bar — Top 10 by market cap, seamless marquee, custom coins & 60+ display currencies, adjustable width (CoinGecko, no API key).

plugins.name: cursor-provider
plugins.description: Cursor model provider using the official proprietary Cursor SDK. Disclosure — uses Cursor's proprietary cursor-sdk (PyPI, bundled binary bridge on loopback) with the user's CURSOR_API_KEY; sends the full conversation, tool schemas/results and images (HTTPS URLs or base64) to Cursor; keeps private per-session SDK workspaces under HERMES_HOME/cache/cursor-sdk; Cursor built-in tools and MCP are requested off and Hermes keeps tool execution and approvals.

plugins.name: cursor-sdk
plugins.description: Experimental model transport using the official Cursor Agent SDK. Requests go to Cursor through its official SDK. The plugin cannot enforce an included-only spending cap and never changes account spending settings. Instructions use a Cursor project rule, not a native system-role override. Permission and prompt-hierarchy equivalence remain unqualified. The plugin spawns Node and a local SDK agent, runs Git initialization in a plugin-owned workspace, and writes project rules, hooks, and SDK state under its own runtime directory. That state may contain private conversation data and currently remains on disk. Credentials come from Hermes's profile-scoped secret accessor. No credential store or vendor token file is read directly by plugin code. Text-only, buffered responses. The bundled model snapshot is not live entitlement discovery. Optional picker hooks require Hermes support. This plugin does not patch the desktop. Disclosure — spawns Node and a local Cursor Agent SDK worker per request (`npm ci` in the plugin dir installs Cursor's official native platform binaries from npm); sends the full conversation, system prompt and tool schemas to Cursor with your CURSOR_API_KEY; Cursor-native shell/file tools are denied by a fail-closed project hook and the run is cancelled if one fires, but that enforcement is not proven in every Cursor runtime; each request's workspace and conversation state stay under the plugin's runtime/ directory until you delete them.

plugins.name: custodian
plugins.description: Autonomous operations monitor for a Hermes install: scans gateway logs, cron jobs, skill journals and agent data directories, classifies findings against a 27-fingerprint registry, auto-repairs Tier 1 problems, escalates the rest, and keeps an append-only issue ledger. Ships /custodian (status, scan, issues, repair, verify, schedule, confidence, init, escalation-runner), four scan/health tools and a grid dashboard. Disclosure — reads gateway logs, cron job state and per-skill journal files under HERMES_HOME to build its findings, and writes repair actions and an issues ledger back there; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — /custodian init registers 3 recurring agent cron jobs (deep scan 4×/day, cron-health 4×/day, escalation runner every 30 min on weekdays).

plugins.name: custom-dangerous-patterns
plugins.description: Add custom dangerous command patterns to Hermes's built-in approval system. Users define regex patterns in YAML; a pre_tool_call hook sends block patterns to Hermes's human approval gate and blocks deny patterns immediately. Modifies no Hermes internals.

plugins.name: darkmoon
plugins.description: Triage the findings file of a Darkmoon autonomous pentest scan (JSON or SARIF): filter by severity and proof status, get a severity-sorted summary and a pass/fail gate for a release. Read-only and offline: no network, no subprocess, no credentials, standard library only. Darkmoon is open source (GPL-3.0); its web dashboard and remediation agent are Pro and are not used here. Disclosure — reads a local .json or .sarif file at a model-supplied path (10 MB cap) and returns its findings; no network, subprocess or writes

plugins.name: dashboard-auth-feishu
plugins.description: Feishu / Lark OAuth sign-in for the web dashboard, admitted by tenant + open_id allow-list. Registers the `feishu` dashboard auth provider once plugins.entries.dashboard-auth-feishu.settings (app_id, tenant_key, owner_open_ids) and an app secret are configured. Disclosure — calls only the fixed Feishu or Lark authorize, token and user_info endpoints; reads HERMES_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_APP_SECRET or, as a fallback, the Feishu gateway's FEISHU_APP_SECRET, plus HERMES_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_SESSION_KEY; stores tenant, open_id and display name per sign-in in a 0600 SQLite file under plugin-data (no upstream tokens); a refused sign-in logs the tenant_key and open_id Feishu returned (identifiers only, for first-time setup); every admitted identity gets full dashboard access; upstream PKCE is not used (confidential client with single-use cookie-bound state); pending logins are in memory, so one dashboard worker only; WebSockets opened before logout may stay open until the session key is rotated and the dashboard restarted.

plugins.name: dashboard-auth-ldap
plugins.description: LDAP / Active Directory password login for the web dashboard. Verifies credentials with an LDAP bind (direct or search-then-bind), never stores passwords, requires ldaps:// or StartTLS, and supports group restriction. Registers the `ldap` dashboard auth provider once dashboard.ldap_auth is configured. Disclosure — dashboard logins are verified by binding to your configured LDAP/AD server with the user's password (TLS with certificate validation required unless allow_insecure is set); sessions are stateless HMAC tokens (12h access / 30d refresh by default) signed with HERMES_DASHBOARD_LDAP_SECRET or a random per-process key, and logout cannot revoke them; group removal and disabled accounts are not re-checked until the refresh token expires; failed logins count toward the directory's account-lockout policy.

plugins.name: dashboard-button
plugins.description: One-click access to the Hermes Web Dashboard (127.0.0.1:9119) from the Desktop app — sidebar row, in-app page that loads itself when the server comes up, and a status-bar chip with a live dot. Front-end only: no agent calls, no tokens, no API keys.

plugins.name: dashscope-image
plugins.description: DashScope (Qwen Cloud) image generation -- Wan 2.7 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) and PAYG (sk-ws-*) keys.

plugins.name: dashscope-video
plugins.description: DashScope (Qwen Cloud) video generation -- HappyHorse 1.1 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Async task API. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) keys.

plugins.name: davinci-resolve
plugins.description: Control DaVinci Resolve Studio live, or generate importable interchange files for free DaVinci Resolve.

plugins.name: deadbolt
plugins.description: Review and approve exact text-artifact writes through a local DeadBolt sidecar. Protects this plugin's commit tool only.

plugins.name: debug-desk
plugins.description: Today's git digest in the current repo, plus the last failed terminal command the Hermes agent ran. Desktop pane, status chip, optional local LLM summary. Does not watch OS or editor terminals.

plugins.name: deepgram-voice
plugins.description: Deepgram Aura text-to-speech and Nova speech-to-text providers for Hermes Agent.

plugins.name: deepinfra-sandbox
plugins.description: Terminal backend running agent commands in isolated DeepInfra cloud sandboxes (deep_sands microVMs). Disclosure — runs agent commands in billable DeepInfra cloud sandboxes and uploads your Hermes skills, cache and skill-registered credential files to the sandbox at /workspace/.hermes; dangerous-command approval is skipped inside the sandbox.

plugins.name: deepseek-search-fetch
plugins.description: DeepSeek Search & Fetch as a backend for the built-in web_search and web_extract. Disclosure — sends web_search queries and web_extract URLs to api.deepseek.com with your DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and DeepSeek fetches the pages server-side; billed to your DeepSeek balance per successful request; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access.

plugins.name: deepseek-whale
plugins.description: Live DeepSeek API peak/off-peak pricing whale for the Hermes desktop titlebar. Blue x0.5 off-peak, grey PEAK at full price, countdown on click, 30s repaint, no backend or API key.

plugins.name: deferred-questions
plugins.description: Durable non-blocking questions with exact answer binding and gateway continuation. Disclosure — its pre_gateway_dispatch hook sees every gateway message and consumes only `dq <id> …` answers from the stored recipient; with `enable_tool` on, the model can send questions to any chat the gateway already authorizes, and a question marked continue_agent resumes that chat's agent with the user's answer; questions and answers are stored unencrypted in $HERMES_HOME/deferred-questions/questions.sqlite3; it calls private gateway and adapter methods, so a Hermes update can break delivery until it is re-pinned.

plugins.name: deja-memory
plugins.description: Memory from the coding sessions already on this machine — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes and the other agents deja reads, including history from before it was installed. No model, no API key, no server. Disclosure — runs the separately installed, unpinned deja binary (brew install deja-vu) as a subprocess; deja reads Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes and other agents' local transcript files, keeps its index under ~/.cache/deja, and recalled text from those agents is injected into Hermes turns; nothing leaves the machine.

plugins.name: desensitize
plugins.description: Chinese-context desensitization for Hermes chats. Replaces PII and business-sensitive entities — person names, company names, addresses, file paths, and magnitude figures — with reversible placeholders before a message reaches the model, then restores them in the reply. Two layers: an optional local/OpenAI-compatible LLM for semantic entity judgment, plus a sub-millisecond regex fallback (phone, ID card, email, IP, path) that keeps the conversation working when the model is unavailable. Disclosure — the semantic layer sends the pre-redaction text to the configured LLM, because recognising a name requires seeing it: with the default provider=ollama that is the local Ollama host and nothing leaves the machine, but provider=openai without an explicit base_url falls back to https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1 (remote); set base_url, or stay on ollama, to keep it local. Also rewrites inbound user messages and outbound assistant replies, so transcript content differs from what you typed; placeholders are code-generated and may over-match (18-digit ID-card-shaped strings, names that collide with the public-entity allowlist); company names are matched greedily and a modifier such as 原北京某某有限公司 is absorbed into the placeholder; magnitude masking drops the numeric value and only fires on the configured trigger words, so a domain term absent from that list is left unmasked without warning; the placeholder mapping is held in memory only and never written to disk.

plugins.name: deskrpg
plugins.description: Hermes gateway integration for DeskRPG virtual offices, with profiles, kanban, cron, artifacts and NPC skill management. Install it through the DeskRPG setup wizard. Optional (off by default): when enabled by the operator, links the plugin into every profile so kanban workers and cron runs can save artifacts. Disclosure — NPC skill management runs hermes skills/curator commands as background subprocesses per profile and edits that profile's skills, config.yaml and memory files; creating new review-policy kanban cards needs a review-policy API that upstream Hermes does not ship (the README points at the author's hermes-agent fork for it), and that feature stays inert on upstream.

plugins.name: devin
plugins.description: Delegate coding tasks to the Devin CLI, on your computer or in Devin Cloud, with live progress cards and change review in Hermes Desktop. Every launch goes through Hermes approval; Cloud runs need a separate Cloud-managed-permissions confirmation. Disclosure — spawns the vendor devin CLI from PATH or cli_path (devin acp, devin acp --cloud, devin --print, devin auth status, devin models list); the CLI edits files and runs shell commands in a folder the model picks (any folder unless allowed_roots is set) under the configured permission mode (accept-edits/smart auto-allow edits, dangerous auto-allows everything and needs allow_dangerous: true), and talks to Cognition's servers; Devin Cloud runs use Cognition-managed permissions that Hermes does not gate. Every model-initiated launch goes through Hermes approval; follow-ups typed on a Desktop run card and answers to Devin's prompts on the card start or allow actions on that click without a Hermes prompt (unanswered card prompts are denied after 300 s by default). Uses the existing Devin CLI login and stores no credentials; Hermes provider, bot and tool secrets are stripped from the child environment (extra_env is passed as set). Background runs continue after the turn up to their timeout and post Devin's output back into the conversation as a message when they finish. Run history (prompts, diffs, command output) and model preferences are saved under plugin-data/devin unless persist_runs is off. Independent community add-on, not affiliated with Cognition.

plugins.name: devkit
plugins.description: One managed home for agent drafts: a per-session scratchpad of named buffers the agent edits in place instead of writing a new temp file per revision. Buffers live under plugin-data/devkit/, open in the Desktop code viewer, are promoted to real files only through write_file, and are removed when their chat is deleted. A Scratchpad tab beside Files groups chats by date like the chat sidebar; click a chat to open it, click a file to view or edit it in a workspace tab, and delete or clear drafts. Disclosure — adds a short placement rule (about 120 tokens) to each turn's user message; reads state.db read-only once an hour from a background thread to find deleted chats, and also removes folders idle longer than idle_days (default 90) using its own stamps; deletes only its own folders under plugin-data/devkit/; no network calls, credentials or third-party services.

plugins.name: dexio
plugins.description: Dexio shared-wiki memory. Before each turn, the pages of your Dexio wiki that match the user's message; tools to search, read and write the pages your other agents and team also use. Nothing is captured automatically: no transcripts or turn logs. Standard library only; no background threads or local services. Disclosure — with DEXIO_API_KEY set, the first 300 characters of each user message go to the Dexio server (default app.dexio.wiki, or DEXIO_URL) as a search query, tool arguments and the agent's profile name go there on tool calls, and the model is prompted to write, overwrite and edit pages in a wiki shared with the user's team and other agents, without a confirmation step.

plugins.name: diaktoros
plugins.description: Unattended GitHub pull-request review between two Hermes agents: one pushes fixes, a different one reviews, rounds are capped in verdicts, a watchdog reports silent stalls, and the loop never merges. Disclosure — runs unattended Hermes agent turns inside bubblewrap (terminal and file tools, no network, no credentials); a host-side broker and the CLI write to GitHub (reviews, comments, labels, issues, repo webhooks, and opt-in fixer pushes, which may push CI fixes, merge commits of the base into a PR's own branch to resolve conflicts, and issue-fix branches and PRs, including an opt-in auto-fix that hands issues its triage seat labels (never P0-P2, capped per day) to the fixer without a maintainer, plus an opt-in clean merge of the base into a review-only author's same-repository PR branch when it conflicts or falls behind, a branch the loop does not own; it never merges a PR) with repo-scope PAT files you provide; edits Hermes's webhook_subscriptions.json directly and its watchdog re-adds this loop's routes while armed; writes gate scripts into the seat profiles' scripts/ folders and creates one hermes cron job (its migrate command replaces the old hermes-review-loop job and copies that plugin's settings); its backup command writes a 0600 archive of the plugin's state, including webhook route secrets, to a path you choose, and restore writes one back into the Hermes home and recreates the cron job (restore only archives you made: a crafted one can place files anywhere under the Hermes home); downloads PR archives from codeload.github.com, failed CI job logs from GitHub's log storage (redirected, without the token) and Rust crates from crates.io on the host; an opt-in observer feed posts loop notices to the chat you name; deletes its own state and closed-PR review dirs in roots you configure; on OAuth seats its host proxy may force Hermes token refreshes that rewrite ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.qwen and profile auth.json credentials, and on Claude subscription logins it identifies as Claude Code (Claude Code user-agent, x-app and OAuth beta headers). Nothing runs until you arm a loop. Linux only.

plugins.name: diff-review
plugins.description: Analyze git diffs for common code quality issues — debug prints, hardcoded secrets, bare except clauses, and unresolved TODOs.

plugins.name: digital-marketing-pro
plugins.description: Open-source marketing toolkit for agencies and in-house teams, one listing with three skill groups and 207 skills registered as Hermes skills: Digital Marketing Pro (strategy, SEO/AEO/GEO, paid media, CRM, analytics; 164 skills), ContentForge (fact-checked long-form content with a run auditor; 22 skills) and SocialForge (a content calendar to images, carousels, video and copy; 21 skills). Skills only: no tools, hooks or background processes. Disclosure — Skills only (no tools, hooks or MCP servers). The optional scripts the skills run call third-party APIs (ad, CRM, e-mail, Slack, LLM and image/video providers) only when run, using the user's own keys from environment variables. Live writes need the user's typed yes. For writes the plugin sends itself, the script creates a single-use approval record when it prepares the write, and the agent approves that record after the yes, so Hermes does not prompt before those script runs. Writes through MCP tools rely on the typed yes alone. Paid image and video generation is quoted first. refresh_models.py reads your Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and (strategy group) Evolink keys. Keys and data live outside the Hermes profile: SocialForge stores API keys in plain text, plus a copy of any Google service-account file, in ~/socialforge-workspace; brand data goes to ~/.claude-marketing; deliverables are copied to ~/Documents/DigitalMarketingPro and ~/Documents/ContentForge. Nothing installs unless the user says yes; installs are exact-pinned pip packages into the Python that runs the script, plus Playwright's Chromium download. See the README and each group's PRIVACY.md.

plugins.name: discord-tps
plugins.description: Show live tokens-per-second and the active model on your Discord bot's presence. Disclosure — Replaces the Discord bot's public presence with the live tok/s figure and the model name of the most recent API call in this gateway (any platform or chat), visible to anyone who can see the bot; updates at most every interval seconds (minimum 10) over the gateway's existing Discord connection. Reads no credentials and makes no network calls of its own.

plugins.name: doc-markdown
plugins.description: Convert one local file to Markdown with doc_convert on Linux and macOS, built on Microsoft's MarkItDown. Microsoft and MarkItDown are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. Disclosure — the doc_markdown toolset is on by default on every surface, including a gateway, so anyone you allow there can call doc_convert; stop it with hermes tools. It does not fetch pages. Unattended sessions still convert when Hermes calls the tool. This plugin creates no cron job. A child process runs MarkItDown with no Hermes keys in its environment; on macOS the plugin runs ps about every 10 ms to watch that child's memory. It stops 8 seconds after its converters load, at 60 seconds if loading never finishes, or above 922746880 bytes. It is not a sandbox: after realpath it may read any allowlisted path it can open. Unpublished Hermes code locates the Hermes home, and a failed check refuses the path. Removal deletes the plugin directory, not the markitdown package. Windows was not tested.

plugins.name: doctorpack
plugins.description: Local-first diagnostics, safety audit, and incident postmortems for Hermes Agent.

plugins.name: document-reader
plugins.description: Profile-scoped document OCR for Hermes Desktop and HUD, with a guarded per-profile Windows service.

plugins.name: done-bell
plugins.description: Ring when a Hermes turn finishes so you can leave the window. OS notification, optional chime, and a busy/done chip. Optional "needs you" when approval is waiting. No API keys.

plugins.name: drag-to-pin-session
plugins.description: Pin or unpin sessions from their row with supported desktop SDK actions.

plugins.name: duty-board
plugins.description: Read-only dashboard tab and model-free /duty and hermes duty summaries for waiting conversations, unanswered messages, running turns, undelivered background results and failing cron jobs. Supports all 17 dashboard languages, including right-to-left Arabic. Disclosure — opens HERMES_HOME/state.db with SQLite mode=ro (sessions, messages, turn leases, async delegations, goals) and reads cron/jobs.json and gateway_state.json; writes only HERMES_HOME/duty-board/dismissed.json for dashboard dismissals. Chat requires in-process Hermes 0.21.7+ and a configured owner; shared-chat summaries default to counts only. No network calls, no model calls, no credentials, no background processes.

plugins.name: eatwise
plugins.description: Eatwise (外卖营养教练) — local-first Chinese dietary coach: deterministic meal nutrition reviews, personal daily energy/nutrient targets, and consented on-device profile and meal history through 9 MCP tools over a bundled open food database (TFND + USDA FNDDS). No network, no accounts, no payments; profile schema rejects name/phone/ID/medical fields by design. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (cbc08f6) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 22.5+ on PATH. Disclosure — the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first.

plugins.name: echarts-in-chat
plugins.description: Render a chart inline in the Hermes Desktop transcript: the model emits ::echarts{labels=... values=...} and the plugin mounts an interactive SVG chart (dataZoom slider, click-to-filter legend, resize-aware, 280-560px height clamp) in the plugin SDK's transcript-directive slot. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no environment variables, no background processes, and nothing read or written outside the message it renders; the chart is drawn locally as inline SVG with no third-party libraries.

plugins.name: edit-ledger
plugins.description: Local ledger of the turns in which the agent changed files with write_file or patch: /edit-log shows how many turns changed files, how many files in all, the median per turn, the most changed file type and how long ago the last one was, per model, platform or day, a table of file types (extensions), or the newest turns, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /edit-log recent lists the newest turns (ten, or up to 100 with /edit-log recent 50). A turn another plugin keeps going is counted once. Disclosure — subscribes to pre_verify as an observer only: always returns nothing, so it never keeps the agent going or changes a turn; writes turn metadata (model, platform, file count, files per extension, a 12-digit hash of the session id; never a path, file name or answer text) to plugin-data/edit-ledger/edits.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; never opens the changed files; no network

plugins.name: effortless-hermes
plugins.description: Picks the reasoning effort for every prompt: a fast judge (Jev/TypeSafe, a local OpenAI-compatible model, or any custom API) reads the next message once per turn and rewrites the request's reasoning effort before it ships — easy questions run cheap, hard jobs get high. Port of effortless for Claude Code. Disclosure — sends the next message (≤4000 chars) plus a short recent-conversation excerpt (≤1600 chars) to the configured judge endpoint (default api.typesafe.ai for Jev; a local or custom OpenAI-compatible API otherwise), solely to pick the effort; the optional model_map setting (off by default) also switches the turn's model to the one you map to the verdict; keeps recent per-turn token counts in its own plugin state; no telemetry; secrets resolved only through Hermes' secret scope; stdlib-only, no pip dependencies.

plugins.name: enchanted-composer
plugins.description: Draft enhancement, reusable prompt libraries, undo/redo, and owner-bound full-duplex voice for Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — Derived from hermes-live-voice by Synero (itself derived from hermes-talk) and prompt-enhance by apoapostolov (both MIT; notices preserved). Starting voice captures microphone audio. The Codex-subscription lane spawns the official codex app-server CLI under its own login with a minimal environment; through it the captured profile's SOUL.md (up to 4,000 chars), the list of installed skills and enabled tools, and Hermes task results go to OpenAI. The API lane runs only when COMPOSER_REALTIME_OFFER_URL is set: it posts the SDP offer to that https URL with COMPOSER_OPENAI_API_KEY, or the profile's OPENAI_API_KEY, as a Bearer token (redirects refused). A user-configured wss:// bridge receives microphone audio, chat/profile identifiers and task results. Spoken requests the voice model delegates run as Hermes agent turns with tools in the chat where voice started; runs that need approval are stopped, not approved. Settings and usage totals are stored under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/enchanted-composer/. No telemetry, no self-updater, no Codex OAuth-file reads.

plugins.name: entropicmem
plugins.description: Durable local memory for Hermes agents: SQLite FTS5 facts with cited, explainable recall; a Markdown vault with knowledge-graph export and an interactive visual graph; and turn-prefetch context injection with reason tokens. Write policy auto-redacts high-confidence secrets at write time (other PII types are warn-only findings) and stored-content injection screening flags and warns on recall and prefetch payloads (flag-and-warn, fail-open by design, not a blocking filter). Includes a 34-command CLI, destructive-op gates with automatic backups, and an append-only audit log. Disclosure — all memory data (vault markdown, memory.db, index.db, backups) stays local under HERMES_HOME/entropicmem/; a shared publish DB defaults to HERMES_HOME/entropicmem-shared/. The CLI init command appends ENTROPICMEM_* settings to HERMES_HOME/.env (append-only). Vector embeddings are off by default; only with embeddings_enabled: true (provider) or ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS=1 / query --semantic (CLI) and the optional sentence-transformers extra installed does first use download all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from huggingface.co; otherwise the provider has no network egress. The CLI ingest command fetches a user-supplied URL; CLI graph export writes to ./export in the cwd by default and its HTML loads D3/marked from d3js.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened; CLI graph serve starts a loopback HTTP server. entropicmem_patch_core edits the plugin's own Core-memory markdown (Persona/User_Profile), not Hermes core, and is off by default.

plugins.name: epistemic-harness
plugins.description: Record a provisional claim or uncertainty before an evidence-gathering step, then link the actual observation to it.

plugins.name: error-ledger
plugins.description: Local ledger of failed provider calls (rate limits, overloads, timeouts, context overflows): /errors shows how many attempts failed per model, provider or cause, how many Hermes could retry, and the most common HTTP status, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /errors days puts one day on each line, newest first; /errors recent lists the newest failures (ten, or up to 100 with /errors recent 50) and how long ago each happened. Disclosure — writes failed-attempt metadata (ids, provider, model, HTTP status, Hermes's failure class, exception class name, timings; no error message, request or prompt text) to plugin-data/error-ledger/errors.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

plugins.name: evalroute
plugins.description: Route a task to the right (model, reasoning effort) arm before you start. Classifies the task into a lane, prints a provenance-carrying route card, and installs per-model reasoning-effort defaults. Strong rules run locally; weak-signal classification calls the host LLM and consumes tokens. The separate harness and shim can make paid provider calls when explicitly run; no plugin-owned credentials. Disclosure — weak-signal task classification sends the task text to your active Hermes model via the host LLM facade (token cost). The model-callable tool, /route, /rate and observed /model and /reasoning commands append task text and command args to a local ledger at <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/labels.jsonl. "hermes evalroute install-routes" rewrites agent.reasoning_overrides in config.yaml when you run it. The bundled harness and Hermes shim are never run by the plugin. When run by hand they make paid provider calls, execute model-generated code on the host via shell checkers, and run hermes -z with approvals bypassed. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute sync" (run by hand) downloads the route table from the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel into HERMES_HOME and route cards then show that dataset's text; "hermes evalroute dispatch" (run by hand) spawns a single-query hermes chat on the routed model (Nous provider by default) — or, with --runner claude-code, a `claude -p` (Claude Code) process under the user's own Claude account, whose per-run cost is recorded in the local sidecar — with the brief as its query, inheriting the current environment except HERMES_YOLO_MODE (the worker never inherits --yolo; its approvals follow approvals.single_query_mode, default deny), and writes its report and a .dispatch.json sidecar beside the brief. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute contribute" (run by hand only) refuses to run unless evalroute.contribute: true is set in config.yaml, and then uploads redacted outcome rows only — lane, routed arm, confirmed arm, verdict, method, facet counts, ISO week and an HMAC-SHA256 task hash; never task text, notes, paths or the salt — to the user's own path (contributed/<hf-username>/) in the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel using the user's existing huggingface_hub login; "--dry-run" prints the exact rows and sends nothing; the per-install salt stays local in <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/contribute.salt. Since evalroute 0.9.1 (schema 2) the same upload also carries lane-correction rows as lane pairs (from_lane, to_lane, method, week) with no task text, plus the max_turns value and harness name the arm ran under. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute install-encoder <dir|owner/name>" (run by hand only) downloads a small text-classification model (the default id keppy/evalroute-lane-encoder is a 146 MB ModernBERT fine-tune on the Hugging Face Hub) into <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/encoder/ and from then on "hermes evalroute route" runs it locally, offline, to classify the task when the keyword rules are weak, instead of the LLM call; it needs torch and transformers in the plugin environment (pip extra evalroute[encoder]), which the plugin does not install; "install-encoder --remove" deletes it. "hermes evalroute export-cases" (run by hand only) writes your --lane-pinned route rows, task text included, to a local file you name, for training your own encoder; stdout carries counts only and nothing is uploaded. As of 0.6.2 the plugin is a thin adapter: all behaviour lives in the PyPI package evalroute (>=0.9.2,<0.10), declared as a Python dependency that Hermes installs on your confirmation.

plugins.name: event-read
plugins.description: Read one CalDAV calendar collection you run, with list_events and read_event. Disclosure — Sends CALDAV_USER and CALDAV_PASSWORD as Basic auth to your CALDAV_URL, does not follow redirects, and starts no local program. Over plain http that password travels unencrypted. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway reads the calendar with your password. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. A watch is a cron job you create yourself with hermes cron create. Each run is at least one model turn, there is no daily cap, and the job stays until you run hermes cron remove. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. When the watch can run, it reports a problem on the first run, when the cause changes and again after 23 hours, or on every run when its data directory cannot be written. Each request gives up after 20 seconds without data, and a whole call has no time limit. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it. State lives in plugin-data/event-read. Not tested against a vendor-hosted calendar.

plugins.name: excel_line
plugins.description: Excel-backed hierarchical long-term memory tree (10-row cap per workbook, dynamic branching, leaf pointers). Classifier defaults to the host model; third-party keyless rotation is opt-in.

plugins.name: field-academy
plugins.description: Learn Hermes by doing real work. Four paths (Messenger, Traveler, Crossroads, Boundary Keeper) climb Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced to a capstone on a problem of your own, and a fifth, Guide, covers setting Hermes up for a client: practice labs built from made-up data, a proposal, one real service run by a scheduled job for several days, a recovery drill, and a review signed by a reviewer you choose. Every mission ends with a check on something you made; your own Hermes scores your written answers in a new chat; passed missions come back for short spaced reviews; and at the end of a path you can create a Field Record, your own self-issued learning record. Field Academy is an independent community plugin. It is not made, issued or endorsed by Nous Research. Disclosure — no network calls (a source link opens in your browser only when you click it); no credentials, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates; registers six tools, two hooks, the /academy command and one skill: pre_llm_call may add one sentence offering a practice to the user message, only in interactive desktop, TUI and CLI sessions, and post_tool_call records which tool was used; pressing Try it or a scoring button opens a new chat and sends the practice or scoring prompt there (on an older Hermes it goes to the clipboard instead); the Desktop page calls gateway list methods only (session.list, cron.manage list, skills.manage list, tools.list, mcp.catalog, commands.catalog, setup.runtime_check); stores progress, pasted documents, practice labs, review packets and saved Field Records in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/field-academy/; reads a file you name (UTF-8 text, max 5 MiB) and hashes a recording you name without copying it; Guide labs write and check made-up .env and auth.json files inside its own labs folder (refusing to build in a real Hermes home) and never read Hermes's real ones; on the Guide path reads Hermes's run-history database read-only, jobs.json and up to 25 log files (2 MiB each), keeping only timestamps for the job you name, and reads install-stamp.json for the Hermes version; no private Hermes imports.

plugins.name: file-tray
plugins.description: Session file tray — paths the Hermes agent touched via read_file, write_file, or patch. Desktop pane and /files. No API keys.

plugins.name: filebox
plugins.description: Dual-panel commander file browser for Hermes Desktop — whitelist-guarded file CRUD, copy/move/symlink, media preview, multi-select, rename, and trash. No network I/O, no model tokens.

plugins.name: financial-datasets
plugins.description: Stock market data from Financial Datasets - financial statements, prices, SEC filings, insider and institutional ownership, KPIs, news, macro data, and a stock screener.

plugins.name: fish-audio
plugins.description: Lifelike voices for your agent: Fish Audio's expressive text-to-speech in 80+ languages, plus transcription, voice cloning and a voice library. The official Fish Audio plugin: Fish's Drama 3 model with word-level direction, speech-to-text, Fish Audio's community voice library, voice cloning and voice design, with a Voices page in Hermes Desktop. Fish Audio becomes a Hermes speech and transcription provider for voice replies, read-aloud, voice notes and Desktop dictation, with sentence-by-sentence streaming in CLI voice mode and Desktop, and live dictation captions on Hermes 0.21.6+ (stt.streaming: true). Adds the fish_speak, fish_voices and fish_transcribe tools, /fish and hermes fish commands, and four skills. Disclosure — sends your Fish API key and the text, audio (with file names) and voice titles, tags, descriptions, cover images and design instructions you ask it to process to api.fish.audio, or to the base_url you configure, and reads your Fish wallet for balances and model choice; with live dictation on, microphone audio streams to api.fish.audio's realtime speech-to-text endpoint while you speak, billed per committed phrase rounded up to a second; synthesis, transcription, cloning and voice design are paid requests billed to your Fish account, except the free s2.1-pro-free model (free through 30 November 2026), whose requests Fish may use to improve its models. The key comes from the profile's secret scope (Hermes stores it in the profile .env; a single-profile install may also read FISH_API_KEY from the environment). Generated audio and subtitles are written to Hermes's audio cache; clone samples and recordings it uploads must be regular audio files, and Hermes config, secret and credential paths are refused. Cloning and deleting voices from chat or the model tools go through Hermes's approval gate and follow your approval settings. The Desktop Voices page and a Fish Audio settings page add gateway routes under /api/plugins/fish-audio/, behind the Hermes dashboard's existing authentication. On the Voices page, previews, clones and voice designs are billed; cloning a voice or saving a designed one creates a voice in your Fish account; cloning and deleting are confirmed on the page (a speaker-consent box, a typed voice name) instead of through Hermes's approval gate; and Use sets the profile's Fish voice, and its speech provider when none is set. The settings page and /fish alias can set or reset the profile's Fish model and voice and save up to 50 voice names in the profile's config. Preview and design audio files are deleted from the gateway once returned; a design's audio is held in gateway memory so you can save it, until it is saved, a later design or save finds it over an hour old, or the gateway stops; clone uploads are deleted after the clone, or by the next upload once idle for 15 minutes. With a key set, Desktop reads your Fish wallet when an agent is selected and about every five minutes, for the status-bar credit; favourites stay in Desktop's plugin storage on that computer, and fetched previews stay in the window's memory until it closes. Includes a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report and files it to this plugin's repository as a public GitHub issue or comment with your gh login only after you approve the exact text; reports leave out keys, credit amounts and your own voice ids, and security problems go to the repository's private advisory form instead. No telemetry.

plugins.name: fleet-policy
plugins.description: For administrators who pin settings through the managed scope: records what each agent role really sends to the provider (model, reasoning effort, service tier, plus the tier the provider says it served) next to the managed-scope state and the effective config (`hermes fleet-policy status --json`); measures cron cost per job — runs, empty runs, $/day, gate present (`crons --cost`); and `watch`, a generic wake gate for cron scripts that replays one read tool on an MCP server and wakes the agent only when new item ids appear (stock `wakeAgent` gate, no LLM call otherwise). Ships two skills (managed-scope admin, recurring tasks). Disclosure — records only model, reasoning effort and service tier per role (no message content, headers or keys) via the pre_api_request and pre_auxiliary_call hooks and a pass-through llm_execution middleware, stored in $HERMES_HOME/fleet-policy/observed.json; crons --cost opens cron/executions.db and state.db read-only and checks each cron run's final reply locally for silence; watch is an operator CLI command that calls one MCP tool at the config's server_url (or the admin-pinned watch_server_url) with config headers in which ${VAR} env values are expanded, follows redirects, and writes seen ids to a state file at the config-chosen path; the recurring-tasks skill has the agent write watch configs under $HERMES_HOME/watches, a script under $HERMES_HOME/scripts and a cron job; no other network access, no telemetry.

plugins.name: fluxer-platform
plugins.description: Fluxer gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Native Fluxer integration using Fluxer's bot REST API for outbound messages, Gateway WebSocket events for inbound dispatches, message edits, agent-requested reactions, pins, reply references, media delivery, and channel-directory enumeration. Component button

plugins.name: fmsg-platform
plugins.description: fmsg platform adapter for Hermes Agent. Real-time inbound over the fmsg-webapi WebSocket (/fmsg/ws), outbound via its JSON REST routes. Authenticates with an fmsg API key (fmsgk_...) exchanged for a short-lived JWT — run the agent as a derived sub-account such as @alice_hermes@example.com. Only http

plugins.name: foresee
plugins.description: Let AI assistants shop for home and auto insurance: compare instant quotes across every carrier. Connects to the hosted Foresee MCP server (Streamable HTTP at agents.go-foresee.com), with three workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package (hosted MCP server plus three skills), no Python and nothing runs locally; the vendor is Foresee Insurance Services, LLC (go-foresee.com). Every quote request sends the profile the user gives in chat (ZIP, age or date of birth, vehicles, drivers, driving record, home details) to agents.go-foresee.com with no account or API key. The live_carrier_quotes tool additionally sends the user's identity (name, date of birth, street address, email, optionally phone and driver's licence number) and, after the user's in-chat consent recorded verbatim, Foresee's agents submit those details to the selected insurance carriers, who may run a soft credit-based insurance score pull and contact the user. Foresee does not take payment or bind policies.

plugins.name: freight-reconciliation
plugins.description: Payer-side freight reconciliation: import carrier bills and trip ledgers into a deterministic local core (SQLite, WAL, no cloud), re-calculate against contracted rates and produce evidence-linked difference lists for human review — 14 MCP tools over uvx stdio (engine pinned to the immutable commit e8cd259c, release v0.4.1), with 3 bilingual workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs uv on PATH. Never approves payments, sends messages or writes back to ERP/TMS; final confirmations route through a local admin page the model cannot reach. Disclosure — the optional freight-admin page listens on 127.0.0.1 and is where a human confirms mappings, rules, matches and exports; nothing leaves the machine.

plugins.name: freshdesk
plugins.description: Generic Freshdesk API v2 tools for Hermes Agent. Unaffiliated community connector, not a Freshworks product. Disclosure: calls the account's native Freshdesk HTTPS origin with profile-scoped secrets FRESHDESK_DOMAIN and FRESHDESK_API_KEY; downloads an attachment into the Hermes cache only from that ticket's own attachment hosts; the two write tools escalate to Hermes human approval and fail closed when no person is present. No third-party dependencies, shell commands, telemetry, or self-updater.

plugins.name: frihet
plugins.description: Official Hermes Agent integration for Frihet — discoverability, setup, diagnostics, and operating guidance for the Frihet MCP. Zero duplicated tools; the canonical 158-operation Frihet surface stays in @frihet/mcp-server and the remote endpoint https://mcp.frihet.io/mcp. Disclosure — /frihet setup and /frihet doctor send an unauthenticated MCP initialize to mcp.frihet.io (or FRIHET_MCP_URL); /frihet doctor also makes one read-only list_invoices call through Hermes's MCP client once you grant plugins.entries.frihet.mcp_allowlist; reads ~/.hermes/config.yaml only to check that an mcp_servers.frihet block exists; the pre_tool_call hook prompts before Frihet MCP calls it classifies as irreversible or unknown, but reads and draft-first creates pass without a prompt unless the server sets trust: untrusted.

plugins.name: fusion
plugins.description: Multi-model fusion router for Hermes: detects the model fleet your harnesses (Hermes, Codex, Claude, Grok) actually have installed and builds a Frontier -> Middle Manager -> Frontier routing structure with pinned models and provenance from execution records. `hermes fusion teams|validate|plan|run|index|report|status`.

plugins.name: fxmacrodata
plugins.description: FXMacroData macro and FX research: official-source economic releases, indicator history, release calendars, policy rates, yield curves, FX, commodities and COT positioning, with source citations. Native tools for 23 REST operations and 49 hosted MCP tools, plus a /fxmacrodata USD brief command. Disclosure — tool calls send their arguments over HTTPS to api.fxmacrodata.com and mcp.fxmacrodata.com only, with FXMACRODATA_API_KEY in a request header when it is set. The key is optional: without it the data catalogue, the USD release calendar and recent USD releases (15-minute delay) work, and other data answers with a subscribe message. No files written, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry. It also adds a short research-guidance section to the system prompt and 72 tools in the fxmacrodata toolset; MCP tool behaviour is served remotely and not covered by the pinned sha.

plugins.name: gadget
plugins.description: Talk to your Hermes from small ESP32 devices with a screen, microphone and speaker: hold a button, ask, and hear the answer. Adds a gateway platform where each device is a chat, plus tools to list devices, show a card on a screen and run device actions (LEDs, relays). Disclosure — the gateway listens for devices on a WebSocket port (8765, all interfaces by default; plain ws:// unless tls_cert/tls_key are set). New devices need a Hermes pairing code unless listed in GADGET_ALLOWED_USERS; GADGET_ALLOW_ALL_USERS skips pairing (development only). A paired device answers the agent's command approvals for its own chat (allow once or deny). The first approved device becomes the platform's home channel by default. Spoken replies that are not WAV are converted with the local ffmpeg. `hermes gadget update --latest` downloads firmware from this repository's GitHub releases, checks size and SHA-256 against the release manifest (files carry build provenance attestations) and sends it to the device. Writes only under plugin-data/gadget/. Uses Hermes's own STT, TTS and image cache; no telemetry. Independent community project, not affiliated with Nous Research.

plugins.name: gbrain-plugin
plugins.description: Community (non-official) plugin wiring GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT) into Hermes as a local memory layer over MCP: /gbrain status command, desktop starter, and per-profile Postgres setup/update/maintenance scripts. Not affiliated with upstream. Disclosure — the plugin itself only adds a /gbrain status command and a Desktop pane; GBrain is installed by the user via scripts/setup.sh, which installs bun (curl|bash), an unpinned gbrain from GitHub HEAD, and provisions PostgreSQL with sudo.

plugins.name: gbrain-pointer
plugins.description: Read-only memory.provider for GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT; not affiliated). After each non-trivial turn it searches a GBrain MCP server (`gbrain serve --http`) in the background and injects up to the configured limit (3 by default, capped at 10) of `[source:slug] title` pointers into the next turn as fallible background context. It never writes to GBrain and adds no tools or hooks. Disclosure — after each non-trivial turn, the first 500 characters of your message are sent to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp; plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless GBRAIN_POINTER_ALLOW_HTTP=1), and the profile's GBrain OAuth client id and secret go to that server's /token endpoint. Redirects and proxy settings are ignored. Only the slug, title and source id of up to 10 results are kept and injected into the next turn as background context; rows GBrain flags as suspected injection are skipped. Tokens and pointers stay in memory only. It never writes to GBrain; no other network calls, no telemetry.

plugins.name: gbrain-retrieval-reflex
plugins.description: pre_llm_call hook plugin, enabled with `hermes plugins enable`: injects ambient context from a GBrain instance before each turn (volunteer_context, then a hybrid-query fallback). Not a `memory.provider`. Silent no-op when GBrain is unreachable or no token is set. Disclosure — before each non-trivial turn the last six user and assistant messages (truncated) and the current message are sent with a GBRAIN_TOKEN bearer token to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp), and returned brain-page text is injected into the turn.

plugins.name: gemini-live-bridge
plugins.description: Realtime duplex voice chat with the Gemini Live API — a status-bar minibar for the Hermes desktop app (transcript, model catalog, thinking level, session token meter, auto-redial via session resumption). Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live WebSocket and the user's key (requires_env GOOGLE_API_KEY); the desktop UI only talks to localhost and receives single-use ephemeral tokens. No agent tools; desktop-focused, dashboard tab hidden. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GOOGLE_API_KEY (or GEMINI_API_KEY) from the environment; input/output transcripts are held in backend memory for the session, and a Gemini session-resumption handle is written to .resume.json inside the plugin's install directory.

plugins.name: genealogy-research-recipes
plugins.description: Fact-checked genealogy instructions for DNA evidence, record searches and proof judgment. Native read-only skill bundle with recipe sources and an offline given-name lookup helper. Disclosure — optional third-party services and commands described by recipes require separately authorized tools and credentials; the adapter itself makes no service calls and registers no tools, hooks or MCP server.

plugins.name: gh-ref
plugins.description: @gh:owner/repo#123 context references: attach a public GitHub issue or pull request to a message (title, state, labels, description, the latest comments; for pull requests also the branches, merge state and change size). Disclosure — sends anonymous HTTPS GET requests to api.github.com only (the referenced owner/repo and number leave the machine; no token, public repositories only, 60 requests an hour per IP address); no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @gh: reference provider.

plugins.name: gigamail
plugins.description: Email and calendar through an existing local GigaMail MCP server, with a workflow skill and stdio launcher. Requires Python and a separately configured backend; no automatic backend installation or updates. Reads real mail and attachments; sending, deletion and calendar writes use GigaMail's out-of-band human approval. Disclosure — a thin stdio launcher for the separately installed GigaMail MCP server from Adecubed inc. (gigamail.ai, github.com/adecubed/gigamail, same author as this plugin); the plugin holds no mail logic or credentials and downloads nothing, but it starts that third-party executable from PATH or a configured path, points it at GigaMail's own data directory under your user profile (%APPDATA%\ADE or ~/.ade), and send, delete and calendar writes are gated by that backend's out-of-band approval rather than by Hermes.

plugins.name: git-autosave
plugins.description: Lightweight local alternative to directory checkpoints for Git projects. Before a mutating tool call it saves the affected repository's working state to a private local shadow ref (refs/hermes-autosave/<branch>, with reflog) through a private index, or copies the single existing file outside Git; `hermes autosave find` and `restore` recover a pre-edit version. Disclosure — runs local git subprocesses in repositories the agent touches (hooks, clean filters, fsmonitor and lazy fetch disabled); writes shadow refs/reflogs into those repositories' .git and unencrypted file copies into its plugin-data directory; never changes HEAD, branches, the real index or the working tree and never pushes; skips credential stores (.env, auth.json, .ssh, .aws, .docker, .kube, gh/gcloud/azure configs) and dependency directories; `hermes autosave sweep` reads the session database read-only and is scheduled by the user; no network, no background processes; it observes only and never blocks or approves a tool call.

plugins.name: git-hook
plugins.description: Auto fetch/pull before reads, and commit + push only the files each turn changed, for every git worktree Hermes touches. Disclosure — after each turn it commits and pushes (push on by default; GIT_HOOK_PUSH=0 keeps commits local) the changed files of git worktrees under GIT_HOOK_ROOTS (default PROJECTS_ROOT, "*" for every repo), pushing to origin HEAD when no upstream is set; it pulls --ff-only before reads. A branch whose direct push the remote refuses on policy grounds (branch protection, a PR-required ruleset) is never committed to again: the hook drops its own unpushed commit, leaves the edit staged and dirty, and reports it once.

plugins.name: git-tasks
plugins.description: Multi-repo GitHub issues & PRs in an Orca-style Tasks view for Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — runs your logged-in `gh` CLI and `git` through Hermes Desktop's shell bridge and scans your configured clone folders for GitHub repos; approve, close and reopen act on GitHub in one click; creates git worktrees and opens seeded Hermes sessions from the detail view.

plugins.name: githermes
plugins.description: GitHub PRs and issues as a right workspace pane in Hermes Desktop, via the connected gh CLI. Disclosure — shells out to your logged-in gh CLI; the in-pane update pill only runs `hermes plugins update githermes` (no fetch-and-replace) and currently compares against upstream main rather than the pinned sha.

plugins.name: github_app
plugins.description: GitHub and GitHub Enterprise tools with bot-first attribution and approval-gated issue/PR writes. Disclosure — authenticates as a GitHub App from GITHUB_APP_ID, GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID and a private key in GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY or GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH/_FILE (read from the profile env or HERMES_HOME/.env, held in memory only, never written or logged), falling back to GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN or `gh auth token` when no App variables are set, and reports which identity acted in every result. Talks only to https://api.github.com or the operator-configured GITHUB_API_URL / settings.api_url (HTTPS, no redirects; no tool argument can change the host). Issue/comment/review/merge writes stay disabled until settings.allow_write_actions is true and each one additionally goes through Hermes's human-approval prompt via its pre_tool_call hook (an 'always' answer does not persist).

plugins.name: glasser
plugins.description: Glasser's hosted MCP: search, inspect and run 1,000+ paid data endpoints (people and company enrichment, SEO, web, social media, US property, stock quotes) with one key, pay per call. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: a stdio bridge through mcp-remote (browser sign-in, no key in the package) plus a bundled skill for setup and the spending rules. Requires Node.js 18+. Disclosure — paid data broker: each run tool call charges your Glasser balance per the endpoint's published price with no in-Hermes confirm step; runs npx mcp-remote@0.14.3 as a local stdio bridge to https://api.glasser.ai/mcp; the sign-in token is cached by mcp-remote under ~/.mcp-auth/.

plugins.name: gmail
plugins.description: Hermes Desktop Gmail mailbox UI for search, reading, and thread inspection, with preview-confirmed send, reply, archive, trash, and label changes. Uses the active profile's existing Google Workspace OAuth setup; email is sensitive external content. Gmail actions and data access require user review and configuration. Disclosure — reads the active profile's Hermes Google Workspace token (google_token.json, refreshed in memory only) and calls the Gmail API; opening an unread message marks it read, other send/trash/label changes go through a confirm step (one setting can skip every review dialog, and then the prepare ticket, account/profile binding, exact snapshot validation and readback verification still run); remote email images load only after the user allows them. Attachment metadata listing and bounded read-only attachment download (25 MB cap) are profile/account-scoped.

plugins.name: go-whatsapp
plugins.description: Outbound WhatsApp tools through GOWA: registers GOWA's native MCP server and adds device listing, pairing, and removal. Setup can connect an existing server or explicitly install pinned GOWA v9.5.0 as a loopback-only authenticated native user service on Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64/arm64, or Windows x86_64. Disclosure — agents can send messages and mutate WhatsApp state through the linked account; session databases grant account access. The plugin does not ingest incoming messages or configure webhooks.

plugins.name: gondola-provider
plugins.description: Gondola, a USDC-settled marketplace API for Venice AI inference

plugins.name: gonogo
plugins.description: Turn a pilot-scale eval score into a deployment decision — Wilson intervals, a confidence threshold that routes uncertain cases to a human, and an honest INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE verdict when the sample cannot support the claim. Disclosure — gonogo_report writes report JSON/HTML to the path the model supplies.

plugins.name: good-student
plugins.description: Wrong-question diagnosis and study-action loop for parents and students — deterministic local core (SQLite, no cloud), host-model recognition gated by parent confirmation. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); good-student MCP server pinned to immutable commit 2469cbb over uvx, with the good-student workflow skill bundled. Needs Python 3.10+ via uv. No credentials required; all data stays on-device and nothing is uploaded.

plugins.name: govee
plugins.description: Discover and control Govee lights (power, brightness, color, white temperature, scenes) through Govee's developer API. Every command is checked against the model's advertised capabilities and ranges, then confirmed by a state read-back. Disclosure — sends device IDs and control commands to openapi.api.govee.com with your Govee API key; the model can change light state; stores nothing on disk.

plugins.name: grok-acp
plugins.description: xAI Grok subscription as a Hermes model provider, driven over ACP stdio. Disclosure — spawns the vendor grok CLI found on PATH (grok agent over ACP stdio, plus grok models / grok login during setup) and drives your existing Grok subscription login; no API key is stored and Hermes provider secrets are stripped from the child environment.

plugins.name: groq-provider
plugins.description: Groq as a Hermes model provider (`--provider groq`, or Groq in `hermes model`): reasoning effort is sent in the form each Groq model accepts, so gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b work (through a custom endpoint, Hermes 0.21.5 sends them a value Groq rejects with HTTP 400), and the model list leaves out Groq's speech-to-text, text-to-speech, prompt-guard and 4K-context models that Hermes cannot run. Not affiliated with Groq. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Hermes' own client with GROQ_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

plugins.name: gurusup-brain
plugins.description: Your company's memory in Hermes: search decisions, people, customers and projects across every source your team connected to Gurusup (Slack, HubSpot, Notion, uploaded documents and more), with the sources behind each answer. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1, no local code and no API keys. Disclosure — hosted-only MCP connector with no local code: every tool call goes to Gurusup's server at mcp.brain.gurusup.com under the signed-in Gurusup account (OAuth via `hermes mcp add gurusup-brain --url https://mcp.brain.gurusup.com/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401), and answers are limited to what that account can see; write tools save knowledge to the company's Gurusup workspace (add_company_knowledge, skills_publish) and send issue reports or feedback to Gurusup (report_issue, send_feedback), and request_human_info can message a teammate on Slack or phone them when its dispatch flag is set.

plugins.name: ha-sidebar-navigator
plugins.description: Full-power sidebar navigator & uncapped project/session explorer for Hermes Desktop. Bypasses the 3-session overview cap with searchable, scrollable project trees and timeline view.

plugins.name: hades-coding-workflows
plugins.description: Coding workflow skills — dual-model harness, subagent-driven development, and implementation planning patterns for Hermes Agent

plugins.name: handflow
plugins.description: Manus-style planning flow — the agent plans in steps and marks them as it works, with a live desktop pane.

plugins.name: health-data
plugins.description: Local health and daily-context data store for Hermes.

plugins.name: health-insights
plugins.description: Deterministic, local-first analysis of your own Apple Health data - weekly trends, rule-based concern checks, nutrition versus Dietary Reference Intakes, an IOM energy target, lab results and opt-in modules (GLP-1 monitoring, medication adherence; all off by default). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package of ten skills that drive the separately installed health-insights command line tool (installed from the plugin's own pinned copy); the plugin itself contains no executable. Works on a self-hosted HealthRelay or Health Bridge receiver database. Disclosure - it handles sensitive health data, so use a local model or one you trust; personal integrations (medication counts, model wording) are off by default. Disclosure — the skills run a separately installed health-insights CLI that reads your HealthRelay or Health Bridge SQLite database read-only and keeps imported lab and ECG results under ~/.local/share/health-insights; the health values it prints are sent to whichever model provider your Hermes session uses.

plugins.name: healthcare
plugins.description: Local-first personal health records: encrypted on-device Vault (AES-GCM) for vitals, medications, activities, emotions, sleep, encounters, diagnosis mentions, medication plans and reminders, served through a Keychain-paired local daemon with 24 scoped MCP tools. Zero-config first run: the plugin bootstraps Vault + daemon + agent pairing automatically under PLUGIN_DATA. Engine pinned to an immutable PyPI release (healthcare-mcp==0.2.1) over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), macOS only, Python 3.11+. Zero network by default; the optional LLM report-import endpoint stays off unless the user configures it. Approval-gated deletes, tamper-evident audit chain. Disclosure — personal health record-keeping, not medical advice (the skill forbids diagnoses and dosage changes); first run has uvx fetch healthcare-mcp==0.2.1 from PyPI; the optional report-import path posts report images to Alibaba DashScope (qwen-vl-max) unless HEALTHCARE_LLM_ENDPOINT points elsewhere, and only when HEALTHCARE_LLM_API_KEY is set.

plugins.name: healthrelay
plugins.description: Read-only access to your own Apple Health data through a self-hosted HealthRelay receiver. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with one stdio MCP server (ten read-only tools, including intake evidence; no raw SQL, no write tools) and three skills for setup, review and troubleshooting. Requires your own HealthRelay receiver (health-bridge) and an iPhone app you sign yourself; the plugin ships neither.
