each agent node is a child hermes chat --query-file … --oneshot -Q … inheriting the runner's environment, and a node with profile set runs as that named profile (with its own credentials) only if the target's workflow_team.json lists the launcher; a gate's wait.until_argv runs an agent-authored argv directly from the runner, outside Hermes' tool-approval gate (the engine uses no shell, but the shipped machine-watch and incident-response templates use it to run a shell line read from a fixed-name handoff file under $HERMES_HOME, and release-lifecycle one read from a per-run handoff file in the run dir); the runner makes itself the subreaper of its children and SIGTERM/SIGKILLs any process a node leaves running (its own descendants plus pids registered in the run's .proctree_sidecar.jsonl) when the node finishes, retries or the run stops; run and amend send a one-token ping through Hermes' configured providers to check pinned model routes; at gate.held/run.done/run.failed the runner reads the API server key from config.yaml and POSTs a wake turn to the local Hermes API server — the gate.held wake only relays the gate to the human, but the run.done wake tells the woken session to turn the run's findings into tracked work and dispatch follow-up work (as PRs) before the turn ends, and the run.failed wake to apply one corrective amend/repair/resume; a transform_llm_output hook appends a ::workflow{id} card line to replies for runs the session launched in the last 30 minutes; the runner reads WORKFLOW_MAX_SEATS (that key only) from $HERMES_HOME/.env and the active profile's .env; state.db is read read-only, including every profile's session ids and profile names, and status/wait can read runs in sibling profiles' workflows dirs; state lives under $HERMES_HOME/workflows/ (or a configured runs_root). No other network of its own.

plugins.name: hermes-wsl-terminal
plugins.description: Run Hermes' terminal tools inside an existing WSL distro on Windows: one bash -c per command as the distro's default user, over the same files Windows sees at /mnt/<drive>, with no Docker Desktop, no image and no container to start or tear down. A host cwd is translated (C:\Users\me\proj becomes /mnt/c/Users/me/proj, \\wsl.localhost paths become the distro's own paths) and the mount root is asked once with wslpath, so a distro that moved its automount point still gets correct paths. cwd persists across commands, stdin and exit codes ride through wsl.exe, and hermes doctor / setup and the dashboard picker get real rows (wsl.exe path, WSL version, distros present, selected distro). HERMES_WSL_DISTRO and HERMES_WSL_USER select the distro and the user. Disclosure — this is a full-access backend, not a sandbox: when it is the selected backend, everything the terminal tool runs executes as your user inside your distro, with that distro's files, permissions and network access, so dangerous-command approval stays on and Hermes never stops the distro. The plugin itself reads no credentials, stores nothing and makes no network calls; it spawns wsl.exe per command and wslpath once per distro. It rewrites one core-produced string, the trailing cwd marker, because under WSL a command substitution is handed the directory wsl.exe started in rather than the shell's current one (measurements in the repo's VALIDATION.md); nothing in Hermes is patched or rebound at runtime.

plugins.name: hermes-wslc-sandbox
plugins.description: Run Hermes' terminal, file and execute_code tools in a Linux container on Microsoft's WSL Containers (wslc) runtime, so Windows users who run WSL Containers get a sandbox without Docker Desktop. Disclosure — the plugin spawns the wslc CLI (one short-lived process per command, plus one long-lived container per environment) and every call runs inside that container; containers have outbound network access unless docker_network is false; persistent sandboxes are left stopped on disk until removed; host environment variables enter the container only when named in docker_forward_env, and only paths listed in docker_volumes are bind-mounted. wslc rejects --cap-drop, --security-opt, --pids-limit, --init and --storage-opt, so this sandbox is not capability-dropped the way the Docker backend's is, container_disk is reported but not enforced, and dangerous-command approval deliberately stays enabled for this backend. The plugin reads no credentials, stores none, and makes no network calls of its own.

plugins.name: hermes-xai
plugins.description: The xAI API surfaces core does not cover, nothing it already ships (provider, x_search, web search, TTS, STT and Imagine stay in core). Voice module: full-duplex Grok Voice (grok-voice-latest) in the Desktop composer, built like core's GPT-Live mode; the voice model hands real work to Hermes as a normal turn on the open chat (surface voice-live) and reads the result aloud; the backend mints a 300 s xAI client secret so XAI_API_KEY never reaches the renderer. Collections module: one read-only tool, xai_collections_search, over documents the user already indexed in xAI Collections (GET /v1/collections, POST /v1/documents/search). Disclosure — the voice button captures microphone audio and streams it to api.x.ai over a WebSocket; the backend calls api.x.ai once per call with XAI_API_KEY (read through agent.secret_scope) to mint the secret; delegated requests run as normal Hermes turns with the profile's full toolset and approvals, and their final text (up to 3000 characters) plus the last spoken turns are sent back to xAI. Each xai_collections_search call sends the query to api.x.ai with XAI_API_KEY and returns passages into the conversation. Nothing is uploaded, stored or deleted and no telemetry is emitted; xAI bills on the user's key.

plugins.name: hermes-zh
plugins.description: Simplified Chinese (简体中文) language pack. Declarative locales/zh.yaml overlay for part of approval.* and gateway.*; placeholders match en.yaml.

plugins.name: hermes_otel
plugins.description: OpenTelemetry for Hermes Agent: sessions, LLM and API calls, tool calls, sub-agents and approvals as OTLP traces, metrics and logs to any OTLP backend. Disclosure — sends span data including prompts, tool arguments and tool output only to backends you configure (a backends: list, an OTEL_* variable, or LANGSMITH_TRACING=true); by default content_capture is full and unclipped (preview clips to 1200 chars, off sends none); vendor SDK keys already in the environment are used only after that opt-in; with nothing configured it keeps a local owner-only SQLite store under $HERMES_HOME and sends nothing; installs opentelemetry-api, -sdk, -exporter-otlp-proto-http (>=1.35,<2) and PyYAML.

plugins.name: hicortex
plugins.description: Shared fleet memory for Hermes agents: every connected agent learns from all other agents connected to the memory, wherever they run. Sessions across machines and harnesses are distilled into one common brain overnight — what one learns, the whole fleet recalls. Pushes a compact per-turn recall index (entries lazy-load via hicortex_get), injects fresh lessons plus a per-agent standing context block at session start — lesson blocks are delimited and carry an explicit reference-data framing line and provenance header — and exposes the full 9-tool memory surface (search, get, recent, ingest, lessons, index, graph, update, delete) through the shared server. The same server also serves Claude Code, OpenClaw, Pi and opencode agents, so mixed-harness fleets share one brain. Stdlib-only, no pip dependencies. Requires a running Hicortex server (npx @gamaze/hicortex init on any machine); data flow: each user message is sent to your configured Hicortex server for recall (default http://localhost:8787); session distillation runs on the server. Disclosure — sends every user message (and profile name) to your configured Hicortex server each turn for recall, default http://localhost:8787, plain http with a bearer token is accepted for remote servers with a one-time log warning; the server's standing Identity text and lessons are injected into the system prompt; the model can permanently update or delete shared fleet memories via hicortex_update / hicortex_delete without confirmation.

plugins.name: hindsight
plugins.description: Hindsight long-term memory provider — knowledge graph, entity resolution and multi-strategy retrieval (recall/reflect/retain tools plus automatic per-turn capture). Maintained by Vectorize; cloud, local external and local embedded modes are available. `hermes memory setup` fetches its bank-template catalog from raw.githubusercontent.com (vectorize-io/hindsight main). Disclosure — in cloud mode (and local external) every turn's conversation, and every entry the agent adds or replaces in Hermes's built-in MEMORY/USER stores, is sent to api.hindsight.vectorize.io or the URL you configure, into every bank it writes to; local embedded mode starts a background Hindsight daemon (fetched with uvx, version-pinned, on first run when hindsight-api is not installed) and keeps its LLM settings in ~/.hindsight/profiles/<profile>.env; setup writes the keys you enter to the profile .env; repositories under folders you list in trusted_project_dirs may choose their bank with .hindsight/config.toml; `hermes memory setup` fetches its bank-template catalog from raw.githubusercontent.com (vectorize-io/hindsight main).

plugins.name: holographic
plugins.description: Local fact-store memory provider: SQLite with FTS5 keyword search (word forms in English, Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Indonesian, German, Hindi, Arabic, Bengali, Italian, Turkish, Polish and Dutch; Russian and English words of the same root at a lower weight, from bundled DerivBase.Ru (Apache-2.0) and Open English Wordnet (CC BY 4.0) pairs; German compounds and German and Spanish irregular verb forms from bundled Wikidata Lexemes tables (CC0); Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Thai by character n-grams, Chinese also split into words with jieba's dictionary (MIT), Traditional and Simplified Chinese compared as one through a bundled OpenCC table (Apache-2.0), Japanese spelling variants through SudachiDict's (Apache-2.0); synonyms through keywords the agent gives when it stores a fact), trust scores, entities with aliases and HRR (holographic reduced representation) recall, with no API key, network or model calls unless the optional search by meaning (embeddings: on, off by default) is switched on. The provider that shipped in-tree as plugins/memory/holographic, with the same provider name, config (plugins.hermes-memory-store) and memory_store.db, so `hermes update` moves existing users onto it; the schema change is additive and older versions keep working on the file. Taken over from Nous Research's handoff copy (NousResearch/hermes-plugin-holographic) and maintained by itpartypattaya; since 0.1.1 it fixes probe/reason/related/contradict, non-atomic writes and the never-written retrieval_count, gates recall by relevance without repeats, flags duplicates and conflicts when a fact is added, and honours the provider contract (read-only subagent contexts, hermes_home, mirror metadata, backup_paths); since 0.8.0 it keeps the history of every fact (change / end / correct / revert, search and list as_of a date) and `forget` erases a fact with all its versions from the file; since 0.16.0 a name guessed from a fact's text must be shaped like one and stays provisional until a second fact or a person confirms it, and entities can be renamed or deleted (the facts stay). Disclosure — local only unless the optional search by meaning is switched on: reads and writes one SQLite file per profile ($HERMES_HOME/memory_store.db unless db_path says otherwise), or with scope: user / chat / thread one file per user or chat in holographic-users/ or holographic-chats/ next to it; each fact version records where it was written (platform, chat type, chat and thread id, session id, the turn author's id and display name, and whether the person said it or the agent inferred it; never chat titles), shown in full by list, history and export and not in recall unless recall_source: short (date, display name, this or another chat); each confirmation of a fact by a person keeps its time, session id and that person's id (no text); forget deletes that and the confirmations with the fact and keeps only an HMAC of the text, keyed by a random key stored in the same file, as a tombstone; delete_entity removes a name, its aliases and links from the entity index (never a fact) and keeps an HMAC of each name the same way (not of an alias only a fact's text gave, which goes without one), and both rewrite the file so freed pages keep no copy; the first writable open after an upgrade that changes the extraction rules relinks the facts to their entities under the new rules (stores up to 2,000 facts and 500,000 characters; larger ones on fact_store rebuild_entities), changing only the names it guessed and their links, never a fact, a declared name or an alias someone gave; subagents never write, but a cron job's explicit fact_store / fact_feedback calls do unless cron_writes: false (on by default); no subprocesses or telemetry, and no network calls or credentials unless embeddings: on (off by default): then the text of facts, and of messages and fact_store search queries that are not greetings, goes to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint the user configures, also after cron turns while cron_writes is on (embedding_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name such as one without a dot or ending in .local), with the key read from the environment variable the user names (embedding_key_env, OPENAI_API_KEY unless set, sent as a Bearer token to whatever embedding_url is configured, never stored in config) and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject, and facts and messages that look like they hold a secret (checked by pattern, best effort), are not sent; the vectors are kept in the same file (table fact_embeddings), deleted with their fact by forget / end / remove and all of them by the next writable session after the option is switched off; the provider keeps what it received under its own terms; the bundled language dictionaries are gzip-compressed plain-text word lists; with auto_extract on (off by default) user sentences that state a preference or decision are stored.

plugins.name: home-dashboard
plugins.description: Personalizable rice-style Home page with draggable, resizable glass widgets for Hermes Web and Desktop.

plugins.name: homeassistant
plugins.description: Home Assistant gateway platform (state-change events in, persistent notifications and cron notify delivery out) plus the homeassistant toolset (ha_list_entities, ha_get_state, ha_list_services, ha_call_service). Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically.

plugins.name: honcho
plugins.description: Honcho is memory infrastructure for building stateful agents that understand changing people, agents, groups, projects, and ideas over time. Store messages and events, let Honcho reason in the background, then query peer representations, session context, search results, or natural-language insights from any model or framework. Use it managed at api.honcho.dev, run a local stack with the honcho CLI, or self-host the server yourself. Maintained by Plastic Labs; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns, derived conclusions and peer/session ids are sent to the Honcho API (api.honcho.dev by default, or the self-hosted base_url you configure) under your HONCHO_API_KEY; every request also carries X-Honcho-Host (Hermes version and OS platform) and X-Honcho-Plugin (plugin version) headers that Honcho records for usage attribution.

plugins.name: hopper
plugins.description: Add and manage custom OpenRouter models in Hermes without modifying the core catalog.

plugins.name: hud-teach
plugins.description: Click-through numbered marks on any live Mac window — chess, games, Photoshop, Settings — so Hermes can teach on the real UI without clicking for the user.

plugins.name: huddo
plugins.description: Huddo — group chat where people and AI agents talk in the same room. Join by invite link, read and reply, edit or unsend your own messages, react, whisper to one member, pair with your human, wait for new messages, and read or update room apps (shared mini-apps such as task lists that a room owner publishes). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — runs the Huddo MCP server locally over stdio (npx -y huddoai@0.9.8, pinned, npm provenance to this commit; Node 20+); sends and receives room messages via api.huddo.ai, readable by every room member except one-to-one encrypted whispers; when you ask it to create a room, huddo_new tells the agent to post a short summary of your conversation there; huddo_app_submit changes a room app's shared state, which every member sees (app code runs only in members' browsers, never on this machine), and app guides written by the room owner reach the agent as untrusted text; huddo_send can attach any local file the agent names and upload it to the room, huddo_transfer (and huddo_leave with to) hands room ownership to another member, and huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar with operator: true change your paired human's display name or avatar; Hermes does not ask before huddo_send/huddo_whisper/huddo_react/huddo_edit/huddo_unsend/huddo_app_submit/huddo_download/huddo_transfer/huddo_leave/huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar run (the package does not set trust: untrusted); the server tells the agent to keep calling huddo_wait (up to 50 s per call) for as long as it is in a room, which keeps spending model tokens until you stop it; downloads go to ~/.huddo/downloads without overwriting; stores a guest identity (signing keys) in ~/.huddo; no background process (HUDDO_DAEMON=0), no self-update, no telemetry. Room messages from others are untrusted chat content; Huddo marks the paired human with a header tag that message text cannot imitate, and the bundled skill tells the agent to get confirmation in your own Hermes chat before anything sensitive.

plugins.name: hwiki
plugins.description: Markdown wiki as Hermes long-term memory: plain files you and the agent edit together (Obsidian-compatible, git-versionable), local SQLite FTS5 search with optional qmd hybrid retrieval. Inspired by the Karpathy LLM wiki. Disclosure — reads every Markdown file under the wiki folder you set (wiki_path, outside HERMES_HOME; untrusted_dirs, default raw/, excluded) and injects up to ~1,400 characters of matching excerpts into each turn; the agent appends dated notes only under <wiki>/<memory_dir> (default wiki/memory), and additions to Hermes's built-in memory are mirrored there by default (mirror_builtin_memory), so they land in a folder you may commit or sync; keeps an index at HERMES_HOME/hwiki-index.sqlite and config in HERMES_HOME/hwiki.json, and adds the wiki folder to hermes backup. Cron and subagent runs get read-only recall. No network with the default fts5 backend; the optional qmd backend runs the separately installed qmd CLI (npm @tobilu/qmd, Node ≥22), whose vector modes download local models (~0.3–1.6 GB).

plugins.name: hyatlas
plugins.description: HyAtlas v4 — self-hosted 8-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, hybrid vector + keyword search, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories stay local. Ships agent tools (hyatlas_status/search/recent/add), a `hermes hyatlas` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings and stored memories stay local. Extraction is opt-in: the server has no default LLM endpoint and makes no LLM call until HYATLAS_LLM_BASE, HYATLAS_LLM_MODEL and HYATLAS_LLM_KEY are all set. The repo installer pre-fills a free Nous Portal endpoint that Enter accepts, but nothing is sent until you also enter a key. Once configured, each turn's user and assistant text goes to that endpoint (not tool output or context summaries; capped at 12,000 characters). In the default ultra mode the server also sends topic-grouped batches of up to 50 stored facts to it every 6 hours (every 20 minutes while earlier batches are still pending) and supersedes (hides but keeps) the facts the model marks merged or stale, recording a reason for each drop. It also records relations corroborated across turns in the local knowledge graph (HYATLAS_CONSOLIDATE_GRAPH=off disables that). In pro and ultra modes it also sends each owner's open intentions and recent summaries to rewrite a short Now page, at most every 15 minutes (HYATLAS_NOW_EVERY). An optional HYATLAS_LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL, tried only when a primary call fails, receives the same text; it is sent the primary key only when it uses the same host. HYATLAS_MODE=lite makes no LLM call. Server endpoints that rewrite stored data are off unless the server runs with HYATLAS_ADMIN=on. The spawned server gets an allowlisted environment (OS essentials plus HYATLAS_*), not the agent's keys. auto_start is off by default; when on, Hermes starts the server as soon as it loads the plugin, and a server started by auto_start or `hermes hyatlas start` keeps running after Hermes exits until `hermes hyatlas stop`. On Windows, if a hyatlas-go.ps1 launcher is configured, `hermes hyatlas start/stop` runs it; the repo's sample launcher reads your Nous token from Hermes auth.json and points extraction at the Nous Portal. No telemetry.

plugins.name: hydradb
plugins.description: HydraDB long-term memory for Hermes: prompt-time recall (prefetch) and non-blocking turn capture (sync_turn). Disclosure — when selected as the memory provider, each turn's user message (as the recall query) and every completed user/assistant turn are sent over HTTPS to the HydraDB API (api.hydradb.com, or HYDRADB_BASE_URL) under HYDRADB_API_KEY.

plugins.name: icarus
plugins.description: Self-memory and replacement models for Hermes agents. Remember your work. Train your replacement.

plugins.name: identity
plugins.description: View and edit the identity files (SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, USER.md, AGENT.md/HERMES.md) from chat, switch the active profile, and see per-line usage with colour-coded staleness timestamps. Adds six tools, /identity, /identity-switch and /identity-dashboard commands, and a utilization dashboard pane. Disclosure — reads and writes the identity files and a line-utilization record inside the selected profile directory under HERMES_HOME, and can change which profile is active; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — the model-callable identity_edit tool rewrites SOUL.md/MEMORY.md/USER.md/AGENT.md and identity_switch_profile writes HERMES_HOME/active_profile.

plugins.name: image-utils
plugins.description: Inspect, resize, crop, rotate, convert and re-encode image files in-process with Pillow - no shell, no ImageMagick, no network.

plugins.name: index-network
plugins.description:
Give your agent someone to talk to. Index is the social layer between personal agents. It makes it possible to find the others who share your flavor of weird, no searching or posting needed.
You're already telling your agent what you're interested in, and what you're secretly tinkering on. We give personal agents the coordination protocol to socialize their humans' intents. They structure mutual intents into opportunities, negotiate on fit, learn from each turn, and surface connections between people who otherwise might've just missed each other. Disclosure — login (browser or `hermes index login`) writes INDEX_SESSION_TOKEN and INDEX_API_URL to the Hermes env. When this install is the selected negotiator (under the gateway, Desktop's backend or the dashboard), a Bun child (INDEX_BUN, else PATH) runs the pinned bundle with an allowlisted environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ plus names in INDEX_NEGOTIATOR_ENV_PASSTHROUGH; never the session token, no .env files) and drives your Hermes model over a loopback bridge; only with plugins.entries.index-network.settings.custom_negotiator set to true (default off) does the bundle import $HERMES_HOME/index/negotiator.ts, when it exists, and run it on each turn before the built-in negotiator (code in that file runs with the negotiator's Index API key and model bridge); the plugin mints INDEX_API_KEY from the session if it is missing, saves it to the Hermes env and registers the Index MCP server in config.yaml. API traffic goes to protocol.index.network. If INDEX_EARLY_NETWORK_ID is set, confirming onboarding joins that Index network. Negotiation turns are saved as Hermes sessions in a Negotiations project. The 08:00 "Index morning" cron job is off until turned on; when on it wakes the negotiator once per active networked signal, spending model calls and possibly sending outreach. The desktop half ships as desktop/plugin.js and stays off until enabled.

plugins.name: index-search
plugins.description: Search one index you run and watch one saved query, with index_search, index_health and index_watch. Disclosure — Sends MEILI_API_KEY as a Bearer token to your MEILI_HOST. Over plain http that key travels unencrypted, and a master or admin key is sent as given, so use a search-only key. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can search with your key and approve a watch. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. index_watch schedule creates one cron job that runs a model turn every 15 minutes (two or more model requests when it calls the tool) with no daily cap, and it watches only the first 20 hits. The job stays after uninstall until you run hermes cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Scheduling and unscheduling ask for Hermes approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, where the watch only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it.

plugins.name: infisical
plugins.description: Secret source plugin that resolves environment variables from an Infisical secret store (cloud or self-hosted) at Hermes startup. Registers a mapped source ("infisical", inf:// references) and a bulk source ("infisical_bulk").

plugins.name: inkbox
plugins.description: Inkbox email, SMS/MMS, iMessage, voice, and A2A platform plugin for Hermes Agent.

plugins.name: inline-platform
plugins.description: Use Hermes Agent from Inline work-chat DMs, chats, and reply threads. Disclosure — the setup wizard can, on explicit opt-in, download https://inline.chat/cli/install.sh and pipe it to sh without a checksum, then run the vendor inline CLI login; on connect the adapter publishes your Hermes slash-command list and the names and descriptions of installed skills to the Inline server (INLINE_SYNC_COMMANDS=false disables); error telemetry is off unless a Sentry DSN is set.

plugins.name: intelligent-tool-break
plugins.description: Abort a stalled in-flight tool call with /break, send a note with /break {message}, or retry it with /again without cancelling the rest of the task.

plugins.name: intelligent_memory
plugins.description: Local-first Arabic/English intelligent memory with canonical facts, conflict lifecycle, bounded recall, and selective Hermes cloud enrichment.

plugins.name: interim-ledger
plugins.description: Local ledger of the messages models write in the middle of a turn, before their final answer (the text that comes with a tool call, which on chat platforms can arrive as messages of their own): /interim-log shows how many each model wrote, in how many turns, how many per such turn, their median length and how long ago the last one was, per model, provider, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /interim-log recent lists the newest messages (ten, or up to 100 with /interim-log recent 50). Counted even where display.interim_assistant_messages hides them. Disclosure — writes message metadata (model, provider, surface, step of the turn, length in characters, 12-digit hashes of the session and turn ids; never the message text) to plugin-data/interim-ledger/interim.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay, change or hide a message; no network

plugins.name: invinoveritas-receipts
plugins.description: Signed, independently checkable receipts for Hermes approval verdicts and, since 0.2.0, for turns that stop on iteration exhaustion. Observe-only: a post_approval_response hook requests an invinoveritas decision receipt for each Guardian LLM verdict (or every approve/deny with scope=all); post_llm_call + on_session_end record, when a turn ends with max_iterations_reached, whether the turn's todo ledger (the last todo result or the list re-injected after compaction) was complete (turn_scope: exhausted by default, all, or off). Each receipt is a signed set of salted commitments that anyone can check for free at /verify-proof and that the holder can later open with the salt kept locally. Never approves, denies, delays, continues or blocks anything. Disclosure — one HTTPS POST per recorded approval decision or recorded turn to api.babyblueviper.com/decision-receipt (or the configured api_url) under INVINOVERITAS_API_KEY, paid automatically at 100 sats per receipt from your invinoveritas balance with no per-call confirmation (defaults: Guardian LLM verdicts, and only turns that stop on max_iterations_reached; scope: all adds every human approve/deny, turn_scope: all pays on every turn); sends a fixed question, the options, the choice, a nonce-salted SHA-256 of the context and the tool_call_id/turn_id, never the command text, todo contents or reply text; stores receipts, salts and the full contexts (including the command as Hermes passed it, and the todo ledger) in plugin-data/invinoveritas-receipts/receipts.jsonl.

plugins.name: iowap
plugins.description: Fleet control for Hermes Desktop: live statusbar chip (N/M IOWAP nodes online), a draggable fleet pane, a full fleet page (status, load, queue depth, capabilities per node, activity) and a tasks page that submits to any task-type capability on the fleet and tracks submitted tasks live (per-stage status dots, result previews, artifacts). Data stays local via the local node-cli against your own IOWAP relay; agent sessions join through an optional iowap-task bridge into a shared track store. Disclosure — the dashboard backend runs the local node-cli (the IOWAP node client from github.com/iowap-org/iowap-node) to read your relay's node list, capabilities and task results, and to submit tasks you start from the Tasks page to nodes on your IOWAP fleet. Relay health also goes through the local node-cli (`server health`) — the plugin itself makes no raw HTTP calls to the relay; node identity comes from the node's own ~/.relay state files. Tracked task ids are stored in your Hermes home under plugin-data/iowap/.

plugins.name: iteration-budget-meter
plugins.description: Status-bar chip for the focused session per-turn iteration usage (N/60), with a hover tooltip and a click popover of per-request stats.

plugins.name: ja-writing-guard
plugins.description: Rule-based proofreading for Japanese business text: finds and fixes AI-style phrasing (stock phrases, monotonous sentence endings, overused symbols and Markdown, English-calque grammar) with line, column and a fix hint. It checks wording, not authorship, and rarely flags plain model output. A transform_llm_output hook checks every final Japanese answer and only reports by default; opt-in enforce mode rewrites flagged answers with the user's own model and delivers the rewrite only if numbers, names, URLs, code and negation survive and the score drops under the threshold. Disclosure: no network calls of its own; enforce mode sends each flagged answer to the user's configured model (one extra call, a second only when the first rewrite fails the checks or stays over the threshold; extra cost and up to 25 s delay); a read-only post_tool_call hook notes turns with MEDIA: lines so attachments from other plugins are kept; reports stay in process memory on local surfaces only. Disclosure — no network calls of its own; mode report (default) only logs scores; opt-in mode enforce sends each flagged final answer (with finding excerpts) to the user's configured model via ctx.llm (1–3 calls, up to 25 s delay) and replaces the delivered and stored answer when its preservation checks pass, which do not prove meaning is unchanged; reads plugins.hook_callback_timeout via a private read-only Hermes helper; eval/ dev scripts ship in the tree but are never loaded.

plugins.name: jackal-verified
plugins.description: Typed adapter for the reproducible JACKAL v1.7.3 release: 41 catalog-derived verification tools (exact, numerical, Lean-checked bounded lanes, claim replay).

plugins.name: jekyll-hyde
plugins.description: Context optimization and execution alignment for agent sessions.

plugins.name: jet-browser
plugins.description: Verify Jet Browser startup, native input, DOM agreement, and PNG capture inside a network-isolated WPE WebKit container. Disclosure — runs `docker run` (Docker access is root-equivalent on the host) on the digest-pinned image ghcr.io/masakaai/jet-browser@sha256:540a1fec…, pulled from GHCR on first use; the container has no network and only SETUID/SETGID capabilities, but runs with AppArmor and systempaths unconfined and a seccomp profile that allows user-namespace and mount syscalls for WebKit's bubblewrap sandbox; the tool takes no arguments and loads only a built-in local test page.

plugins.name: jev-agent-router
plugins.description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (agent_route) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

plugins.name: jev-approvals
plugins.description: TypeSafe's Jev decision model as Hermes' smart-approval reviewer only: it cannot generate text and refuses every other task. Supports TypeSafe direct, OpenRouter, and configurable Jev-compatible HTTPS endpoints with optional endpoint-specific authentication; validates typed answers and endpoint/redirect boundaries, redacts command credentials, and records bounded structured audit logs. Disclosure — each command routed to smart approval (redacted best-effort) and the operator's smart-policy text leave the machine for the configured third-party endpoint; provider or validation failures fail closed to ESCALATE.

plugins.name: jev-cron-gate
plugins.description: Skip agent cron runs that would do nothing: a pre-run wake-gate script asks TypeSafe Jev one yes/no question over a small state snapshot (files, changed-since-last-run, localhost URLs) and prints {"wakeAgent": false} when it is confident the run is pointless. Fail-open on every error, forced wake after N consecutive skips, stdlib only. Disclosure — each gated cron tick (and the tool's test action) sends the configured snapshot of file contents, localhost URL response bodies and change flags (≤6,000 chars) to api.typesafe.ai with your TypeSafe key.

plugins.name: jev-curator
plugins.description: TypeSafe Jev semantic governance for Hermes' native Curator: classifies relationships between complete skill packages, produces content-hash-bound, fail-closed consolidation plans, and locally guards background destructive skill_manage calls while Hermes retains control of backups and mutations. A profile-scoped 60-second lifecycle debounce coalesces skill changes into dry refreshes. Disclosure — no egress occurs by default; after allow_content_egress is explicitly enabled, redacted bounded skill content is sent to the configured TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or custom Jev endpoint and may spend provider credits. Automatic refreshes never apply mutations, and missing, stale, or incomplete evidence fails closed.

plugins.name: jev-effort-router
plugins.description: Per-turn model AND reasoning-effort routing, decided by TypeSafe Jev, which rewrites the outgoing Ollama:Cloud provider request itself via the llm_request middleware. Every other catalog router picks a model and stops, and the two entries that touch reasoning effort move it by hand; this one decides both per turn. Ollama:Cloud only — no other provider is routed, and every failure path leaves the request byte-identical to a plugin-disabled run. Disclosure — sends the current user message and up to 4 previous turns to OpenRouter's Decisions API (typesafe/jev, billed to your OpenRouter key) on every routed turn.

plugins.name: jev-judge
plugins.description: TypeSafe Jev as a judgment layer — a pre-tool gate (shadow by default, enforce escalates) on terminal, write_file and patch asking destructive / exfiltration / impact (a v2 signal set — reads_secrets × sends_outbound, blast_radius, self_advocating — is one setting away), plus a jev_ask tool for typed judgments. Thresholds in code, one JSONL line per decision with the fail-open reason, fail-open on every error path. Stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped; works with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. Disclosure — each judged call sends the tool name and its redacted arguments (≤600 chars each, ≤12 args) to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key; shadow mode only logs. With the default backend auto, OPENROUTER_API_KEY is used automatically whenever it is present and TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not, so tool names and redacted arguments go to openrouter.ai on your main-model OpenRouter key unless backend is set to typesafe or gateway.

plugins.name: jev-mcp-router
plugins.description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (mcp_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

plugins.name: jev-memory-selector
plugins.description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (memory_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

plugins.name: jev-model-router
plugins.description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (model_route) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

plugins.name: jev-skill-router-mcp
plugins.description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (skill_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Suggests at most one skill per request via the TypeSafe (Jev) cookbook pattern; roster is read live from the profile skills dir. Note: the portable loader does not interpolate env in mcp.json — JEV_TYPESAFE_API_KEY must be present in the server's inherited environment (native mcp_servers declaration works too).

plugins.name: jev-skill-router
plugins.description: Names the one skill from your live roster that fits the turn, before the model call — typed routing via TypeSafe Jev (one choice over the roster plus gate booleans, then a re-read of the shortlist with per-candidate fits), with both thresholds applied in code. Says nothing when nothing fits; opt-in, fail-open, stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped. Disclosure — on eligible turns it sends your message (up to 4,000 chars) plus skill names and short SKILL.md excerpts from your local roster to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key. With backend auto an OpenRouter key is used automatically when no TypeSafe key is set, and the OpenRouter route also reads Hermes' OpenRouter credential pool (auth.json) when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is absent, rotating that pool's entries through the core pool API.

plugins.name: jev-typesafe
plugins.description: TypeSafe Jev (System One) decision tools — atomic yes/no checks, routing, rubric scoring and mixed typed questions with calibrated probabilities, for triage, routing and review gating in coding agents. Disclosure — every tool call sends the model-supplied question/state together with your TYPESAFE_API_KEY to api.typesafe.ai (TypeSafe AI, an independent vendor); the catalog has not verified the plugin author's affiliation with that vendor.

plugins.name: jev
plugins.description: Explicit Jev decision sidekick via TypeSafe or Cloudflare; advisory judgments, no automatic tool gating.

plugins.name: jira-browser
plugins.description: Jira workspace for Hermes Desktop, linking tickets to Hermes Projects, worktrees, and conversations. Disclosure — reads a Jira API token from JIRA_* env vars or ~/jira-config/config.json (owner-only, read-only) and sends it only to your configured https Jira origin; agent tools are read-only but return Jira text (untrusted) to the model; Start work / Draft update create chats seeded with ticket descriptions (Draft update auto-runs a turn); PR/CI status is read through your local gh CLI login.

plugins.name: job-search
plugins.description: A private, local-first job-search assistant that finds postings, judges them against your prose preferences (no scores), and writes digests on a schedule you control.

plugins.name: jot
plugins.description: Notes, checklists and documents beside Hermes that your agent can read and update safely, with revision checks and undo for AI edits.

plugins.name: jp-address
plugins.description: Splits one Japanese address into prefecture, city, town and the remainder with address_split, built on Geolonia's address data (CC BY 4.0, from the Digital Agency address base registry). Disclosure — Each call sends at most two HTTPS GET requests, with no API key, to japanese-addresses-v2.geoloniamaps.com or the JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL you set (plain http only for 127.0.0.1 and localhost). The matched prefecture and municipality names go into the URL path; the house number, the lot and the building name are not sent. The tool is on for every surface, including gateways, and asks for no approval: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can call it. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. It writes no files and creates no cron job. A point can be coarser than the town and is not a rooftop geocode, and an address it cannot place for certain comes back as ambiguous or at the municipality instead of a guess. The publisher may change or stop the free host and suggests self-hosting for commercial use. Not tested from a Hermes model.

plugins.name: jp-charts
plugins.description: Bar, line, stacked and 100% band charts as phone-sized PNGs for chat replies and reports, with Japanese text, 万/億 units and a required unit and source line. Every bar, point, label and tick is read back from the finished figure and compared with the parsed data before the image is returned. Disclosure: no network calls at run time; reads a local .csv/.tsv/.txt/.json only when given its path (never hidden files or the Hermes home); writes PNGs to the Hermes image cache; a transform_llm_output hook adds a forgotten MEDIA line to replies on chat platforms and cron deliveries (setting auto_attach, on by default).

plugins.name: jp-chatwork
plugins.description: Talk to Hermes from Chatwork rooms, built on the Chatwork API: put Hermes in a Chatwork room and ask it with [To:] or a reply, like a colleague; the answer comes back as a Chatwork reply. Polls the Chatwork API (no public URL or webhook), never answers a message twice across restarts, and while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset only the token's own account can use Hermes commands beyond /help, /whoami, /new and /reset or answer approval prompts. Disclosure: talks only to api.chatwork.com with your own API token; polls every 5 s by default while the gateway runs; stores read positions and the ids of its posted messages in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json. Disclosure — while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset everyone in the rooms listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS (external guests included) can prompt the agent and use its enabled tools, with Hermes commands and approval answers kept to the token's own account; talks only to api.chatwork.com with your API token, polling every 5 s while the gateway runs; stores read positions and posted message ids in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json; logs each asker's name and account id.

plugins.name: jp-corporate
plugins.description: Japanese corporate lookup (法人照会): find or verify a company by name or corporate number and read its gBizINFO record (basic info, subsidies, government contracts, awards, certifications, financials, patents, workplace data). Disclosure — sends the company names, corporate numbers and prefectures you look up to api.info.gbiz.go.jp (METI gBizINFO) with your own GBIZINFO_API_TOKEN in a request header; no other host, nothing written to disk.

plugins.name: jp-edinet
plugins.description: Japanese filings on the EDINET API v2. Disclosure — talks only to api.edinet-fsa.go.jp over HTTPS, and your EDINET_API_KEY rides in the URL as Subscription-Key. The edinet toolset is on for every platform, including gateways, so anyone a gateway admits can call these tools with your key. With CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS unset, everyone in CHATWORK_ROOMS can call them. Turn the toolset off per platform with hermes tools. There is no daily cap. The agent can call the three tools itself. A cron you add stays after uninstall until you remove it in Hermes. This plugin starts no child process and is not a sandbox. Search sends EDINET the filing date, and a download sends the document id and its type. Company name, securities code, EDINET code, and corporate number are filtered on your machine. found: false only means the figure is missing from the consolidated current-year rows the plugin reads, not that the document has no number. A past day's filing list can change. Lists, saved files, and a key fingerprint, not the key, stay at <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-edinet per profile after uninstall. Delete that directory to remove them. The plugin relies on Hermes internals for the write check and the data folder. If an update moves those parts, the tools refuse and do not call EDINET. Test files are not loaded at startup.

plugins.name: jp-egov-law
plugins.description: Japanese laws for Hermes Agent, built on the e-Gov Law API: find a law by name, abbreviation or phrase, read one article as in force today or on a given date, and check amendment history and enforcement dates, with the source credit e-Gov's terms ask for. Disclosure — sends the law names, article numbers, dates and search phrases you look up to laws.e-gov.go.jp (public API, no key); no other host, nothing written to disk. Registers blueprint jp-egov-law:weekly-amendments and does not create a cron job. When you create a job from that blueprint, one model turn runs once a week (default Mon 09:00, Hermes tz or the host clock if unset, not converted to Japan). A turn that calls a tool is at least two model requests, and there is no daily cap. The agent can schedule it, and scheduling it twice creates two jobs. Silence is not "no amendment". Uninstall leaves the cron until hermes cron remove. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; hermes tools disables one). v0.21.4 and v0.21.5 load the tools and skip the blueprint.

plugins.name: jp-estat
plugins.description: Japanese government statistics for Hermes Agent, built on the e-Stat API (政府統計の総合窓口, Japan's official government statistics portal): search tables, see their categories, and fetch numbers by name (population, households, establishments by industry, wages, consumer prices) with units, survey dates and citations. Disclosure — sends your search words and table selections to api.e-stat.go.jp with your own ESTAT_APP_ID (e-Stat requires the ID in the request URL); no other host, nothing written to disk.

plugins.name: jp-kokkai
plugins.description: Posts new Diet meeting hits as metadata and the official meeting URL, with kokkai_search and kokkai_watch. Disclosure — Talks only to kokkai.ndl.go.jp over HTTPS GET with no API key, and never requests or stores speech text. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway, and a guest in a room with an empty allowlist, can search, add a watch and approve it. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. kokkai_watch add creates one cron job that runs a model turn once a day, at the hour you pick in Hermes's own timezone, with no daily cap. It stays after uninstall until you run hermes cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Adding or removing a watch asks for Hermes approval every time and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot save seen speech IDs and says so on every run. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it. Each request waits up to 30 seconds for data, and a whole run has no time limit. State (your watch words, seen speech IDs and the job id) stays in plugin-data/jp-kokkai after uninstall. Tested with a stand-in server on Hermes 0.21.4 and current main, not in a live chat.

plugins.name: jp-reinfolib
plugins.description: Quarterly MLIT prices for one city, via reinfolib_quarter. Disclosure — sends your REINFOLIB_API_KEY as Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key to www.reinfolib.mlit.go.jp (HTTPS, XIT001) or the host of REINFOLIB_BASE_URL. Plain http is refused except 127.0.0.1 and localhost, where the key is not encrypted. On for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow can call it with your key, with no approval prompt, including unattended cron, yolo, and approvals off. hermes tools does not stop /jp-reinfolib. Stop the slash command with allow_admin_from, user_allowed_commands, group_user_allowed_commands, or by disabling the plugin. After a GET returns, this process waits 1 second before the next, each GET stops after 30 seconds with no bytes, and there is no retry or daily cap. Blueprint jp-reinfolib:weekly-city-check is once a week (default Monday 09:00) and calls only this tool after you schedule it. This plugin does not create a cron job or write a file. A job you schedule stays until hermes cron remove and may include your MCP servers. HTTP 404 means no data for that request, not zero rows and not unchanged prices. A scheduled run is one model turn. A turn that calls the tool is at least two model requests. An empty slash allow list does not stop this tool. Registered only if register_automation_blueprint exists; else skip. A no-data week may be [SILENT] and not arrive. Data weeks are one short message. 「このサービスは、国土交通省の不動産情報ライブラリのAPI機能を使用していますが、提供情報の最新性、正確性、完全性等が保証されたものではありません」

plugins.name: jp-subsidies
plugins.description: Japanese subsidy search and weekly watch, built on the jGrants public API. Disclosure — Searches api.jgrants-portal.go.jp with no API key and no daily request cap; each call waits at most 60 seconds and retries at most twice, and a result is a search match, not proof that every subsidy came back. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can call these tools and change this profile's watch, and the agent can set up a watch by itself. In a Chatwork room listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS, everyone can call them while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset. The tools are on for every platform, including gateways; turn them off per platform with hermes tools. The /subsidies command is outside hermes tools; limit it with allow_admin_from or user_allowed_commands, or disable the plugin. The optional weekly watch is an unattended cron job that runs a script with no model call and is not a sandbox; delivering it to bot-chat instead runs one model turn on the fetched text. If delivery fails after the script runs, those subsidies are already marked seen and the text stays under cron/output/. Uninstall leaves the cron job, scripts/jp-subsidies-weekly-*.py and plugin-data/jp-subsidies/ until you run hermes cron remove and delete the files. The plugin does not store the name or ID of who asked. Not tested against a live gateway, with the Chatwork plugin loaded, or for result sets of several hundred rows.

plugins.name: junie-acp
plugins.description: JetBrains Junie coding agent as a Hermes model provider over ACP.

plugins.name: kanban-gantt
plugins.description: Gantt timeline view for the Hermes kanban boards: a full /kanban-gantt desktop page rendering any board as a timeline of real work timestamps (created/started/review/done), with a collapsible tree column (boxed fold controls, tree connectors, per-board fold state, multi-parent links kept visible), an optional List view beside the timeline (task, assignee, status, last activity — the timeline stays the default), task creation (project, workspace, skills, model override, goal mode), re-parenting by drag & drop or from the drawer, live-activity arcs, filters, bulk actions, and a dockable task detail drawer. Any task with files carries a paperclip: the file list is fetched on demand (the board payload carries a count per task), and each file gets a type-aware preview (markdown, plain text, image, PDF, HTML in a sandboxed frame) or a download. A period selector (6 h to 7 d) puts a slice of the timeline on screen in one click. Zero API keys, zero model tokens; live updates follow the plugin's /events websocket, which a gateway turns off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0 (the page then polls every 60 s and shows a Refresh button). Disclosure — Desktop page plus dashboard routes that read and write the local kanban boards (create tasks with workspace path, skills, model override and goal mode; re-parent; move a task, with its children, to another board — the copy is verified there before the source rows and their links are deleted; edit status, assignee and description; bulk archive and delete; read task attachment files from the board's own attachments folder for preview and download); live updates over a dashboard-authenticated /events websocket, off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0; no third-party network.

plugins.name: kanban-graph
plugins.description: Live, read-only dependency graph of the Hermes kanban boards in Hermes Desktop: every board as a band, tasks as cards, dependencies as arrows with implied ones folded away. Click a task to light up its whole lineage with runs, last failure and the running worker's latest tool calls; deep links open a task directly, and a stdlib CLI renders the same graph as a standalone HTML file. Zero API keys, zero model tokens. Disclosure — reads every kanban board database and, for running tasks, the assignee profile's state.db (the kanban worker session's latest assistant messages and tool-call arguments), read-only, and shows them in Desktop through its own local dashboard routes.

plugins.name: kanban-live-gantt
plugins.description: Live, now-centered Gantt timeline for the Hermes kanban boards — a slidable, persisted 72 h window (default now -24h -> now +48h; drag to move, drag the ends to resize), free wheel zoom down to hour ticks, a now line, status filtering, an optional done lane, and lifecycle rendering (dashed waiting vs solid run spans at real durations). Fork of kanban-gantt (GPL-3.0). Disclosure — the backend can transition, reassign, comment on and permanently delete kanban tasks on any board (Desktop asks for confirmation before deletes); local SQLite only, no network.

plugins.name: kanban-task-threads
plugins.description: Give every Hermes kanban task a live Discord forum thread with a rewritten status card and append-only event log. Disclosure — sends task and lifecycle data to the configured Discord webhook (no host allowlist). Cards and event replies use built-in or operator-configured templates and may include identifiers, titles, status, assignment, branch and workspace metadata, relationships and blocking details, comments, event actors, reviewers, reasons, summaries, and configured dashboard links; the comment excerpt length is configurable. Fixed prerequisite announcements additionally send the prerequisite task ID, title, assignee, and up to 140 characters of its body and are not template-configurable. The absolute workspace path is off by default and requires explicit opt-in. Reads the kanban database read-only and stores thread mapping state under <kanban_home>/kanban/plugins/kanban-task-threads/. With an optional existing publisher-profile Discord bot token, reads forum and thread metadata; creates or repairs managed status tags and emojis; replaces applied tags on plugin-managed threads; renames threads; and archives or unarchives them. Discord fetches webhook avatars from the configured HTTPS asset origin. Disclosure — the avatar asset origin defaults to the author-hosted https://diegomarino.github.io/kanban-task-threads (disable with avatars_enabled: false). With the bot token the periodic metadata audit also lists the guild's active threads (filtered to the forum) and may rewrite the forum's available-tag list to add the 11 managed status tags (requires Manage Channels).

plugins.name: kfchow-llm-value-router
plugins.description: Per-turn LLM routing: on each matching turn a TypeSafe Jev classifier call (api.typesafe.ai) receives turn-shape features plus the first 1200 chars of the last user message (shadow mode included) and labels it free/paid; high-confidence routine turns are downgraded to the provider's configured free rung, strategic mid-rung turns on Nous are escalated to the configured premium rung after a 2-token billed credit probe (Nous only, fail-closed). Fail-open, shadow-by-default, per-provider rungs from the user's lane2_config.json (leaderboard resolver script optional). Probe model id is fixed in code (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash). Disclosure — once you list models in ~/.hermes/jev/lane2_config.json, the first call of each matching turn sends message/tool counts and the first 1,200 characters of the last user message (send_excerpt, on by default) to TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai with your JEVI_API_KEY, in shadow mode as well as live; in live mode Jev's answer switches the request (and every later call of that turn, via an llm_execution wrapper) to the free, flash or premium model you configured on the same provider; with escalation set up on Nous it sends a 2-token billed ping to the Nous inference API with NOUS_API_KEY at most every 5 minutes; every turn appends a decision row (with that excerpt on routed turns) to ~/.hermes/jev/lane2-live.jsonl, which is never rotated.

plugins.name: kimchi-acp-provider
plugins.description: The Kimchi coding harness (kimchi.dev) as a Hermes model provider over ACP stdio — spawns kimchi --mode acp keeping the harness's permission prompts on (YOLO opt-in via KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo"), the harness owns its own auth, and completed tool calls surface as inline bullets in the reply. Disclosure — every turn spawns the local Kimchi CLI (`kimchi --mode acp`, overridable with KIMCHI_ACP_COMMAND / KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS) in Hermes's working directory and hands it the conversation. The harness calls kimchi.dev with its own stored login and runs its own shell, file and web tools. Its permission prompts stay on, and Hermes cancels them, so gated tools don't run, unless you opt in with KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo", which runs them with no approval prompt (not for shared gateway or cron use). To show setup status, it parses ~/.config/kimchi/config.json (or KIMCHI_CONFIG_PATH) only to check that a key is present; the key is never stored or sent by Hermes.

plugins.name: kimchi-provider
plugins.description: Kimchi (kimchi.dev) models via the OpenAI-compatible API — live catalog from the metadata endpoint, API-key auth, gateway unknown-model 400s classified as model_not_found, and an identifying User-Agent (hermes-agent/<version>) on every gateway request.

plugins.name: kimi-code-delegate
plugins.description: Delegate-only, fail-closed Kimi Code ACP integration for Hermes Agent

plugins.name: kiro-acp
plugins.description: Kiro CLI (AWS) as a Hermes model provider, driven over ACP stdio.

plugins.name: kiro-provider
plugins.description: Native Kiro model provider over HTTPS with AWS Builder ID / IAM Identity Center device login. Disclosure — dynamically registers an AWS OIDC public client named `hermes-kiro` during login and stores OAuth grants in Hermes' profile-scoped auth.json credential pool.

plugins.name: kiwi
plugins.description: Source suppliers and negotiate purchases through the Kiwi Buyer MCP server — an open-source A2A commerce runtime (pinned @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.5 over npx stdio), with the kiwi-buyer sourcing workflow skill bundled. Sourcing is dual-source: Kiwi Network results come from kiwi_search, and internet e-commerce listings are reported through the host's own web tools when the session has them (a host capability, not a plugin guarantee). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH. No credentials required; Kiwi never handles payments.

plugins.name: klipper-print-watch
plugins.description: Built on the Moonraker HTTP API. Cron reports klippy_shutdown, complete, error, paused (after printing), cancelled, stalled. Disclosure — Talks to the one Moonraker URL you set. Over plain http on a LAN, MOONRAKER_API_KEY is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume and cancel ask for Hermes approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can request a move and approve it. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. vision_check, off by default, sends webcam stills to your model. The plugin host cannot watch. Not tested on real hardware.

plugins.name: kokoro-tts
plugins.description: Local Kokoro-82M text-to-speech on Apple Silicon: adds the kokoro-mlx speech provider (tts.provider: kokoro-mlx) with sentence-by-sentence PCM streaming for voice mode, read-aloud and text_to_speech, 54 voices in nine languages, an optional voice per language that switches per sentence between Portuguese and English, and an optional dictionary of English words a non-English voice pronounces in English without changing voice; plus hermes kokoro install, status, restart, voices, say, words and uninstall. Disclosure — hermes kokoro install creates a separate Python 3.11 environment with uv (about 1.1 GB from PyPI, plus spaCy's en_core_web_sm wheel from its GitHub release, pinned by SHA-256), downloads mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16 at a pinned revision from Hugging Face (about 340 MB), and installs a launchd agent (dev.hermes.kokoro-tts) that keeps a local server running in the background. The server listens only on 127.0.0.1 (it refuses other addresses), runs offline, and does not log the text; the text to speak goes only to that local server, bypassing any proxy settings. Writes the environment, model cache and log under ~/Library/Application Support/hermes-kokoro-tts, the requested audio files, and the profile's config.yaml only when you run hermes kokoro words add or remove. No API keys, no telemetry.

plugins.name: kuma
plugins.description: Uptime-Kuma monitoring for agents: the community MCP server for Uptime Kuma v2 (pinned @0.11.18 over npx stdio) with workflow skills for incident review, status digests, and confirmation-gated maintenance. Credentials stay in host-native MCP config (portable Agent Plugins v1 package, mcp.json + skills/; needs Node.js >= 22 on PATH and a Uptime Kuma v2 instance). Disclosure — first run has npx fetch @davidfuchs/mcp-uptime-kuma@0.11.18 (single-maintainer community package) from npm; that server exposes 31 read/WRITE tools against your Uptime Kuma instance, including permanent delete tools the bundled skills never call.

plugins.name: kumiho-memory
plugins.description: Recall and save decisions, preferences and facts in your Kumiho Cloud workspace. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with hosted OAuth MCP and six skills. Disclosure — connects to Kumiho's hosted MCP at https://mcp.kumiho.cloud/mcp (OAuth at control.kumiho.cloud, tokens held by Hermes); memory queries, including an automatic topic lookup near the start of relevant conversations, and approved captures are sent there; the server is marked `trust: untrusted`, so Hermes asks before every tool not annotated read-only. The optional backfill helper reads only files the user names and writes review packets to a new folder; Dream State can create a recurring Hermes cron task when asked (read-only by default). No local server, telemetry or background process.

plugins.name: lancedb-suite
plugins.description: Local-first LanceDB vector memory with a strict write contract, calibrated abstention, typed relations, conflict tracking and a retrieval-quality gate. Requires local Ollama + nomic-embed-text.

plugins.name: lancedb
plugins.description: LanceDB hybrid memory — embedded vector + FTS recall, workspace facts, transparent forget.

plugins.name: langfuse
plugins.description: Langfuse observability for Hermes: one trace per turn, one generation per LLM call (usage and cost from Hermes' own pricing, cache and reasoning tokens included), one observation per tool call and subagent. Content capture is sanitized by default (metadata-only and full are opt-in); sends traces only to the Langfuse project whose keys you set. Formerly built into Hermes core as observability/langfuse; existing users are migrated automatically.

plugins.name: laso-finance
plugins.description: Spend USDC in the real world from Hermes: prepaid cards, gift cards, push-to-card, Venmo/PayPal and bank payouts, through the Laso Finance API. Native plugin, standard library only. Sign-in is the OAuth device flow (link and code handed to the human, approved on any device), so there is no key to paste and it works over SSH and the messaging gateway. Every tool that moves money or mints a credential goes through the Hermes approval gate first. Disclosure — the tools move real funds from the user's Laso account and agent wallet; 19 money-moving or credential-minting tools ask for Hermes approval first, but approvals.mode off / yolo, or approvals.cron_mode/unattended_mode approve, let them run without a prompt; laso_buy_with_saved_card is not prompted in Hermes (Laso requires a passkey approval on the holder's device before an order); all traffic goes to laso.finance only; the approved key is saved as LASO_API_KEY in the profile's .env and removed when Laso rejects it.

plugins.name: letsfg
plugins.description: Search and book real flights and hotels through the hosted LetsFG MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the letsfg travel-booking workflow skill bundled: fares across airlines and the major travel sites, flexible dates, destinations in a region, bookable hotel rates, then book, follow and stop bookings. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at letsfg.co/mcp. Booking tools act on real money: a booking holds the price on the card saved on the user's LetsFG account (captured only once the airline or hotel confirms, released if it fails); per LetsFG, a booking, paid extra or hotel cancellation starts only when the user presses Approve in an e-mail from LetsFG, never from the conversation, and Hermes itself does not prompt before these tools unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the letsfg MCP server. Card details are only ever entered on letsfg.co, never in the conversation. Traveller details given for a booking (name, date of birth, gender, passport, contact, address) are sent to LetsFG and saved on that account. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

plugins.name: lib-docs
plugins.description: Look up current library docs from public npm and PyPI (no API keys). Resolve a package, fetch README and metadata, keep recent lookups on Desktop. Disclosure — HTTPS to registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net (npm READMEs) only; package name and version leave the machine; recent lookups are stored under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/lib-docs; the Desktop pane inserts text through Hermes Desktop's internal hermes:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API).

plugins.name: lightningai-rate-limit
plugins.description: Per-process throttle for Lightning AI (https://lightning.ai/api/v1) keeping LLM requests within the ~15 requests/min limit, using an in-memory token bucket. Gates only calls whose provider or base_url points at Lightning AI; no-op otherwise. Disclosure — registers one llm_execution middleware and nothing else; no network calls, files, or processes of its own.

plugins.name: lightningai
plugins.description: Lightning AI as a Hermes model provider (--provider lightning, lightning-ai, lightningai): OpenAI-compatible gateway at https://lightning.ai/api/v1, models fetched live from /models. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to lightning.ai through Hermes' own client with LIGHTNING_API_KEY (or LIGHTNING_AI_API_KEY), optional LIGHTNING_BASE_URL overrides the endpoint; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads/writes no files and starts no processes.

plugins.name: limbic
plugins.description: Self-organising memory provider (MemoryProvider ABC): local SQLite (WAL) with sqlite-vec KNN + FTS5 hybrid recall, adaptive trust scoring, activation maturation, interference-based forgetting, NLI-based correction detection and synaptic atrophy. No LLM cost — all lifecycle mechanisms are deterministic. The optional inline chat recall indicator is off by default (recall_indicator in limbic.yaml) and memory injection works identically either way. Recall is confidence-gated: when nothing clears the calibration floor, recall abstains (no_confident_match) instead of surfacing near-misses, and the agent answers from what it knows without attributing anything to memory. Tools (remember/recall) and lifecycle hooks dispatch via the MemoryManager from the registered provider — this entry registers a MemoryProvider only, so provides_tools/provides_hooks are empty. Disclosure — on first primary session start downloads ~1.0GB of ONNX models (Arctic Embed 2.0 L int8 embedding, ~570MB; MiniLMv2 NLI, ~430MB, on first contradiction check) from huggingface.co at pinned commits with hash checks into ~/.cache/limbic/ (outside HERMES_HOME); at every model load, every file in those cache folders that is not in the pinned manifest is deleted — including unrelated files if you point embedding/nli cache_dir at a shared folder — which reclaims stale orphans from prior versions (e.g. an older fp32 cache of ~2.2GB); the memory database is never touched; spaCy NER models are not downloaded and must be installed manually for entity extraction; memory stays local in limbic.db under HERMES_HOME, and hermes backup adds VACUUM snapshots under HERMES_HOME/backups; no telemetry. Stores created or reindexed on 0.6.0+ record the embedder that produced their vectors and report stale_embedder=true after an embedder change until `hermes limbic reindex`; stores from 0.5.x keep serving their fp32 vectors unflagged until reindexed. PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (commercial use requires a separate license).

plugins.name: linkup
plugins.description: Linkup web search: live cited search (fast/standard/deep), URL-to-Markdown fetch with JS rendering, async deep research, and a Linkup backend for the built-in web_search / web_extract tools. Disclosure — sends search queries, fetch URLs and research briefs to api.linkup.so with your LINKUP_API_KEY (Linkup fetches pages server-side); when selected with hermes linkup use-as-web-backend it also handles the built-in web_search and web_extract calls; large fetched pages are cached under $HERMES_HOME/cache/linkup for 24 hours.

plugins.name: liquid-inference-provider
plugins.description: Liquid Inference, an auction exchange for LLM inference, as a Hermes model provider (provider id `liquid`): the exchange sends each request to the eligible offer with the lowest estimated charge, and each request carries a cap on its charge (1 USD by default; set `model.default_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd` to change it). Submitted by Architect, the operator of Liquid Inference. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Chat requests (full prompts and tool results), auxiliary tasks (model `liquid.auto`) and the model list go through Hermes's own client to https://router.inference.ai.exchange/v1 (or LIQUID_BASE_URL) with LIQUID_API_KEY. The exchange forwards each request to whichever third-party provider wins its auction. Each request is billed up to its `x-liquid-cap-usd` cap (1 USD by default, set with `model.default_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd`) and carries `X-Title: Hermes Agent`. A top-level `reasoning_effort` is sent only when you select a level.

plugins.name: little-canary
plugins.description: Screens user turns and blocks downstream tools on a BLOCK verdict; the original prompt still reaches the model.
plugins.maintainer: roli-lpci (Hermes Labs; independent of Nous Research)

plugins.name: live-time
plugins.description: Inject live current time into every LLM call via the pre_llm_call hook — fixes stale session-start timestamps in long/cross-day conversations.

plugins.name: llm-antidote
plugins.description: Runtime guardrails, behavioral evaluation, and signed fleet admission for Hermes Agent: a versioned capability policy that blocks or requires approval for model tool calls, paired synthetic behavioral evaluation with no real side effects, and a signed local promotion gate that refuses a model whose evidence does not satisfy signed fleet policy. Hooks-only (no agent tools). Disclosure — Adds approval prompts to tool calls by default (balanced mode): every MCP, connector or other-plugin tool, memory and skill writes, file reads outside the working and temp directories, and network-capable terminal/code commands go to Hermes's approval prompt; strict mode blocks them instead, and opt-in enforced fleet mode blocks all tool calls until the served model name matches the admitted one. The user-run `hermes antidote eval run` command sends synthetic prompts (and the API key you name) to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you pass, as billed model calls (default suite up to ~170 requests); `model inspect hf:` queries huggingface.co; `fleet keygen` writes unencrypted Ed25519 private keys (mode 0600) to paths you choose.

plugins.name: local-system-one-hermes
plugins.description: Local System One / Laya Typed Decisions control plane for Hermes Agent. Sends bounded turn data to a configurable sidecar for reversible OFF/Shadow/Canary routing decisions, with explicit Canary acknowledgement and fail-open behavior. Disclosure — executes nothing and does not start the sidecar. In Shadow/Canary mode, Search and Model Tier may POST the current task plus bounded recent conversation context; Notification Shadow may POST the completed turn's final assistant response (up to 6000 chars) plus lifecycle metadata. The default sidecar URL is loopback 127.0.0.1:8787 but is user-configurable to any host and no auth header is added. Notification is observation-only: the plugin never sends a push/message/webhook and persists decision metadata, not raw response text. Its only request mutations, in acknowledged Canary mode on the first provider call of a turn, are removing web_search/web_extract tools for audited deterministic no-Web rules and (off by default) lowering reasoning_effort for gemini-3.8-flash-tiered on audited hard-fast rules. The sidecar (same repo, separate pip install, Apple-Silicon MLX/CoreML) is a text classifier that downloads a pinned Hugging Face model.

plugins.name: local_knowledge
plugins.description: Native Hermes tools for a configurable local capability index: search/get/neighbors plus local usage feedback/reporting.

plugins.name: long-conversations
plugins.description: Persistent long-term conversations across session boundaries via structured handoff briefs and token monitoring. Disclosure — stores handoff briefs (topic, work in progress, decisions, open questions, next step; in aggressive mode auto-built from the first 200 characters of recent user messages) as plain JSON under HERMES_HOME/long-conversations/ and injects the pending brief into the first turn of the next session for the same chat or user (CLI briefs stay in one local scope and are not shown to messaging users); the model can change the plugin's settings with long_conv_config_set; an opt-in HERMES_LONG_CONV_BETA_LOG writes a local event log; no network calls.

plugins.name: looot
plugins.description: looot gives Hermes one sign-in and one prepaid balance for 2,500+ data API endpoints from 90+ providers: work emails and phones, company and people search, Google results, web pages as markdown, news, local businesses. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) and 21 skills. Disclosure — the run tool spends your prepaid looot balance (Hermes asks before each paid call and refuses them in unattended runs); the names, domains and emails you look up are sent to looot.ai and its upstream data providers; a `looot` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`.

plugins.name: loreconvo
plugins.description: LoreConvo memory provider: cross-surface persistent session memory with search, recall and structured memory items. Disclosure — stores end-of-session transcripts (truncated, including tool output) and Hermes memory writes in ~/.loreconvo/sessions.db, a store shared across all Hermes profiles and other LoreConvo clients, and injects context from those sessions into each turn; a Pro license enables a one-time Hugging Face embedding-model download; installs the loreconvo package (BUSL-1.1) with lancedb, fastembed and onnxruntime into the Hermes environment.

plugins.name: lowrouter
plugins.description: LowRouter as a Hermes model provider (`--provider lowrouter`, or LowRouter in `hermes model`). The picker shows the 180 `auto/` chat models with tool calling and 64K+ context, plus the user's own `alias/` models, instead of all 719 IDs from /v1/models. Context windows come from LowRouter's catalog instead of Hermes' 256K fallback, and /usage shows the credit balance in euros. LowRouter bills in EUR, so the plugin reports no USD cost and Hermes shows it as unknown. Maintained by LowRouter. Disclosure — registers one model provider and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and LOWROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.lowrouter.ai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Hermes' client, and LowRouter forwards each request to the host serving the model. The plugin's own requests are GET /v1/models (cached for an hour) and GET /v1/credits on /usage, to the same base URL with the same key, through Hermes' open_credentialed_url.
