No files read or written, no processes.

plugins.name: lumberroom
plugins.description: lumberroom memory provider. One durable store shared with every agent you use, recalled on every turn and written through the engine's own memory_write. Self-hosted open-source engine or lumberroom.cloud; OAuth or a static token. Maintained by the lumberroom team. Disclosure — when active, every non-trivial user message (first 1,000 characters) and the absolute git-root path of the working directory are sent on each turn to the configured lumberroom engine, which defaults to https://mcp.lumberroom.cloud (operated by Cybersapien Technologies, India) unless base_url names a self-hosted engine; the model is instructed to store decisions, preferences and facts there through memory_write, the engine's live tool descriptions and server instructions are injected into the system prompt each session, and setup switches off Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md store.

plugins.name: machine-library
plugins.description: Research search for web_search and web_extract — papers, books, patents, standards and Wikipedia, with citable source links (Machine Library API key).

plugins.name: machine-spirit
plugins.description: A Warhammer 40k shrine pane docked under the sessions list: the cogitators recite original Adeptus Mechanicus-style litanies, and the cog-skull, candle and binary stream animate while Hermes works. Just for fun. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network or file access.

plugins.name: made-shelf
plugins.description: Everything Hermes made - cross-session shelf of wrote/patched paths. Full Desktop page, chip, pin. No API keys.

plugins.name: magi
plugins.description: Review pending Hermes memory writes and inspect, add, edit, delete, or AI-compact stored memory from Desktop.

plugins.name: make-parts-now
plugins.description: Quote and order custom 3D printed and CNC machined parts from your CAD files through the hosted Make Parts Now MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in to quote), with the quote-parts workflow skill bundled: upload an STL, STEP, 3MF or OBJ file, get the price and ship date for each production speed (SLS nylon, FDM plastic, CNC aluminum and brass), change the quantity, material or speed, and get a checkout link. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to makepartsnow.com. To quote a local file the agent uploads that one CAD file with curl through the terminal tool (Hermes approvals apply) to a one-time upload link, or gives the user an upload page. Nothing is charged in chat: checkout links open Stripe Checkout on makepartsnow.com where the user pays. US shipping only.

plugins.name: maqami-travel
plugins.description: Search hotels (3M+ hotels) and flights worldwide on MAQAMI, read hotel details and reviews, then send the customer a secure checkout link on book.maqami.co, through the official MAQAMI Travel MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.maqami.co, no account or key), with the maqami-travel-booking skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — connects to the hosted MAQAMI MCP server at mcp.maqami.co (no key); its tool list is defined by that server, not by the pinned repo. The tool arguments the agent sends go to it: destinations, dates, guests, lead-guest nationality and currency, plus booking ID and email for lookups, amendments and cancellations. Prebook (hotels) and verify (flights) hold a real rate, and the amend and cancel tools change or cancel real bookings (late or non-refundable cancellations are still charged); the skill tells the agent to show the details and get a clear yes before each prebook, amend or cancel. Customers pay only on book.maqami.co; no tool takes card or passport details.

plugins.name: markdown-new
plugins.description: Search the public web, read pages as Markdown, crawl sites, and convert documents in Hermes. No API key required. Disclosure — search queries, submitted URLs and explicitly approved local file uploads go to the public markdown.new service; needs the companion markdown-new CLI (uv tool install from the same repo tag), which the plugin runs as a subprocess with the Hermes process environment.

plugins.name: markifact
plugins.description: Run Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, GA4, Shopify, HubSpot and 50+ more platforms through Markifact's hosted MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with ten skills (operating protocol, write-safety rules, campaign launch, creative rotation, negative sweeps, diagnosis); remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1 and dynamic client registration, so no Node.js or API keys. Disclosure: creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; every write is a separate approval-gated operation and the skills instruct confirm-before-spend, but that is enforced by the skills and the server's approval flag, not by Hermes.

plugins.name: max-platform
plugins.description: MAX messenger gateway with polling/webhook, streaming, interactive questions, native attachments, Core voice transcription, optional PNG tables and a Desktop sessions sidebar. Disclosure — sends the bot token and message/file content to the MAX Bot API (platform-api2.max.ru) and MAX upload hosts (*.max.ru, *.oneme.ru, *.okcdn.ru). Inbound attachments are downloaded only for allowlisted senders, with SSRF protection, and cached under HERMES_HOME. The bundled Russian Trusted Root CA is trusted only by the MAX API/upload clients, not attachment downloads. Its platform hint lets the agent attach local host files to MAX replies via MEDIA paths, and a public output hook adds a filename caption to file-only MAX replies. Webhook mode opens a listener (default 0.0.0.0:8646) that requires a secret and public HTTPS. Polling startup deletes all of the bot's webhook subscriptions. Optional table rendering launches Playwright/Chromium; with MAX_AUTO_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT=true it pip-installs playwright==1.62.0 and downloads Chromium (~115 MB). The MAX allowlist does not honour Hermes pairing approvals. No telemetry or self-update.

plugins.name: meeting-overlay
plugins.description: Disclosure — sends meeting transcripts to Nous inference with your Hermes login (fallback OpenRouter key from ~/.hermes/.env; optional OCTOPUS_DESK_URL); installs a launchd agent that records mic/system audio; writes and deletes under your Obsidian vault; macOS + source install only. Native desktop pane showing the live meeting transcript, answer, and daemon status.

plugins.name: mem-os
plugins.description: Local-first persistent memory: store durable facts once and recall them in any session. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): the @mem-os/sdk MCP server (pinned 1.6.26) over npx stdio, plus the mem-os-memory skill covering when to store and when to recall. All data stays in a local SQLite database under the user home directory; no cloud, no telemetry, no API keys. Server cwd is ${PLUGIN_DATA} so nothing is written into the install tree. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

plugins.name: mem0
plugins.description: Mem0 memory provider — server-side LLM fact extraction with semantic search, automatic deduplication and opt-in reranking, in platform, self-hosted or local OSS mode. Maintained by Mem0; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns and recall queries go to the configured Mem0 backend (api.mem0.ai in platform mode); at this pin the mem0ai library's anonymous PostHog usage telemetry stays on unless MEM0_TELEMETRY=false is set; `hermes memory setup` can start Docker (pgvector) and Ollama containers for local mode.

plugins.name: memanto
plugins.description: Memanto memory agent — typed long-term memory (remember/recall/answer) with auto-recall, turn capture, and RAG answers. Disclosure — each user turn (as a recall query), completed user+assistant turns, Hermes memory writes and memanto_answer questions are sent to Moorcheh cloud (api.moorcheh.ai) under a per-profile agent namespace by default; requires MOORCHEH_API_KEY; settings in $HERMES_HOME/memanto.json.

plugins.name: memex8
plugins.description: Self-hosted vector memory (Qdrant + TurboQuant compression) with auto-discovered knowledge realms, semantic search across conversations and ingested documents, and a slumber pipeline for memory consolidation. v1.1.0 adds optional per-session injection dedup with char-budget gate, decision/evaluation memory-type promotion (slower decay for load-bearing turns), prompt-injection sanitization on read, configurable system-prompt template, export/import memories as JSON, and a /memex8 slash command. New memory behaviours are opt-in; /memex8 export|import is confined to $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/memex8 unless enable_export_import=true. Disclosure — auto-stores a truncated copy (first 300 chars) of every user and assistant turn, plus per-message previews of the whole transcript at session end and before context compression, to the memex8 server at MEMEX8_BASE_URL (self-hosted; default http://localhost:8080) using MEMEX8_API_KEY.

plugins.name: memlock
plugins.description: Reasserts pinned standing instructions after context compaction. Disclosure — scope=global pins apply to every session sharing the same HERMES_HOME; memlock_setup.py edits config.yaml and .claude/settings.json (with backups) only when you run it.

plugins.name: memobase
plugins.description: Memobase memory provider — self-hosted user profile + event timeline recall, with hybrid BM25/vector/entity retrieval and automatic per-turn prefetch.

plugins.name: memoria
plugins.description: Memoria Cloud memory provider with scoped recall, explicit memory tools and opt-in background capture. Disclosure — sends recall queries and explicit memory operations to api.thememoria.ai by default (or a configured self-hosted origin). When enabled, auto capture uploads completed user/assistant text for fact extraction, excluding tool results and media. A local SQLite outbox stores pending text; credentials are resolved through the active Hermes profile's MEMORIA_API_KEY secret.

plugins.name: memory-review
plugins.description: Checkbox staged memory writes and approve or reject the selection from a dialog.

plugins.name: memory-rewind
plugins.description: Automatic version history for the built-in memory (MEMORY.md, USER.md), SOUL.md and skills/ (including curator-archived skills): browse, diff and restore any past version with `hermes memory-rewind`, or view it from any chat with the read-only `/memory-history`. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — runs the local git binary (isolated from the user's git config, hooks and signing) to keep a bare repository in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/memory-rewind/; reads only the tracked files (never .env, auth.json, databases or skills/.hub/); rewrites tracked files only when the user runs `restore`; no network.

plugins.name: memory-shield
plugins.description: Keeps your agent from rewriting or wiping what it remembers about you: by default the agent may add facts to the owner profile (USER.md) wherever it may write and may correct one only when the owner asks in a direct chat, the CLI or a trusted chat, and nobody may delete one; the agent's notes (MEMORY.md) cannot be deleted; group chats are read-only except for the people and owner-only chats you trust, and once trusted_users is set a direct chat with anyone not listed is read-only too; Hermes' unattended background review may not touch the owner profile. Block, ask through Hermes' approval prompt or just log, and undo edits and deletions from snapshots. Disclosure — no network calls, credentials, shell commands or background processes. One pre_tool_call hook reads the turn's platform, chat type, chat id and name, sender id and name and the cron flag (gateway.session_context) and whether the run is Hermes' unattended review (tools.skill_provenance.is_unattended_review), checks memory tool calls, and checks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls only for a write into, or a removal of, USER.md, MEMORY.md or the memory folder (reading a memory file or copying it elsewhere passes in calls up to 16 KB; a longer call that names them is refused); mode approve asks through Hermes' approval gate in the owner's direct chats and the CLI and blocks in shared chats, cron and direct chats with people not in trusted_users. Writes plugin-data/memory-shield/audit.jsonl (the last 500 refused or flagged writes: time, chat, sender and a 160-character excerpt) and snapshots/ (full copies of USER.md and MEMORY.md taken right before an allowed edit or deletion, 20 per file by default). Reads the memory files and holds the memory store's lock files while it reads or writes them (not on Windows); /memory-shield restore overwrites one memory file. /memory-shield log and restore answer only in direct chats, the CLI and trusted_chats, and once trusted_users is set only the people listed there (a session without a user id, such as the CLI, counts as the owner); /memory-shield, snapshots and whoami answer in any chat with settings, counts, times, sizes and the caller's own id, name and chat key.

plugins.name: memory-zvec
plugins.description: Community Zvec memory backend for Hermes Agent - in-process HNSW + RocksDB FTS store with native hybrid retrieval and session-safe lock governance; embeddings via any Ollama-compatible endpoint (local Ollama bge-m3 by default).

plugins.name: memtomem
plugins.description: Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Notes live in ~/.memtomem and are searchable from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kimi Code. Runs at user scope. Disclosure — the server is launched with `uvx --python 3.12` and downloaded from PyPI (memtomem[onnx]==0.6.8) on first start, with Python 3.12 if uv cannot find one; it runs as a stdio MCP server for the session and reads the directories you ask it to index. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing else leaves the machine; an existing memtomem configuration may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM provider, Cohere reranking or search webhooks. At startup the server also reads the nearest .env found upward from its installed location inside uv's cache (normally ~/.env), setting variables not already present, outside Hermes's MCP environment filtering.

plugins.name: mermail
plugins.description: Privacy-first agent email inboxes and workspace automation through hosted Mermail MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, seventeen skills bundled); authenticate with OAuth via `hermes mcp login mermail`. No credentials are stored in mcp.json. Disclosure — the bundled skills also expose Mermail's paybox wallet tools over the hosted MCP (x402 payments, xStocks trading, standing grants); the skills allow the agent to move funds without a same-turn confirmation when your message already states exact terms, so spending controls live on your Mermail account, not in Hermes.

plugins.name: metamask-wallet
plugins.description: MetaMask Agent Wallet for Hermes — chat-only setup, reads, and approval-gated transfers/swaps/signatures, a gated Guard Mode policy editor, and a background 2FA watcher. Keys stay in MetaMask.

plugins.name: metronix
plugins.description: Metronix memory provider for Hermes with prefetch recall and built-in memory write-through.

plugins.name: microsoft365
plugins.description: Pre-release Microsoft 365 Graph tools for Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Calendar, Teams, To Do, and Planner.

plugins.name: mindgraph
plugins.description: MindGraph — semantic graph memory with hybrid retrieval, goal/decision tracking, and cross-document synthesis.

plugins.name: minecraft-platform
plugins.description: Minecraft gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Spawns a Mineflayer bot that joins a Minecraft server, wanders around, and relays chat messages between players and the Hermes agent. Supports offline and Microsoft-authenticated accounts.

plugins.name: minimax-image
plugins.description: MiniMax image generation -- Image-01 models via MiniMax platform. Supports text-to-image and image-to-image with subject reference.

plugins.name: minimax-search
plugins.description: MiniMax web search via the Token Plan API — keyed, no CAPTCHA

plugins.name: minimax-video
plugins.description: MiniMax (Hailuo) video generation -- Hailuo 2.3/02 and S2V-01 models via MiniMax platform. Async task API. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and subject-reference-to-video.

plugins.name: mistral-vibe
plugins.description: Direct Mistral Vibe subscription access — browser PKCE login, dedicated credential pool, account-visible catalog discovery, relay-verified reasoning_effort for GLM models. Disclosure — unofficial, not affiliated with Mistral. "hermes auth add mistral-vibe" runs a browser PKCE sign-in against Mistral's Vibe console endpoints (console.mistral.ai/api/vibe/*) and stores the returned API key in the Hermes credential pool (auth.json, slice mistral-vibe), or uses MISTRAL_VIBE_API_KEY. Prompts and model listing go only to api.mistral.ai/v1. Vibe subscription coverage of API use is not guaranteed and may bill as pay-as-you-go. Logout clears the local pool but does not revoke the key remotely.

plugins.name: mnemostack
plugins.description: Persistent agent memory over a mnemostack service or a local Qdrant — hybrid recall (vector + lexical + graph), verbatim capture with self-echo suppression, and soft retraction. Multi-tenant when pointed at a shared authenticated service; the tenant is resolved server-side from the service key. Disclosure — the pinned directory is a discovery shim; the provider code installs from PyPI at the version pinned in plugin.yaml pip_dependencies (hermes-mnemostack==1.0.3) into the Hermes venv. Configured via MNEMOSTACK_* env vars; no key is required for a purely local Qdrant setup.

plugins.name: mnemosyne-dashboard
plugins.description: Local-only web dashboard for browsing and visualising Mnemosyne memories, triples, stats, and consolidation history.

plugins.name: mnemosyne
plugins.description: Local-first memory layer for Hermes Agent — SQLite with vector + FTS5 hybrid recall, episodic consolidation, temporal knowledge graph. Zero cloud. Disclosure — the mnemosyne_remember_media tool refuses local file paths unless MNEMOSYNE_MEDIA_ALLOWED_PATHS is set and sends media only to an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint when modality_enabled is on; video uses ffmpeg/ffprobe from PATH; the embedding model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) downloads from Hugging Face on first use.

plugins.name: mnemoverse
plugins.description: Persistent memory for agents, shared across tools: save preferences, decisions and lessons and recall them later by natural-language search; rating a recalled memory as helpful or misleading re-ranks what comes back next; shared rooms (beta) let several people's agents work from one memory. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at the hosted Mnemoverse MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR); the two bundled skills load under a namespaced name. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; Hermes runs no code from the package (scripts/ holds the repository's own CI checks). Every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.mnemoverse.com (authorization server auth.mnemoverse.com, browser sign-in on console.mnemoverse.com); memories the agent writes are stored in the signed-in user's Mnemoverse account, and recalled memories are pulled into the session context. OAuth tokens are held and refreshed by Hermes, never by the package. No telemetry, background process or self-update code.

plugins.name: model-drift-watch
plugins.description: Scheduled check that the model you use in Hermes has not quietly got worse: 34 fixed, exactly graded questions (reasoning, instruction following, Japanese, plus your own) run through Hermes cron, each run tested against the same model's own baseline with an exact per-question test and a same-day confirmation run, and a message only for a confirmed drop, a changed served model or a failed measurement. Not yet tried against a real LLM API (checked with a local mock model and real Hermes cron). Disclosure — each check calls your own model through ctx.llm on your bill, capped per check by the plugin (default 120,000 tokens / $0.50, no daily cap; the agent can start checks itself via the model_drift tool, and the scheduled agent turn is extra); price lookup goes through Hermes's pricing code (may fetch OpenRouter/models.dev prices); 10 optional code questions, off by default, run model-written Python in a limited child process (not a hostile-code sandbox) including in unattended cron runs when enabled; `schedule` creates one Hermes cron job that survives plugin removal (run `unschedule` first); writes run history to plugin-data/model-drift-watch; no telemetry.

plugins.name: model-router
plugins.description: Profile model settings, opt-in Heavy/Light task routing, fallback controls, runtime limits and Fast inheritance. Reads Hermes profile configuration; explicit saves update selected profiles via the native CLI. Routed jobs launch background Hermes children using the user's configured providers/MCP and store private prompts/results locally. No separate credential store, telemetry, self-updater or approval bypass. Disclosure — once you enable routing for a profile, the model-callable `coding_route` tool starts detached background Hermes agents. They get file, terminal and code-execution tools in any existing folder the model names, run under that profile's credentials and approval policy (single-query mode: dangerous commands are refused unless `approvals.single_query_mode: approve`), and their per-job time limit can be set to none. Prompts and results are stored in `plugin-data/model-router/jobs/`. Saving settings writes model, delegation, auxiliary, fallback and `skills.disabled` keys into the config.yaml of the profiles listed in the preview (backups are taken first) and copies a skill into those profiles' `skills/` folders. From install, native subagents inherit the parent session's Fast (priority/ultrafast) tier on first-party OpenAI/Codex routes, which can raise costs.

plugins.name: model-usage-status
plugins.description: Provider-native Claude and Codex remaining allowance windows in the Hermes Desktop status bar. Disclosure — spawns the local `codex app-server` and `claude auth status` CLIs and reads the Claude OAuth token read-only through Hermes core; the optional install.sh (not part of the catalog install) edits the statusLine in ~/.claude/settings.json; macOS only.

plugins.name: monid
plugins.description: Connect your agent to third-party tools and APIs (web search and scraping, people and company data, social media, media generation, email and phone) through one integration. The agent discovers, compares and runs tools at runtime, paid per call from one Monid balance. Disclosure — Monid (monid.ai, by Monid / monid-ai) is a paid third-party marketplace: the agent installs the @monid-ai/cli npm package or connects to mcp.monid.ai, sends your requests and any uploaded files to Monid and on to its providers, and each run spends your prepaid Monid workspace balance. The "confirm the price first" step is an instruction to the model in the bundled skill, not a Hermes approval prompt, unless you add `trust: untrusted` to `mcp_servers.monid`.

plugins.name: morning-briefing
plugins.description: Personal daily newspaper for Hermes: gathers weather, calendar, AQI, curated 36-hour news (timestamped Reddit RSS + X + web search, per-story QR codes), and newsletter digests, renders one 8.5x11 newsprint page, and prints it every morning via a cron job.

plugins.name: mrscraper
plugins.description: MrScraper web search, rendered extraction, crawling, and scraper tools. Disclosure — every tool call is a paid MrScraper API request billed to your account; URLs, prompts and schemas you pass are sent to mrscraper.com.

plugins.name: ms-decision-provider
plugins.description: Microsoft-Decision-1 (Azure AI Foundry System One) decision provider for bounded agent decisions. Registers typed-decision tools (decision_noul, decision_choice, decision_score, decide) that preserve full probability distributions, plus an opt-in pre_tool_call hook that requests human approval for known-risk calls without sending their arguments to Azure. Reference implementation of the typed decision-provider runtime in #113008. Disclosure — the four decision tools send the caller-supplied state/questions text to the Azure Foundry endpoint you set in AZURE_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL (nothing is sent while it is unset); with MS_DECISION_GATE=1 the pre_tool_call gate sends only a coarse operation label for known-risk tool calls to that endpoint and routes them to Hermes's human approval prompt (MS_DECISION_GATE_MODE=block hard-denies instead); the labelled eval corpus under tests/ contains literal destructive commands as should-refuse examples.

plugins.name: my-github
plugins.description: Desktop and dashboard plugin: statusbar chip, palette command, and dashboard tab listing your GitHub repos (public + private) via the gh CLI.

plugins.name: mybot-farm
plugins.description: Search mybot.farm, plant/reinstall Hermes packs (Desktop Recruit + CLI), and post GAF listings. Disclosure — plants third-party Hermes profiles (config, SOUL, skills, memories) from mybot.farm sellers with no hash pinning; force/clean delete profiles.

plugins.name: myswarm
plugins.description: Discover, visualize, sanitize/export, and import community agents.md swarm configurations. Outputs abbreviated agent/persona/goal tables, renders ASCII topology diagrams (.svg and .png images + portable 7-bit copy-paste ASCII symbol blocks), generates rich themed swarm illustrations across 12 curated signature themes and orthogonal intensity levels (understated, normal, overstated) via Hermes default model and image_generate, exports sanitized agents.md files, and imports/reverts shared configs with on-screen file preview and best-effort import warnings; every import/revert asks for approval. Disclosure — myswarm_import/myswarm_revert replace the workspace AGENTS.md/agents.md (a file Hermes loads into every session's system prompt) after a Hermes approval prompt; choosing "always" approves all later imports. The import security check is a best-effort regex + model warning, not a security boundary — only import files you trust. Swarm file contents are sent to your configured model for parsing and PII scrubbing (also best-effort; review exports before sharing), and myswarm_visualize_image calls your configured image_generate provider (may cost credits). Adds a ~2.8k-character MySwarm guidance section to every session's system prompt. Writes myswarm-ascii.svg/.png and .md exports into the current folder (exports may overwrite an existing .md file there), plus a .agents.md.myswarm.orig sidecar, and keeps import backups under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/myswarm/.

plugins.name: nachos
plugins.description: Durable memory and context compression for Hermes Agent with local SQLite or flat-file storage. Disclosure — replaces the memory provider (memory.provider: nachos) and, only when context.engine: nachos is set, the context engine; the provider injects a system-prompt block telling the agent to use the nachos_memory_* tools and keep built-in memory disabled; opt-in semantic ranking either runs a separately installed nachos-embeddings CLI or sends the turn query plus memory titles/summaries to api.openai.com with OPENAI_API_KEY; all storage is local under /nachos/.

plugins.name: needs-you
plugins.description: Hermes is waiting — full Desktop page for pending approvals. Queue, chip, OS notify. Redacted previews only. No API keys.

plugins.name: nerve
plugins.description: Nerve is a supervisory nervous system for Hermes Agent with provider-neutral Jev, Laya, and OpenJev Reflex backends, evidence-backed Kanban supervision, context governance, token-budget trajectory control, and durable SSH workers. Disclosure — the default Reflex backend is hosted Jev; with the default settings (enabled / admission_enabled on) each turn's user prompt (up to 12k characters) and redacted tool/result previews are sent to the configured Jev provider (OpenRouter Decisions / TypeSafe Jev) using your OPENROUTER_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY, spending your credits on every turn. Laya and OpenJev can be configured as local/self-hosted backends. The operator-only nerve setup CLI can copy a local HermesContextBus checkout into HERMES_HOME/plugins/hermes-context-bus and runs hermes plugins enable/disable for that plugin when a profile is saved; the model cannot trigger this.

plugins.name: netmind-provider
plugins.description: NetMind OpenAI-compatible model provider with a bundled model catalog. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests go to https://api.netmind.ai/inference-api/v1 through Hermes' own client with NETMIND_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

plugins.name: next-prompt
plugins.description: Suggests your next message after each turn as a pill under the Desktop composer: your likely answer when the agent asks you something, or the natural next step.

plugins.name: next-steps
plugins.description: Next-step suggestions under the Hermes Desktop composer after each turn: local Ollama inference, per-session state, target routing (session, new tab, bots, kanban), tiny-model capacity profiles, EN/DE UI. No API keys. Disclosure — after every agent turn, sends the last 8 messages (each cut to 200 chars) plus the working directory to Ollama on localhost; clicking a suggestion immediately submits it as a prompt in the current session, a new session, or another profile's session, or creates a kanban card, and for non-current targets also attaches the working directory and the last 6 messages (on by default, can be turned off under Targets).

plugins.name: nextcloud-talk
plugins.description: Signed Nextcloud Talk bot webhooks and text replies for Hermes, with JSON/XML OCS support. Disclosure — runs an HTTP webhook listener (default 0.0.0.0:8788, HMAC-verified with the bot secret) and sends messages and optional Basic-auth room lookups to your Nextcloud server; registers the `nextcloud_talk` gateway platform.

plugins.name: nextdns
plugins.description: Read-only NextDNS tools - DNS query logs, blocked queries with the blocklist that matched, and aggregate analytics by domain, device, blocklist or protocol. For triaging DNS problems and answering "was this blocked, and by what". Uses the official NextDNS API; makes no configuration changes.

plugins.name: nexus
plugins.description: Self-hosted long-term memory on Qdrant: automatic per-turn prefetch and write-back, plus recall/remember/forget, guardrail rules and a knowledge graph; Hermes and any MCP-connected agent share one collection. Embeddings run fully local by default (sentence-transformers with Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 1024d, about 1.2 GB from Hugging Face on first use; on Apple Silicon the model is pinned to the CPU, because PyTorch's MPS backend aborts the whole process under two overlapping encodes). A cloud embedder runs only when NEXUS_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER names it and its key is present, and a key that merely sits in the environment never selects one. Access levels fail closed: a memory, a protection rule or a graph label without a known level counts as the most restrictive. A local service on 127.0.0.1:9122 serves embeddings and the full MCP toolset; its /embed and /mcp routes demand a per-installation key (service_auth.key, mode 0600) and reject non-loopback Host/Origin, while the open /healthz answers liveness only. The plugin starts that service when Hermes cannot load the embedding stack, and it keeps running afterwards. Session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint from Hermes config.yaml, and the consolidation daemon to its configured model, which defaults to a cloud model; reads ~/.hermes/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 opts into a GitHub release check. Disclosure — when Hermes cannot load the embedding stack (and always on Apple Silicon unless NEXUS_EMBED_IN_HOST=1), the plugin starts `nexus-memory serve` on 127.0.0.1:9122 (embeddings, the full Nexus MCP toolset and a consolidation daemon whose default model is a cloud model that receives memory text), and the service keeps running after Hermes exits; its /embed and MCP routes require a per-install key in ~/.nexus-memory/service_auth.key (0600) and a loopback Host/Origin; session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint in Hermes config.yaml; reads ~/.hermes/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; opt-in NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 adds a GitHub release check and an upgrade nudge to the system prompt.

plugins.name: ngrok-ai-gateway
plugins.description: The ngrok AI Gateway as a Hermes model provider (`--provider ngrok`, or ngrok AI Gateway in `hermes model`): one access key for all your model providers, with failover. The model list comes live from your gateway, and gateway errors (unrouted model, access-policy and upstream-key failures, out of credit) map onto Hermes' fallback instead of a generic error. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1 (or NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL) through Hermes' own client with NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

plugins.name: nine-balance-widget
plugins.description: Nine AI provider balances in one desktop widget — live balance/usage and quota reads, token-based spend estimates with off-peak price windows, drop alerts, and an anime mascot per provider with rotating flavour lines (DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok). Fully English UI. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Keys are entered in the widget's settings page and stored in plugin-scoped storage; the widget only calls those providers' official APIs. Ported from MeteorNOX/DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget (MIT). Disclosure — API keys you enter in the widget's settings are stored in plaintext in Desktop plugin storage (not Hermes' secret store); while the widget is on, the Desktop renderer polls the balance/usage endpoint of the provider matching your current model every 60 s with that provider's key (api.deepseek.com, api.minimaxi.com / api.minimax.io, open.bigmodel.cn / api.z.ai, api.moonshot.cn / api.moonshot.ai, api.kimi.com, token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com, api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com with the key in the URL, api.x.ai); each key goes only to its own provider; draws a floating widget over the app window.

plugins.name: node-search
plugins.description: Bounded Markdown metadata+graph prefilter for configured local roots

plugins.name: nowstamp
plugins.description: Give the agent a clock. Appends the current date and time, plus the real gap since the previous message, to every user turn. Optional spaced-out timestamps on tool results for long runs.

plugins.name: ntfy-approval
plugins.description: Answer Hermes' approval prompts from your phone: once selected with security.approval.transport: ntfy, each dangerous-command prompt arrives as an ntfy push notification with Approve once, Approve for session and Deny buttons, and no answer still means deny. Disclosure — once selected, anyone who can read the ntfy topic can approve dangerous commands (the one-time answer codes are in the notification), so on the public ntfy.sh default the topic name is the only secret and NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN is optional; each pending approval publishes Hermes' reason, the redacted command (unless send_command is false), the non-default profile name and one-time answer codes to the configured ntfy server, then reads <topic>-reply and deletes the notification; any failure or timeout is a deny; reads NTFY_APPROVAL_TOPIC/NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN from the profile .env, never puts the token in a notification, follows no redirects, writes no files and starts no processes.

plugins.name: nvidia-app
plugins.description: NVIDIA App control through its local MCP server: overlay capture and state, driver status and release notes, game optimization, and app launch. Requires NVIDIA App 11.0 or newer on Windows; the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while the app's service is running. The plugin reads the endpoint and token NVIDIA App publishes in its own McpServer server.json on every connection, so a changed port or token needs no reconfiguration. Disclosure: the tools read and change NVIDIA App settings on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.

plugins.name: nvidia-broadcast
plugins.description: NVIDIA Broadcast control through its local MCP gateway: camera, microphone and speaker effects, Studio Voice profiles, device selection, camera resolution, and effects on local media files. Requires NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 or newer on Windows (2.2 and older have no gateway); the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while NVIDIA Broadcast is running in the user's desktop session. Disclosure: the tools change live audio and video effects on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.

plugins.name: obsidian-memory
plugins.description: Browse, search, and edit Obsidian vault notes from the Hermes dashboard. Features force-directed graph visualization, multi-vault support, markdown rendering with wikilinks, and inline note editing.

plugins.name: oc-free-provider
plugins.description: Unofficial OpenCode Zen free-model transport for Hermes. Discovers live zero-cost tool-capable models by intersecting OpenCode Zen and models.dev over HTTPS, persists only the last successful intersection for restart fallback, and bidirectionally translates compatible OpenCode and Hermes tool schemas, calls, choices, and replayed history while Hermes executes tools locally. No OpenCode CLI, Node.js, npm, or npx dependency. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results, and other conversation content leave the machine for OpenCode and the selected model provider; model availability, retention, data use, and permission are governed by their current terms.

plugins.name: offpeak-bekci
plugins.description: Makes Ollama Cloud's off-peak window visible and actionable in Hermes: a desktop status-bar chip shows the countdown and the queue item counts (Ollama off-peak hours: weekdays 18:00-12:00 UTC, weekends one block), a one-shot notice fires 30 minutes before the window opens, and approval is taken only from the user (`/offpeak-onayla <id,id>`) — work runs only if approved, and items never enter the queue by themselves. `/offpeak-durum` prints a readable report by default (machine-readable JSON with `/offpeak-durum json`), and `/offpeak-kur` prints the cron job it would install in full plus a `plan_hash`; nothing is installed without a hash-bound approval typed by the user, and the plugin never writes the cron store. One `llm_execution` middleware measures the call rate for Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window and ships measure-only (`kuru_kosu: true`): it records what it would delay and never delays. No network calls, no telemetry, no credential reads; the only local files it touches are the queue ledger and its own JSONL measurement log. Output language is English by default; `dil: tr` selects Turkish. Auto-delivery is host-dependent: in a classic CLI session the request enters the agent queue; on the Ink TUI / desktop-panel host the core asks for a persistent `session_key`, which the command handler does not receive, so the command prints the parameters as a single line of JSON. Injecting into a gateway additionally requires `plugins.entries.offpeak-bekci.allow_gateway_injection: true` (default off); the only in-process way to read that key is the private `gateway.session_context` module (rule 9 -> not used). Requires Hermes >= 0.22.2. Disclosure — the llm_execution middleware can sleep Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window once `kuru_kosu: false` is set (default is measure-only); it writes a JSONL measurement log and, on `/offpeak-onayla`, rewrites the user's queue file; `/offpeak-kur` and `/offpeak-kaldir` leave cron install/removal requests in the session (or, with `allow_gateway_injection: true`, inject them into the gateway) for the agent's own cron tool to act on; no network calls, no credential reads, never writes the cron store.

plugins.name: omh
plugins.description: Oh My Hermes (OMH) bridge: routing hints and role context for OMH workflow skills, per-task delegation model routing, plan todos and a status tool, a Hermes Desktop status pane (off until enabled), bounded evidence probes that keep prepared work apart from observed results, and a file-backed memory provider. Disclosure — omh_delegate_route writes delegation.model/provider/reasoning_effort in $HERMES_HOME/config.yaml and the session hooks restore them; omh_gather_evidence runs allowlisted checks (python -m unittest with reporting flags only, python -m compileall, git diff --check, omh doctor/probe/docs/release checks) via subprocess on the host, outside any sandboxed terminal backend and without Hermes' terminal approval, in the agent working directory or below it, so it runs whatever test code that directory holds; omh_team (only with the separate OMH core package installed) asks once through the Hermes approval prompt for an exact list of up to 8 check commands from an accepted plan, then runs them on the host as each helper returns; omh_jev_ask posts model-supplied state and questions to api.typesafe.ai (openrouter.ai only when the operator opts in via ~/.omh/jev/settings.json) with the user's own TYPESAFE_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY, only in a turn where the user names Jev; opt-in egress_attempts (re-registers chosen core tools, needs the operator's tool-override grant) and browser_adapter (vetoes core browser_* tools) settings; reads session and cost metadata from state.db read-only; state lives under ~/.omh and <project>/.omh.

plugins.name: omnivoice
plugins.description: OmniVoice TTS provider for Hermes Agent

plugins.name: opaque-composer
plugins.description: Keep the desktop composer solid while scrolling so conversation text stays readable.

plugins.name: openai-compatible
plugins.description: GPT Image through CLIProxyAPI, New API, or any OpenAI Images-compatible gateway, with gateway-aware errors and requested-vs-returned size reporting. Disclosure — sends image prompts and any source images (local files, data URLs or public HTTPS URLs) to the OpenAI-compatible gateway base_url you configure, authenticated with OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_API_KEY.

plugins.name: openalex
plugins.description: Scholarly search, citation traversal, grouped counts, and fulltext access through OpenAlex with session spending limits.

plugins.name: opencode-shepherd
plugins.description: Watch over opencode sessions from anywhere: alerts for stopped turns, questions and permissions, plus a dependency-free CLI to reply. Disclosure — the skill has the agent install the ocshepherd CLI from GitHub at a pinned commit and, after asking you, add a cron entry or systemd unit that polls your opencode server; the CLI talks to that server with the password you provide, can reply to its questions and permission prompts, and optionally sends alerts to Telegram or runs a notify command you configure.

plugins.name: openinvest
plugins.description: Self-hosted AI investment committee — skills for portfolio review, a decision ledger, and a 4-role LLM committee (macro / quant / risk / CIO) that debates a symbol. Disclosure — the skills run the openinvest backend from PyPI via uvx (pinned in run.sh) and keep portfolio, ledger, committee records and any keys you add in plaintext under ~/openInvest (or $INVEST_HOME); it fetches public market data and RSS news, and on the Direct path / daily report sends your portfolio and wealth context to the LLM you configure (default api.deepseek.com) and, if installed, to the agy or gemini CLI for a second opinion; news ingestion can trigger extra committee runs (LLM spend). The MCP tools are a server you add to config.yaml yourself (the printed snippet runs the plugin's pinned run.sh with `trust: untrusted`, so Hermes asks before ledger writes); buy/sell/deposit/withdraw only edit the local ledger — it never connects to a broker or places orders.

plugins.name: openltm
plugins.description: Long-term memory for Hermes agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. Runtime notifications and read-only OpenLTM tool requests are excluded by named guards so ops noise never becomes memory. No cloud, no telemetry, no API keys required; optional semantic recall via a local llama.cpp embedding server. MIT licensed. Disclosure — local SQLite in HERMES_HOME; runs git config to read the repo remote; memory text goes to Gemini or OpenAI embeddings, or to the llama.cpp server URL you set (default 127.0.0.1:8080), only if selected in openltm.json (default local Ollama)

plugins.name: openmail
plugins.description: Gives a Hermes agent its own email address. Inbound mail wakes the agent over a websocket, replies go out in-thread, plus tools for sending, reading and provisioning inboxes.

plugins.name: openrouter-picker
plugins.description: One install: the Desktop model picker and the OR Picker composer provider. Checking a model here is what the composer lists. Disclosure — the optional OpenRouter management key is stored in plaintext in Desktop localStorage; the plugin reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from your environment, Hermes secret store or HERMES_HOME/.env and sends it only to openrouter.ai (credits, usage, and the Test-model button, which spends credits).

plugins.name: openrouter-spend
plugins.description: OpenRouter API-key spend and recorded chat costs in USD/INR. Disclosure — sends the configured OpenRouter key (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or the variable named in api_key_env) only to openrouter.ai's read-only key and generation accounting endpoints, and fetches public USD/INR rates from api.frankfurter.dev unless a manual rate is set; middleware on every LLM request records ids, model, token counts and reported cost (no prompt or reply text) to its own ledger; the dashboard reads accounting metadata (session ids, token counts, billing provider) read-only from the state.db and OpenRouter Spend ledger of every profile under the Hermes root.

plugins.name: openrouter-voice
plugins.description: OpenRouter speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers for Hermes Agent (stt.provider / tts.provider = openrouter).

plugins.name: openspec
plugins.description: OpenSpec CLI tools for spec-driven development workflows

plugins.name: openviking
plugins.description: Long-term memory for Hermes. Capture conversations, recall useful facts across sessions and search your knowledge. Choose Quick Local, OpenViking Service (managed cloud) or your own server. Disclosure — conversation turns, tool results and MEMORY.md / USER.md edits are sent to the configured OpenViking server. Quick Local setup installs the newest OpenViking 0.4.x server release from PyPI at setup time (checked against PyPI's hash, not the version reviewed here; re-running setup upgrades it) plus a hash-pinned llama-cpp-python wheel and a local embedding model. It copies the active Hermes static LLM API key into a private file under the profile for extraction, and its localhost server keeps running after Hermes exits and after plugin removal (stop it with `hermes openviking local stop`). Extraction can use a remote LLM. Custom localhost connections can start openviking-server from PATH with the profile environment minus Hermes bot, gateway, GitHub and dashboard secrets; model and tool API keys still pass.

plugins.name: operations
plugins.description: A Hermes Desktop page for running a fleet - topology, model traffic, handoffs, traces, merge requests and conformance checks in one place. Disclosure — reads hermes-metrics-dash's <hermes root>/metrics/metrics.db, the kanban board, every profile's config.yaml (plugin enable state, rolectl-mcp entries, default model) and plugin-data/gitlab-mr/device-aliases.json, all read-only; calls your GitLab (host and token from the plugin settings or GITLAB_HOST/GITLAB_TOKEN), the local model router (MODEL_ROUTER_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8867) and LM Studio (LMSTUDIO_URL, default 127.0.0.1:1234); runs git status/rev-parse/ls-files in the project folders it checks and shows matching lines (including any keys found) on the page. Page buttons create, assign, schedule, unblock and close kanban cards and start their workers at once, write <hermes root>/conformance/conformance.yaml, and "Propose a rule" pushes a branch and opens a merge request on the standard's GitLab project. A hook on every kanban dispatcher tick starts cards scheduled from the page; with alert_target set it posts new attention items through hermes send; with drift_action: automatic it files and starts a fix card for drift_profile for each drifting host with a verified report (at most daily) carrying the standard's remediate commands. With Activity summaries on (off by default), Activity sentences and each "Explain this session" click send log lines and trace details to the model set for the operations_summary auxiliary task.

plugins.name: optchat
plugins.description: OptChat-style endless memory for Hermes: an append-only verbatim log plus a binary summary tree, exposed as recall through the MemoryProvider ABC. Background compactor builds the tree with a cheap auxiliary model (call_llm task optchat_compact); prefetch returns a fixed-budget view of the whole history; optchat_zoom/optchat_date tools open any line down to the verbatim message. Disclosure — every turn's user messages, agent replies, tool calls and tool results (each result capped at 30,000 characters, after Hermes's secret redaction) are appended permanently to unencrypted owner-only files under $HERMES_HOME/optchat/, with no deletion or retention limit; a background compactor sends those messages and the surrounding summary view to your auxiliary model route (task optchat_compact) for summarization; each turn injects up to view_budget_chars (default 16,000) of that history into the model context.

plugins.name: optmem-hermes
plugins.description: Independent Hermes integration of Victor Taelin's OptMem design: local, append-only memory with regex/BM25 recall and a bounded wake digest. Hybrid and guarded OptMem-only modes; verified migration and rollback. Local by default. Compaction is manual unless auto_nap is enabled. Optional LLM summaries run only when both auto_nap and llm_summary are on; they send memory blocks to the configured provider via host-owned authentication and may incur token costs. Summaries are lossy, raw records remain recoverable, and conflicts are not resolved automatically. Wake consumes model context. See README for upstream attribution. Disclosure — memory is stored locally under HERMES_HOME; optional auto_nap+llm_summary sends stored memory lines to the user's configured model provider; the optmem-only mode (explicit CLI with --yes) disables Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md injection after a verified backup.

plugins.name: orbit-desktop
plugins.description: Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by Hermes. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working Hermes provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Nous Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the Hermes tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current Hermes conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local Hermes session API and kept in the browser only. The Nous Atelier theme contains Nous Research logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Nous Research.

plugins.name: orcaslicer
plugins.description: Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. Includes explicit printer upload/control, camera snapshots and monitoring through supported protocols. Protocol and hardware limits are documented. Independent of OrcaSlicer and Nous Research. Disclosure — executes the installed local slicer and exposes printer upload, start, pause, resume and cancel; agent-supplied confirmation is not independent human authentication. Printer/camera credentials are read from ORCA_*/HERMES_ORCA_* environment variables named in tool arguments (HTTPS required unless allow_plaintext_credentials is set); plugin state lives in ~/.hermes-orca (HERMES_ORCA_HOME), outside HERMES_HOME.

plugins.name: osv-ref
plugins.description: @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: context references: attach a vulnerability record from OSV.dev to a message (summary, aliases, severity, affected packages with version ranges and fixed versions, details, references), with package data merged from up to four alias records. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id> only (the referenced id and up to four of its alias ids leave the machine); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: reference providers.

plugins.name: parallel-search
plugins.description: Free web search and page fetching through Parallel's hosted MCP, with a setup skill bundled. No account or API key required. Queries and requested URLs are sent to Parallel. Adds direct MCP tools alongside Hermes's native web providers.

plugins.name: parcel-deliveries
plugins.description: Track package deliveries with the Parcel app (parcelapp.net). List what's on the way, add tracking numbers and look up carrier codes, with a built-in guard for Parcel's strict rate limits. Disclosure — sends tracking numbers, descriptions and optional postcode/order email to api.parcel.app (Parcel Premium API key); the model can add deliveries to the user's Parcel account (add-only, capped at 20/day); caches delivery lists in plugin-data.

plugins.name: parlor
plugins.description: Rooms where AI agents of any vendor talk to each other. A room is a URL; agents join, read and post over plain HTTP, with no accounts and no sign-in. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: the parlor skill plus the hosted parlor MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no authentication, 8 tools). Disclosure — hosted unauthenticated MCP connector at parlor.sh/mcp (tool set is server-controlled, not pinned) plus a curl fallback; messages the agent writes go to parlor.sh or the server in a given room URL and rooms are public to anyone with the link; room tokens are stored under ~/.local/state/parlor; the skill may keep background wait loops running.

plugins.name: parrotnotes
plugins.description: Find, search, summarize and save insights for your ParrotNotes in-person meeting notes through the hosted ParrotNotes MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0 + DCR), with the parrotnotes workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.parrotnotes.app (OAuth via a Supabase auth backend); note titles, transcripts and insights from the user's ParrotNotes account are pulled into the session context, and text the model passes to save_note_insight is written to that account. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add parrotnotes --url https://mcp.parrotnotes.app/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

plugins.name: pass-secrets
plugins.description: pass (password-store) secret source: resolves secrets from a local, GPG-encrypted, git-tracked password store into environment variables at startup, as a first-class SecretSource beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources. Stdlib-only (subprocess + pathlib), no Python deps, no network — ever. Config: secrets.pass.{enabled,store_path,subdirs,override_existing,timeout_seconds}. Disclosure — when enabled, shells out to the local pass binary (10 s per entry) for every .gpg entry under the configured store subdirs and injects each as an env var that by default overrides .env and shell values; when enabled, also adds a ~900-char system-prompt note about secret resolution; no network.

plugins.name: pastdotdev
plugins.description: past.dev memory provider: recall before each turn from source-traced memory of past conversations, with sessions sent to past.dev when they end. Maintained by past.dev. Disclosure — the user's message (as the recall query) and each session's user and assistant text, with common secret shapes redacted, are sent to the past.dev API (api.past.dev by default, or the address you configure) under your past project key, with a past-hermes/<version> User-Agent; the key and identity are read from PAST_API_KEY or ~/.past/config.json, which past.dev's other connectors share; off by default on messaging-gateway sessions.

plugins.name: pay-cli
plugins.description: Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins from a wallet on this machine, through the local `pay mcp` stdio server of the official Pay CLI, with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; the user installs the `pay` CLI (brew or npm) and runs `pay setup` first, and the server is offered only while `pay` is on PATH. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: Hermes starts `pay mcp` as a long-running local process; the curl tool spends the local wallet's stablecoin balance; each payment is confirmed by the user through MCP elicitation (PAY_FORCE_ELICITATION=1, declined when nobody can answer) and the server is marked untrusted; every profile using the plugin shares the same local wallet.

plugins.name: pay
plugins.description: Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins through the official hosted Pay MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://connect.pay.sh/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys or local wallet), with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: the curl tool spends the hosted Pay account's stablecoin balance; hosted Pay enforces the account's spending limits (none move until the user sets them) and confirms each payment through MCP elicitation, declined when nobody can answer; the plugin marks its server untrusted, but the documented OAuth setup (`hermes mcp add pay`) replaces that entry with a native one that runs at `trust: full` unless the user sets `mcp_servers.pay.trust: untrusted`; chats sharing a Hermes profile share its Pay account; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

plugins.name: pcs-security-tls-posture
plugins.description: Read-only audit of local TLS posture — certificate validity, key strength, deprecated protocols, weak cipher suites, and the certificate each server's configuration points at. Disclosure — reads a fixed list of system certificate and nginx/Apache config paths under / (or a caller-supplied prefix); makes no network connections and runs no subprocesses. If the sibling plugin pcs-security-core is installed, its copy of the shared contract is loaded in preference to the bundled one.

plugins.name: pdf-surgeon
plugins.description: Model-driven editor of PDF text whose result keeps the original typesetting, by rewriting the page content stream in place — the string operand inside the existing BT/ET block is replaced and the Tm origin of everything after it on the line is retargeted, so font, size, colour, baseline, char/word spacing, horizontal scale and kerning survive untouched because they are never rewritten. This is the alternative to redact-and-re-stamp, which defaults to Helvetica 8pt and makes you restate font, size and colour by hand; get any of that wrong and the page reads as forged. The phrase must match exactly (whitespace is ignored); a fuzzy match is refused rather than allowed to edit text the caller never named. Until an edit is accepted the output is written under a temporary name next to the destination and moved into place only after verification passes, so a failed check leaves nothing behind; the destination must end in .pdf, must not already exist, must not resolve to the input, and must have an existing parent directory, because the path arrives from the model. Verification enforces that the edited line reads exactly as the original with the phrase swapped and nothing else, that every other line on the page is unchanged, that block count, baseline, font, size and spacing hold, that the old phrase's occurrence count dropped by exactly one (allowing for copies inside the replacement), and that the page's font/size/colour set is unchanged; a pixel-diff band is reported for information and does not decide the outcome. Refuses, writing nothing, on scans, Type3/XObject text, pages with more than one content stream, and a replacement needing a glyph the embedded subset lacks — it never falls back to substituting a typeface. Widths are measured from the embedded font program, not the system font of the same name. action="inspect" lists each line with its baseline and BT/ET block count so a caller can tell whether a document is editable before choosing what to replace. Requires a digital-born PDF whose text is laid out as one block per word/run with an explicit Tm origin (Word, LibreOffice, Excel, Google Docs). Disclosure — this can alter documents such as certificates or invoices; use it only on documents you are entitled to change. The edit is not visible on the page and not recorded in the Info dictionary. It is detectable at file level: the PDF is re-saved by PyMuPDF as a single revision, so the file hash and the second trailer /ID change, any earlier incremental-save history is dropped and any digital signature no longer validates. Writes only a new .pdf that does not exist yet and never touches the input. No network, credentials or subprocesses. Depends on PyMuPDF (AGPL-3.0), which Hermes installs for this plugin. Output files inherit the 0600 mode of the temporary file they are moved from.

plugins.name: penny
plugins.description: Penny core memory and private notes for Hermes. Disclosure — automatic recall sends the first 4,000 characters of each nontrivial local prompt to app.mypenny.ai as a search query, and the agent can save notes there through penny_remember without a Hermes approval prompt; works only in local CLI/TUI conversations (cron, subagents and gateways are refused); login is a manual command that registers its own OAuth client with clerk.mypenny.ai and briefly listens on 127.0.0.1 for the callback; tokens are kept in <HERMES_HOME>/penny/auth.json (owner-only) and are not removed on uninstall; no raw transcript upload, telemetry or other-client credential reuse.

plugins.name: pep-ref
plugins.description: @pep:<number> context references: attach a Python Enhancement Proposal to a message (status, type, authors, Python version and its first section, usually the Abstract), or one section with @pep:<number>#<section>, with PEP number and title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to peps.python.org only (the PEP index and the referenced PEP's page; section names and autocomplete text are matched locally); keeps the index in memory for an hour; no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @pep: reference provider.

plugins.name: personae
plugins.description: A messenger-style roster for Hermes Desktop: one row per profile with its live sessions, per-profile colour, status lights, search, groups, multi-select and an Apropos beta that starts a new session already knowing the ones you picked. Disclosure — a Desktop pane over all your local profiles: it reads each profile's sessions, cron jobs and settings through the app's own requests and, only when you click, deletes or archives sessions (deletes ask first), changes cron jobs or edits profile settings; Apropos starts a new session with a hidden pointer message naming the sessions you picked; no network calls or telemetry.

plugins.name: phone-harness
plugins.description: Drive a real phone from Hermes with one phone_exec tool: an iPhone via iPhone Mirroring on a Mac, an Android over adb, or a cloud phone from Phone Harness Cloud. Disclosure — runs model-written Python on this computer with your user's permissions through the phone-harness package (installed from PyPI); every phone_exec call goes to Hermes's approval prompt unless you opt in to classifier auto-run, a heuristic, bypassable check that decides which scripts ask first; taps and types into your real phone and its apps and accounts; screenshots go to the system temp folder and are attached to the tool result for vision models; a cloud phone streams its screen to Phone Harness Cloud, bills by the minute, and uses phone-harness's own cloud sign-in (~/.config/phone-harness/auth.json); phone-harness's PostHog telemetry (script text, script output, helper arguments) is off under Hermes unless you opt in.

plugins.name: pinned-folders
plugins.description: A Pinned tab in the Desktop sidebar that files your pinned chats into nested folders: drag to order and nest, folder colors, right-click menus (including Unpin), unread/working badges on collapsed folders, a filter box, open-folder-as-tabs, and layout export/import via the clipboard. Layout stays local to the app; pins belong to the backend. SDK-only build (desktop/plugin.js); no network.

plugins.name: pixel-worlds
plugins.description: Watch your agents inhabit pixel-art realms in Hermes Desktop, with imported scenes and a minimal PW Agents display.

plugins.name: plan-mode
plugins.description: Claude Code-style plan mode for Hermes: the agent explores and writes a plan, and edits nothing else until you approve it. It works on every interactive Hermes surface: /plan or /planmode on blocks mutating Hermes tools dispatched through pre_tool_call (writes outside .hermes/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) while the agent explores, asks clarifying questions and writes a plan. The agent shows the complete plan, submits it with plan_mode(submit) and one approval card asks: approve and auto-accept edits, approve and review each file edit (when Hermes approvals are on, every write_file and patch then gets Hermes' approval prompt with its path and a preview), or keep planning; Other sends feedback, and the revised plan says what changed since the last revision. Once approved, it implements in the same turn and tracks todo_list progress. To change the plan yourself, keep planning, run /planmode edit, save, then /planmode show and /planmode approve; the text you were shown is saved as an approved snapshot, so later edits to the file do not change the approval. The classic profile (plan_profile: classic), approval_card: false and surfaces without a card use Hermes' own approval prompt (gateway buttons, the TUI/Desktop card, the CLI panel or /approve). When yolo or approvals.mode: off would auto-approve, it asks through clarify instead, so a person still decides. By default plans are compact and decision-complete, the lean profile asks at most three targeted questions, and the agent does not commit unless asked (plan_style, plan_profile, allow_commits and plan_skill settings). Classic CLI enforced on every supported Hermes; gateway, TUI and Desktop from Hermes v2026.9.24 (0.21.5), and refused on older builds; 0.21.6 recommended. On the interactive classic CLI, Hermes' inline diff shows a new plan file in full, so the agent does not retype it (write_once). A report-a-problem skill drafts a bug report and files it with gh only after you approve the draft. Disclosure — plan-mode does not enforce Codex app-server exec/applyPatch or TUI /background and btw side agents. A plan is approved only on its approval card (a clarify question only the plugin issues and checks), through Hermes' own approval prompt, or with /planmode approve. It reads nine groups of internal Hermes seams for session identity, workspace, profile, skills.inline_shell and the classic CLI's inline diff, each guarded with a documented fallback. It creates .hermes/plans under the session working directory, reads plan files there, saves the approved text of an edited plan as a new file under .hermes/plans/approved, and keeps per-session state in plugin state. It adds a turn note while planning or executing, a ≤200-char system-prompt hint, and a one-line footer to short replies on chat platforms. When a turn ends while a submitted plan still awaits approval and no approval card was answered, it adds one line to that reply on any surface, whatever its length, saying how to approve (unless footer is off). When you pick "Always" on a plan approval or a per-edit review, Hermes core writes a plugin_rule:plan-mode entry to command_allowlist in config.yaml; each entry is keyed to one plan revision, so it cannot approve another plan. With allow_gateway_injection: true it queues one message to start work after a typed /planmode approve. On TUI, Desktop and hermes serve sessions (lean profile, plan_once) it reads the visible reply text from post_api_request while planning and saves its <proposed_plan> block as the plan file. On the interactive classic CLI (lean, write_once) it checks that Hermes printed a newly written plan file in full, then tells the agent not to retype it. Its report-a-problem skill has the agent file to the plugin repository with gh only after the user approves the exact saved draft. The plugin itself makes no network calls, launches no subprocesses and has no self-updater.

plugins.name: pocket-watch
plugins.description: Dashboard-only cron companion: a Pocket Watch pane showing cron jobs by schedule (daily/weekly/monthly), a health view of run outcomes and consecutive failures, a timeline, and maintenance actions — a read-oriented window onto the scheduler rather than another agent-facing toolset. Disclosure — the pane's API reads the cron jobs file under HERMES_HOME to render schedules and run history; it registers no tools, hooks or middleware, performs no network I/O and holds no credentials.

plugins.name: post-cortex
plugins.description: Self-hosted long-term memory through a post-cortex daemon (https://github.com/julymetodiev/post-cortex): typed records (decisions, fixed problems, code changes) in an entity graph with local semantic search. Recalls related records from the profile's workspace before each turn, mirrors built-in memory writes as records, and adds post_cortex_search, post_cortex_record and post_cortex_context (graph neighbours and reverse dependencies of named components) plus the post-cortex:memory skill. Profiles are mapped to shared workspaces by name glob, so a team of profiles recalls each other's records. Disclosure — talks only to the post-cortex daemon at the configured URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3737; a remote daemon over plain HTTP should sit on a private network or behind TLS): each non-trivial user prompt (up to 2,000 characters) is sent as a search query, and built-in memory writes and post_cortex_record calls are sent as records; nothing goes to third parties. Disclosure — the daemon stores records in its own database and redacts credentials, e-mail addresses, phone numbers and public IPv4 addresses on write. Disclosure — PCX_TOKEN (and optionally PCX_URL) is read through the Hermes secret scope; the only local state is $HERMES_HOME/post-cortex.json (0600, never holds the token). No background threads or processes, no shell commands, no deletes in post-cortex; cron and subagent runs never write automatically.

plugins.name: pricewin
plugins.description: Live hotel and flight prices from Booking.com, Agoda, Trip.com and Traveloka through the PriceWin MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.price.win, no account or key), with the pricewin-travel-search skill and inline hotel/flight cards for the Desktop transcript bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Booking is a request the hotel confirms; nothing is ever charged. Disclosure — connects to the hosted PriceWin MCP server at mcp.price.win (no key); search arguments including a verbatim excerpt of the user's request go to it, and four of its twelve tools act on bookings (request_booking sends guest details to the hotel, cancellation needs a token emailed to the guest); nothing is charged.

plugins.name: print-job-watch
plugins.description: Reads one OctoPrint printer. A cron watch reports printer_disconnected (not a pause); error; complete after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, Paused, Resuming, or Finishing; paused after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, or Resuming; cancelled; and stalled. This plugin can be used with OctoPrint. OctoPrint is a registered trademark owned by Gina Häußge (https://octoprint.org). Disclosure — Talks to the one OctoPrint origin you set in OCTOPRINT_URL with your OCTOPRINT_API_KEY, plus an optional webcam still from the same host, fetched without the key when it is on another port. Over plain http, that key is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume, and cancel ask for Hermes approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, and when those checks cannot run. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can ask for a move and approve it. Running hermes tools does not remove the slash command. Answering "always" adds one unused line to config.yaml, and that line does not approve the next move. The optional watch is a cron job you create from the CLI (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. At that default it is 288 runs a day with no daily cap. The watch needs plugins.isolation: in_process; under host it only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Not tested on a physical printer, with access control off, or with the stock webcam.

plugins.name: prism
plugins.description: Prism OpenAI-compatible inference with long-context DeepSeek models.

plugins.name: privacy-gateway
plugins.description: Local Presidio-based PII pseudonymization for Hermes model requests and tool results with an encrypted profile-scoped alias vault. Disclosure — PII detection runs locally with Presidio and the spaCy en_core_web_lg model, which you install manually; alias mappings are stored encrypted in the Hermes plugin DB under HERMES_PRIVACY_GATEWAY_KEY; requests are blocked when the engine cannot load; tools outside rehydrate_tool_allowlist receive alias tokens, not plaintext.

plugins.name: profile-models
plugins.description: Read-only Desktop model map for main, auxiliary, sub-agent and MoA routes. Disclosure — reads the selected profile's full config.yaml through the host's `config.get` (the response includes any credential fields it holds); only model-routing fields are kept and nothing is stored or sent off the machine.

plugins.name: profile-pane
plugins.description: Disclosure — copies .env key values (and opt-in auth.json backups) between profiles; rewrites other profiles' SOUL, memory and config.yaml. Cross-profile config pane with copy+manifest reconcile and per-group scope.

plugins.name: profile-picker
plugins.description: Pick the profile for a new chat right in the composer, next to the model pill, and see which profile a running chat belongs to.

plugins.name: progress-squash
plugins.description: Collapses carriage-return progress bars (tqdm, git clone --progress and similar) in terminal output to the frame a terminal would show, so the model reads one line instead of every redraw: a 300-step tqdm loop goes from 17,396 characters to about 120. Other text written between redraws, CRLF line endings and output without a carriage return are left as they are. Disclosure — register() adds one transform_terminal_output hook that rewrites the output string in memory; no tools, network access, subprocesses, files, settings or environment variables.

plugins.name: prompt-enhance
plugins.description: Rewrite a composer draft outside the chat and put the finished prompt back in the field. A prompt library keeps saved prompts, and a one-call model pick does not change the session.

plugins.name: prompt-enhancer
plugins.description: A composer button for Hermes Desktop that rewrites a rough draft into a structured prompt (task / scope / constraints / output shape) and restores the original on a second click. One stateless gateway call, preserves @file and /command chips, per-session state. UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體.

plugins.name: prompt-optimizer
