up to 4 MB each, links followed as the engine follows them) are read from the directory that prompt names (else the engine's TERMINAL_CWD or the gateway's working directory), and .hermes.md, HERMES.md and the AGENTS names also from the gateway's working directory and HERMES_HOME, which may be outside HERMES_HOME; to tell whether the prompt carries them as they are on disk; only a verdict, the file names, sizes and times are kept, never the prompt's or a file's text; every tick HERMES_HOME/memories/MEMORY.md and USER.md (up to 4 MB each) are read to count their characters against the limits, the waiting writes in HERMES_HOME/pending/memory and pending/skills (up to 2,000 files) for their names and times and, of the memory ones (up to 256 KB each), each add's target and length, and the time of HERMES_HOME/skills/.curator_ledger.jsonl; never a notebook's, an entry's or a waiting write's text, and nothing there is written; the private hermes_cli.version_info._cached_version_info and the signature of agent.prompt_builder._read_text_with_timeout are read from modules the gateway already imported, and nothing is called or changed on them; the release check keeps only each release's version and publication time and downloads, installs or replaces nothing; config.yaml is read through Hermes' own YAML parser for the memory limits, switches, approval gate and provider name, skills.write_approval and each platform's skip_context_files; the plugin's own code never reads the Telegram bot token and never writes vendor credential files (Hermes' auth code it calls for Grok and Kimi may, as said above), and no request the plugin's own code sends with a token in a header follows a redirect; the latest Hermes release is read from api.github.com without a token at most once per 15 minutes (releases/latest with the last answer's ETag; the release list releases?per_page=100 only when Latest names another version); an operator-configured drift_command, if set, runs as a subprocess; the delivery record is written under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/.

plugins.name: telnyx-provider
plugins.description: Vendor-maintained Telnyx inference provider with an authenticated live model catalog, hosted open models, frontier routes, and catalog-derived pricing.

plugins.name: thomas
plugins.description: Fine-tune a small calibrated encoder classifier on Modal and rate it with gonogo. Every GPU launch goes through the human approval gate with the exact config shown; data checks and evaluation run locally for free. Disclosure — thomas_encoder_train spends the user's Modal GPU credits and uploads the chosen training JSONL rows to Modal after the human approval gate; the base model is downloaded from Hugging Face on the Modal side. Training and inference run in a separate Python interpreter the user configures via THOMAS_PYTHON (with the author's thomas package, torch and modal installed); the Hermes venv only gets gonogo-eval. Runs and artifacts are written under HERMES_HOME/thomas/runs; the eval tool writes report files to the path the model supplies.

plugins.name: time-gap
plugins.description: Inject an implicit time-gap sense only when a gap or a date rollover crosses.

plugins.name: tinyfish
plugins.description: First-party TinyFish plugin: free Search and Fetch as a web provider, plus credit-gated remote Browser sessions and the tinyfish_agent web agent. Disclosure — sends search queries, URLs to fetch and tinyfish_agent goals with your TINYFISH_API_KEY to the TinyFish API (*.tinyfish.ai). Browser sessions and tinyfish_agent runs spend TinyFish credits. Under the default `request` policy each one goes through Hermes's approval prompt first (a session/always answer covers every later call; cron and unattended runs are denied unless you allow them). Setting `tinyfish.credit_policy.<feature>: allow` or YOLO skips the prompt. `hermes tinyfish setup` / `browser enable` (run by you) save the key to Hermes .env, set web.search_backend/extract_backend and browser.cloud_provider in config.yaml, enable the web/browser toolsets, and can install the agent-browser CLI after asking.

plugins.name: titanos-mcp
plugins.description: Connect Hermes to Titanos marketplace, Amazon, listings, Ads, and product research tools through the pinned Titanos OAuth MCP client. This portable Agent Plugin v1 package bundles seven operating skills, requires Node.js 20.18.1 or newer, and uses browser authorization with a Titanos account. Disclosure — starts the npm package @titanos/mcp-agents@1.47.2 via npx (fetched from npm on first run); its tools read and WRITE live marketplace/Ads accounts under your Titanos OAuth session.

plugins.name: token-cost-meter
plugins.description: Live token usage, model-aware USD cost and prompt-cache savings in the Hermes Desktop status bar, with a persistent per-day ledger that survives restarts. Disclosure — Desktop only; no network calls of its own (prices come from the gateway's model.options and a bundled models.dev rate table); stores per-day token totals, per-session counters and last-known rates in its own Desktop plugin storage; costs are list-price estimates, not billing data.

plugins.name: tokenwatch
plugins.description: Monitor Hermes token usage, notify at thresholds, and freeze tool/gateway activity at configured limits.

plugins.name: tokstat
plugins.description: Live token usage in the Hermes Desktop status bar: cumulative total, a real-time this-turn counter, last-turn delta, context occupancy, and prompt-cache hit rate. Event-driven (no polling, no RPC); English and Chinese, follows the app locale.

plugins.name: tool-slimmer
plugins.description: Reduce Hermes tool-schema overhead and show selector savings in the dashboard. Disclosure — optional mode jev (off by default; needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY) sends each turn's request text and up to 32 candidate tool names and descriptions to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai); all other modes run locally. Optional user-run scripts can patch Hermes core on older Hermes and install a systemd user self-heal unit; the dashboard advisor edits the tool_slimmer section of config.yaml with a backup.

plugins.name: toolaria
plugins.description: Rescues oversized MCP and web tool results before they flood context.

plugins.name: touchdesigner
plugins.description: Drive a live TouchDesigner session through the twozero MCP server (Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1:40404), with the touchdesigner-mcp workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); TouchDesigner itself runs on macOS/Windows.

plugins.name: tsubasa
plugins.description: Tsubasa OpenAI-compatible model provider (tool calling not supported yet). Disclosure — sends prompts and your TSUBASA_API_KEY to api.tsubasa.sh, operated by PalmAndWand; the API currently serves Canada only and answers HTTP 451 to requests from elsewhere.

plugins.name: ttsbuddy
plugins.description: Native TTS Buddy speech provider using the existing TTS Buddy CLI, with offline voice selection, MP3 generation, Hermes voice-message conversion and exact-job recovery, plus terminal-only account deletion through CLI 0.16.0+. Disclosure — runs the user-installed `ttsbuddy` CLI (argument array, speech text on stdin), which sends the text and voice settings to TTS Buddy, downloads the hosted audio and uses the account's quota. Credentials come from the profile's `TTSBUDDY_API_KEY` secret or, when the user selects `cli_config_dir`, from that CLI profile's own saved login, which the CLI may read and update. The model-callable `ttsbuddy_recover` tool downloads an existing job to a new MP3 path the model chooses (never overwrites). The terminal command `hermes ttsbuddy account delete` can permanently delete the TTS Buddy account, its hosted files and identity, and cancel subscriptions, after `--yes` and a fresh email code entered at a hidden prompt or protected stdin.

plugins.name: turn-bell
plugins.description: A bell in the Hermes desktop composer that pings the ntfy topic Hermes already uses when a turn finishes. Click to cycle off, current turn, or all turns. Disclosure — when enabled, posts the first line of each finished reply plus model, duration, token and cost figures to the ntfy server/topic Hermes is configured with (default ntfy.sh); reads NTFY_* from the profile .env and falls back to the ntfy CLI's ~/.config/ntfy/client.yml login (read-only).

plugins.name: turn-usage
plugins.description: Usage and cost footer appended to every reply — tokens, cache hit rate, cost and context occupancy, plus a per-tool time breakdown showing which tool actually consumed the wall clock. Waiting time (a blocking user prompt) is reported separately and excluded from the active-time denominator. Pure computation, never calls a model; any failure leaves the reply untouched. Disclosure — the usage footer is appended to the stored assistant reply, so it is replayed to the model on later turns and adds tokens to every turn.

plugins.name: twenty-crm
plugins.description: Twenty CRM for Hermes Agent with managed self-hosting, external-instance connectivity, REST, GraphQL, and live schema introspection.

plugins.name: typesafe-skill-router
plugins.description: TypeSafe (Jev) skill routing: the request is routed before the model call and the one skill from the live roster that fits it is named in a single <skill_relevance> line on the user message — nothing is injected when nothing fits.

plugins.name: umt
plugins.description: Connect 28 production-ready MCP servers to any coding agent. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): three zero-config stdio servers out of the box (Hacker News, arXiv, npm registry, each pinned to an exact npm version), plus the umt-mcp skill that drives the umt CLI to wire any of the 28 servers into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Zed and more. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

plugins.name: unbrowse
plugins.description: Unbrowse: websites as APIs. Read any page as clean markdown, run tasks on sites through learned first-party APIs (no browser), and drive a cloud browser with saved logins when nothing matches. Also a web_extract backend and a guard that routes public-web browser_* calls to Unbrowse. Disclosure — hosted service: page URLs, task text and tool arguments are sent to unbrowse.ai with your API key, pages are fetched and site logins are stored on Unbrowse's side, and verified calls bill the Unbrowse account; once UNBROWSE_API_KEY is set the plugin blocks the built-in browser_* tools and web_extract on public URLs by default (settings blockBrowser/blockWebExtract, or UNBROWSE_ALLOW_BUILTIN_BROWSER=1).

plugins.name: unitares
plugins.description: Records each Hermes session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Fail-open; never blocks the agent. Disclosure — sends only to the server named in UNITARES_MCP_URL, which you host; there is no default server. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can delay a call by roughly 40 seconds (connection plus call timeout). After 3 consecutive failures the plugin stops reporting for that session only, until the session is finalized or reset; it stays fail-open and never blocks the agent. If UNITARES_BEARER is set, it is sent as a request header to that same server only.

plugins.name: unraid
plugins.description: Read-only Unraid monitoring for Hermes Desktop: server metadata, array capacity, Docker containers, virtual machines, and grouped alerts. Disclosure — sends fixed GraphQL queries to the user-configured Unraid host and stores a VIEWER key through Hermes secret scope; no telemetry, background process, shell, SSH, MCP, or mutations.

plugins.name: usage-flame
plugins.description: Pinned glowing chip + fire-themed panel with live subscription-quota windows (remaining %, reset countdown, burn-rate pace and run-out forecast with sparkline history) for every provider Hermes reports usage for. 12 color themes and fonts, RU/EN, zero dependencies, works on Windows. Disclosure — runs hermes usage --json through the Desktop gateway (cli.exec) every 1–15 minutes and sweeps up to 8 providers every 15 minutes; each run queries that provider's usage endpoint with the credential Hermes already holds. Reads the composer's selected provider from Desktop localStorage. No network calls of its own.

plugins.name: usage-guard
plugins.description: Keeps an agent inside its subscription allowance: refuses a provider dispatch once a subscription usage window is exhausted, so an account that allows paid extra usage stops at the wall instead of spending overage. Reads the usage Hermes already displays, holds no credentials, and never touches account or billing settings. Disclosure — refuses main-loop provider calls (including MoA turns) for the providers in `provider_keys` (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex by default) when a subscription usage window reaches `threshold_percent`, and by default (`fail_open: false`) also refuses when usage data is missing, stale, unreadable, or the guard's own config is malformed; usage is read through Hermes's own account-usage fetcher (no credentials held, at most one read per source every 180 seconds by default) and cached in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/usage-guard/usage.json; a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a short usage note to the next turn's context at 80% and 90% used by default, and an opt-in (off by default) `llm_request` middleware lowers an existing output-token budget near the usage limit; both read only the cache, never the network; auxiliary calls (compression, vision, titles, MoA advisors) are not gated.

plugins.name: usage-ledger
plugins.description: Local-only content-free usage tally and native Desktop statusline (Windows and macOS beta).

plugins.name: usage-stats
plugins.description: Multi-provider usage/balance for the Hermes Desktop status bar — shows live usage for OpenCode, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, NovitaAI, ZAI, Alibaba, Arcee, plus gateway-native Claude/Codex/Cursor/Nous.

plugins.name: vault-view
plugins.description: Local Markdown vault workspace for Hermes Desktop: visual editing, progressive reading, cached image previews, optional per-conversation workspaces, pinned tabs, explicit selection quoting, tag search, links, backlinks and a graph. Compatible with Obsidian vaults. File transport requires a Linux/macOS gateway; Windows Desktop requires a WSL-hosted Unix backend, not a native Windows gateway; ffmpeg thumbnails are optional. Remote images and agent guidance are independent opt-ins and disabled by default; automatic note-content sharing is disabled; direct Obsidian opening is temporarily hidden. Disclosure — reads and writes notes in the vault folder you choose through Desktop shell commands on the gateway host; remote Markdown images and agent navigation guidance stay off until you opt in.

plugins.name: vaultknox
plugins.description: Secret-leak protection for Hermes chats. Scans inbound messages and outbound replies for API keys, tokens, and passwords with a 28-pattern detector registry, redacts them before they reach session storage or the user, and injects safe secret-handling rules so the agent never asks for secrets in chat. Zero dependencies, fully offline detection; pairs with the optional hermes-vault CLI for encrypted storage. Disclosure — rewrites inbound user messages (regex secret redaction, may false-positive on password-like strings), injects a secret-handling prompt each conversation and rewrites assistant replies that ask for secrets; outbound replies are value-redacted with the same registry (regex-based, so a shape no detector covers passes through), with findings logged as detector name plus SHA-256 fingerprint and never the raw value. The vaultknox tool is inert unless the separate vaultknox pip package is installed, its write gate is a tool argument the model sets, and a vault policy that authorises raw consume_token returns the plaintext to the model.

plugins.name: vaultwarden
plugins.description: Vaultwarden / Bitwarden Password Manager (bw CLI) secret source

plugins.name: vector-platform
plugins.description: Vector (vectorapp.io) messaging platform plugin: Hermes becomes a first-class Nostr-based Vector bot (its own nsec/npub identity), relaying DMs through a local Rust sidecar that wraps vector-sdk. First run needs `hermes gateway setup`, which provisions the bot identity (create or import). Disclosure — `hermes gateway setup` downloads a prebuilt vector-bridge binary from github.com/BonesGit/hermes-vector-platform/releases (tag v<version>, sha256 checked against that release's SHA256SUMS; set vector.prebuilt.download: false to build from the bundled Rust source), merges `vector:` settings into ~/.hermes/config.yaml, writes VECTOR_* to ~/.hermes/.env, and publishes a public bot profile (kind-0, bot: true) to Nostr discovery relays.

plugins.name: vet402
plugins.description: Look a paid x402 or MPP URL up in vet402's public record of real purchases before the agent pays it. BLOCK stops the tool call, and a WARN backed by evidence against the seller asks for approval. Disclosure — sends each guarded or model-queried URL (scheme, host and path; userinfo, query and fragment stripped) to vet402.com in up to two HTTPS GETs; fails open, so a vet402 outage or unknown URL lets the payment run unless VET402_UNKNOWN=approve.

plugins.name: vidiq
plugins.description: Grow on YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok with vidIQ. Disclosure — skills only; you add vidIQ's hosted MCP server yourself with hermes mcp add vidiq --url https://mcp.vidiq.com/mcp --auth oauth; tool calls send your prompts and authorized channel data to vidIQ and spend vidIQ account credits.

plugins.name: vk-platform
plugins.description: VK Messenger gateway with community Long Poll, media attachments, allowlists, and project-lane routing.

plugins.name: voice-ledger
plugins.description: Local ledger of the voice messages and recordings Hermes transcribes (voice messages from messaging platforms, CLI voice mode): /voice-log shows how many recordings there were, how much audio in total and typically, and how long ago the last one was, per speech-to-text provider, model, source, language or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days or everything recorded; /voice-log recent lists the newest recordings (ten, or up to 100 with /voice-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes recording metadata (source, provider, model, language, file size read from the file system; no audio, file path, prompt or transcript) to plugin-data/voice-ledger/voice.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, always returns None so the transcription request is unchanged; no network

plugins.name: voicestudio
plugins.description: Client for the local VoiceStudio text-to-speech app (debpalash/VoiceStudio): speak short text, design or clone voices, browse voices, render chaptered long-form audio, dub videos, and check server status. Six tools with mirrored slash commands plus a bundled skill. Disclosure — sends the text, script files, videos and voice samples you point it at to the VoiceStudio server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:3900, plain HTTP) and saves the returned audio under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/voicestudio; no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

plugins.name: vornik-companion
plugins.description: Vornik as Hermes's hardened broker and long-term memory: Hermes holds no credentials; privileged work runs in operator-approved workflows on your own Vornik daemon. Disclosure — talks only to the self-hosted Vornik daemon at VORNIK_URL with VORNIK_BROKER_TOKEN (and VORNIK_MEMORY_TOKEN for memory); broker tools let the agent start operator-approved workflows on that daemon (writes are approved by a person in Vornik); when selected as memory provider it sends each turn's user query for recall, mirrors MEMORY.md and USER.md writes to the daemon, and asks the daemon to stop recalling (not delete) a mirrored entry that Hermes removes or replaces (/vornik-memory lists and /vornik-forget forgets what Vornik keeps); artifact tools expose only named outputs allowed by the approved workflow from completed runs and read bounded text or return short-lived binary download links from the daemon; task diagnosis tools (offered only when the daemon advertises companion-progress) return a broker task's execution events and closed error classes as the daemon serves them to a broker key; hermes vornik approvals on writes security.approval.transport (and vornik_companion.approval_namespace) to Hermes config, after which Hermes's own dangerous-command prompts (the redacted command text) are sent through the local vornikctl agent host-approval to the daemon and answered on the paired phone, any failure or a Vornik outage denying the command unless transport_fallback: builtin is set, and the plugin never decides itself; hermes vornik connect runs the local vornikctl, which adds an MCP entry to Hermes config.

plugins.name: wait-ledger
plugins.description: Local ledger of the times Hermes stopped to wait for you (approval prompts, clarify questions, password prompts): /waits shows how many waits there were, how many were answered or left unanswered, and how long Hermes stood still in total, typically and at most, per kind of prompt, per platform or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /waits recent lists the newest waits (ten, or up to 100 with /waits recent 50). Disclosure — writes wait metadata (session id, platform, kind of prompt, how it ended, wait time; no prompt text, answer or session key) to plugin-data/wait-ledger/waits.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot answer, delay or change a prompt; no network

plugins.name: wallaby-provider
plugins.description: Wallaby Token — curated open-weight inference (Kimi K3); adds Wallaby to the hermes model provider list.

plugins.name: wallpaper-theme
plugins.description: A Hermes Desktop theme that follows your wallpaper. Reads Pywal's ~/.cache/wal/colors.json by default, or any palette JSON you point it at (settings page or ~/.config/hermes-wallpaper-theme/config.json), derives a palette with checked contrast floors and repaints live when the file changes. Optional glass mode paints a translucent background for native window materials or compositor blur. Disclosure — the desktop half uses only @hermes/plugin-sdk; the palette file is read by the package's own backend route (dashboard/plugin_api.py, GET /api/plugins/wallpaper-theme/palette, mounted once the plugin is in plugins.enabled), polled every 3 seconds with a change stamp. That route reads only JSON files inside the user's home directory (or XDG_*_HOME) under 256 KiB and returns colour fields only, never raw file text. No network calls, no shell commands, no credentials, no telemetry.

plugins.name: watchline
plugins.description: Watchline delivery adapter for Hermes Agent. Polls a Watchline pull channel and forwards matched events into the Hermes gateway as inbound messages.

plugins.name: waypoint
plugins.description: Session status for Hermes Desktop: a thin bar next to every sidebar session with four states — Working (remembers your next step), Waiting on someone (who/what plus a follow-up reminder), Done (outcome plus a fresh-start handoff) and untracked. Suggests 3 next steps per session (instant quick ideas from the chat, opt-in AI ideas from the auxiliary model, priority colours) with one-click Ask, a Power up button that asks a strong model for sharper ideas on demand, and Mark complete to stop suggestions. Adds a Status Board page (columns, follow-ups due, stale sessions, archive all done), triage of untracked sessions, a resume banner above the composer, a status-bar counter, a daily summary, palette commands and English/Arabic (RTL). SDK-only: session-row slots, a route, sidebar nav, status bar, composer banner, palette. Disclosure — no network calls of its own (all model calls go through Hermes llm.oneshot); AI next-step suggestions are OFF by default; when enabled, after new replies (at most every 90 s) the plugin sends the focused session's last ~12 user/assistant messages (≤ ~7,000 chars) plus its title and the user's notes to the auxiliary task title_generation (Hermes default "auto" = your main model); Power up runs only when pressed — also with AI suggestions off — and sends a longer excerpt (last ~20 messages, ≤ ~12,000 chars) to the plugin's own auxiliary tasks waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 (registered by __init__.py; unset they resolve to "auto" = your main model) or, for "My chat model", to the open session's model; an optional automatic big idea (off by default) uses the same choice at most every 10 minutes; Power up call log (2.5.0): the Python half also registers two observe-only hooks (pre_auxiliary_call, post_auxiliary_call) that ignore every auxiliary task except waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 and, for those, write one line per call to the user's own Hermes log (logs/agent.log) and append a record to <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/waypoint/power-calls.jsonl (rolls over at ~1 MB): model, provider, reasoning effort, response time, token counts (logged as 'unknown' with a reason when Hermes reports none), finish reason and status — never prompt, message or reply text, nothing leaves the machine, and the hooks never modify a call; reads session history (session.history) and titles (session.list); statuses, notes and cached suggestion text are kept in desktop plugin storage; archives sessions only when you press Archive (undo offered) or confirm "Archive N done" on the board (no undo; sessions stay under Archived); posts in-app and native OS notifications for due reminders and a once-a-day local summary; writes composer drafts only on Ask / Insert / Start fresh session and never sends them.

plugins.name: weather
plugins.description: Weather data, radar/model imagery, and verified meteorological calculations. Built on metrust, rusbie, wrf-rust, rustdar, and ecape-rs.

plugins.name: web-defuddle
plugins.description: Defuddle content extraction — local, free, no API key. Shells out to the defuddle CLI for clean article markdown. Extract-only; pair with SearXNG or another search provider.

plugins.name: web-meta-ai
plugins.description: Meta web search — routes web_search through the server-side web_search tool on Meta's Responses API (Muse Spark); search-only. Disclosure — each search is a separate billed Meta Model API call (per-query web search fee plus tokens) on MODEL_API_KEY.

plugins.name: web-octen
plugins.description: Octen web search with query-focused highlights and page extraction.

plugins.name: web-ollama-cloud
plugins.description: Ollama Cloud web search + content extraction via Ollama's native REST API. Search returns web results; extract fetches page content. Reuses OLLAMA_API_KEY (https://ollama.com/settings/keys).

plugins.name: web-oxylabs
plugins.description: Oxylabs AI Studio web search and extraction provider for Hermes Agent. Requires OXYLABS_API_KEY (sign up at https://aistudio.oxylabs.io/api-key).

plugins.name: web-search-plus
plugins.description: Multi-provider web search, URL extraction, quality reports, and opt-in research mode. Disclosure — reads the operator's HERMES_HOME/config.yaml (read-only) for its own Desktop settings block (country, language, max_results, auto_routing, provider_order, searxng_url, donsetch_bin) and, in its status command, the web backend and keyless_rescue settings; may spawn an operator-configured local donsetch CLI as a subprocess (argv, no shell).

plugins.name: web-serply
plugins.description: Serply web search provider for Hermes Agent. Google web results via the Serply SERP API. Requires SERPLY_API_KEY (sign up at https://serply.io).

plugins.name: web-toon
plugins.description: Paid web extract over TOON: web_extract pays a TOON node about $0.001 per page from a local payer sidecar; the node fetches through an Anyone network exit and returns markdown with a wuzzy/crawl v1 content hash. Disclosure — with TOON_PAYER_URL set and web.extract_backend toon, every web_extract URL goes to the user's anonfetch payer sidecar and spends about $0.001 from its TOON payment channel with no per-call confirmation; the sidecar's daily cap and origin allowlist are the only spending controls; pages are fetched through Anyone network exits.

plugins.name: web-venice
plugins.description: Venice AI web search + extract — privacy-first, zero data retention, $0.01/request.

plugins.name: wechat-social-assistant
plugins.description: Local-first WeChat relationship memory assistant for macOS: captures only what is visible in the WeChat window via system OCR/Accessibility, stores everything in a local SQLite database (0600/0700 permissions, no cloud), and serves contact briefs, follow-up planning, outreach drafts and weekly relationship reports through 32 MCP tools. Engine pinned to the immutable PyPI release wechat-social-assistant==1.5.1 over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs uv on PATH. All data confined to PLUGIN_DATA via WSA_ALLOWED_ROOT + path enforcement. Never reads WeChat databases, never injects into WeChat, never sends messages — outreach is drafts for human review only. Disclosure — reads WeChat only by screenshotting/OCR-ing and walking the macOS Accessibility tree of the frontmost window (not WeChat's databases or a bot API), compiles bundled Swift helpers with swiftc into ~/Library/Caches/wechat-social-assistant/bin on first use, and needs Screen Recording (optionally Accessibility) permission for the host terminal; no network egress, never sends messages.

plugins.name: whatsapp-agent-platform
plugins.description: Community platform plugin (not affiliated with Meta or Nous Research) connecting a WhatsApp Agent to Hermes through Meta's WhatsApp Agent Platform API (/agent/v1): long-poll inbound (no public URL), text and media. Disclosure — sends the API key and message content, files included, only to Meta: api.whatsapp.com, plus lookaside.fbsbx.com for downloads (per WhatsApp's Third-Party Agents Terms, agent chats are not end-to-end encrypted); stores the poll cursor, recent message ids and the creator's id under HERMES_HOME; no other network egress, no telemetry, no self-update. Exception: Hermes fetches image URLs in replies (SSRF-guarded, no key), revealing the server's IP to that host. Files go only to the creator; Meta keeps uploads up to 30 days. Received files are cached under HERMES_HOME (deleted after ~24 h while the gateway runs) and may reach the configured model, vision or speech-to-text provider. WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_MEDIA_ENABLED=false disables media. By default only the agent's creator (verified through Meta's API) can message Hermes; WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOWED_USERS or WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS widens that explicitly. The agent API key is saved to the Hermes .env; the state file under HERMES_HOME is 0600 and never contains the key.

plugins.name: wicked-memory
plugins.description: Persistent, wallet-scoped long-term memory for Hermes: remember, semantic recall, versioned update, history and approved hard delete, backed by the hosted Wicked Memory service, plus skills for using it and for connecting the Wicked MCP server. Works with no setup (a wallet is generated on first use; search uses the service's shared free key). Disclosure — sends the memory text and search queries the agent chooses to memory.wickedapi.com (or your configured base_url), each request signed by the agent's wallet, plus one GET to /v1/status on first use to read the published community key; stores a generated private key unencrypted in the plugin data dir unless you supply WICKED_MEMORY_PRIVATE_KEY; no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry; every wicked_memory_forget asks for human approval. The bundled wicked-suite-mcp skill walks you through adding the author's hosted Wicked MCP server (https://mcp.wickedapi.com/mcp, 75 tools, some x402-priced); that server is a separate manual step and is not covered by this pin.

plugins.name: wiki-ref
plugins.description: @wiki:<title> context references: attach the lead section of a Wikipedia article to a message, or one section with @wiki:<title>#<section>, with title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to <language>.wikipedia.org/w/api.php only (the referenced title and the typed autocomplete prefix leave the machine; a section is cut locally); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @wiki: reference provider.

plugins.name: wolfmarkdown
plugins.description: Create, clean, and verify standalone Markdown with conservative semantic repair and deterministic artifact checks. Disclosure — skill-only plugin that has the agent run its bundled Node.js 22+ scripts through the terminal; on first use it runs `npm ci` in the plugin folder (lockfile-pinned packages from registry.npmjs.org), and the optional `/wolfmarkdown setup` also creates skill symlinks in ~/.agents/skills and ~/.claude/skills.

plugins.name: woof
plugins.description: Plan, launch, watch and compare WOOF weather simulations on your own NVIDIA GPU: size runs with WOOF's own planner, launch them locally or on an ssh/WSL GPU host, get maps in the chat while the forecast runs, compare physics or resolution, run multi-arm research campaigns and score runs against radar and surface observations. Disclosure — runs need Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU (plan-only elsewhere); the user-run hermes woof install pip-installs recast-woof>=1.0.0,<1.1 into ~/woof-env and downloads WOOF tables and optional geography (about 1.6 GB); runs execute the WOOF CLI as detached background jobs writing to ~/woof-runs and fetch public weather data; run events are pushed into the chat as user-role messages; the optional serve/ scripts download llama.cpp and a Qwen GGUF and start an unauthenticated local model server.

plugins.name: wyoming-voice-bridge
plugins.description: Wyoming speech-to-text and text-to-speech for a Wyoming server you run (stt/tts provider `wyoming`), plus a wyoming_voice_status tool that lists the server's models and voices. Disclosure — Audio and text to speak go to the WYOMING_* host:port you set over cleartext, unauthenticated TCP (public addresses accepted). Once selected, the providers send speech in every session, including cron and webhooks. Non-WAV audio is converted with your local ffmpeg. wyoming_voice_status asks for approval on each call and refuses under cron, yolo, approvals off, -q and unattended platforms; answering "always" leaves a command_allowlist line in config.yaml. It calls internal Hermes approval, config and write-guard helpers, so a Hermes update can disable the status tool or speech file writes (both fail closed).

plugins.name: xchat
plugins.description: X Chat gateway platform: talk to Hermes in X's end-to-end encrypted DMs. Hermes runs as the X account you connect: chat with it in your own self-chat ("message yourself"), or give it a separate account and DM that. Messages are decrypted and encrypted locally with X's official Chat XDK, so X only routes ciphertext. Encrypted media, threaded replies, group mention gating and cron delivery.

plugins.name: xmemo
plugins.description: Native XMemo memory provider for Hermes Agent — durable, identity-aware cross-session memory with semantic search. Disclosure — cloud memory provider: sends each user prompt (for recall), model-written memories and mirrored built-in Hermes memory writes, plus a stable install ID, to xmemo.dev (Yonro Co., Ltd.); reuses the xmemo login token from ~/.config/xmemo if present.

plugins.name: yantrikdb-hermes-dashboard
plugins.description: Local-only YantrikDB dashboard for Hermes Agent memory operations

plugins.name: yantrikdb
plugins.description: Persistent memory for Hermes. Canonicalizes duplicate memories, surfaces contradictions between structured or recognized single-valued claims for review, and returns a why_retrieved reason list with every recall. Embedded by default: no server, no token, no GPU. Optional HTTP backend for HA clusters; pluggable embedders (bundled potion-2M default).

plugins.name: yolo-auto
plugins.description: Yolo-Auto: flat-rate OpenAI-compatible API with plan-filtered live model discovery.

plugins.name: you
plugins.description: You.com skills for live web search, URL content extraction, cited research, finance research, and integration discovery via the You.com MCP servers (api.you.com). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, five skills bundled); auth via YDC_API_KEY, OAuth, or MPP/x402 — the free profile works keyless.

plugins.name: zalo-platform
plugins.description: Zalo Bot Platform gateway adapter for Hermes Agent — relays messages between Zalo DMs/groups and the agent over the official Bot API (bot-api.zaloplatforms.com), long-polling or webhook mode. Adds slash commands and moderation. Zero extra dependencies (uses httpx, already a Hermes dependency). Production-tested on multiple Vietnamese deployments. Disclosure — connects to the third-party Zalo Bot API (bot-api.zaloplatforms.com) with your bot token; long-polling by default, or opt-in webhook mode with a listener on 127.0.0.1 by default that checks the X-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header; the setup wizard writes ZALO_* values to ~/.hermes/.env; group chat history is stored locally under <HERMES_HOME>/zalo-history.

plugins.name: zerosignal
plugins.description: ZeroSignal — private, pay-per-request inference through the local zs-proxy; no API key, your wallet is the credential.

removed.name: or-picker
removed.reason: Folded into openrouter-picker. Installing the provider alone left the picker broken. Install openrouter-picker.
